items.book_statement: Every odd integer greater than 5 is a sum of three primes.
items.note: Lean proves the theorem from three hypotheses: Platt's GRH verification, binary Goldbach to 4·10¹⁸, and Ramaré's μ(n)/n bound. The large-N part uses major arcs ≥ 1.049 and minor arcs ≤ 1.0376 (× x²/κ) against the book's 1.058259 and 1.00948; the cases n ≤ 10²⁷ use a kernel-checked Proth-prime ladder in place of [HP13].
items.evidence: Lean: Statement := ∀ n, Odd n → 5 < n → IsSumOfThreePrimes n, from PlattGRH, BinaryGoldbachInput, RamareMoebius; book: same sentence.

lean.note: PlattGRH → BinaryGoldbachInput → RamareMoebius → Statement; the conclusion is the book's sentence.
Same statement with the three hypotheses as Fact instances; proof is statement_of_upTo_of_from at C = 10²⁷.
∀ n, Odd n → 5 < n → ∃ primes p, q, r with p + q + r = n.
TernaryGoldbachUpTo C and TernaryGoldbachFrom C give Statement.
Odd N ≥ 10²⁷ by the circle method (§14.4); uses PlattGRH and RamareMoebius only.
Odd 5 < n ≤ 10²⁷: binary Goldbach to 4·10¹⁸ plus a prime from the kernel-checked Proth-prime ladder; replaces [HP13] up to 8.875·10³⁰.
Kernel-checked prime in [(111616i − 2047)·2⁴⁵ + 1, 111616i·2⁴⁵ + 1] for 1 ≤ i ≤ 254638308.

items.changes_since_2013: Identical to the unnumbered 'Main Theorem' of 1312.7748v2 (§1.1), which also proved n ≥ 10²⁷ analytically and cited [HP13] for the rest.

items.note: Heuristic display; its concrete instance in Lean has main-term margin 0.0114 and error constant 6.7·10⁶, against the book's 0.04877 and 7.3306.

items.evidence: Lean: identity for summable weights on ℕ over (0,1] with e(−Nα); book: weights on ℤ over ℝ/ℤ with f̂(α) = Σ f(n)e(−αn).

items.label: eq:koj
items.book_statement: For a Dirichlet character χ and Re s > 1, the negative logarithmic derivative of L(s,χ) is the Dirichlet series Σ_{n≥1} χ(n)Λ(n)n^{−s}.
items.note: Book use: last step of (9.4), proof of Lemma 9.1.1. Not reproved in the repo; Mathlib supplies it, and ArithmeticFunction.LSeries_vonMangoldt_eq_deriv_riemannZeta_div for ζ (Explicit/XiPartial.lean:249). The cites index links (1.5) to TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.buthe_psi and TernaryGoldbach.ButhePsi, but those docstrings cite Büthe's (1.5), not [H].

lean.note: Line 157 applies Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.LSeries_twist_vonMangoldt_eq (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Dirichlet.lean:408), which is (1.5) for every χ and Re s > 1, to get Σ Λ(n)χ(n)(n/x)^{−s} = x^s(−L′/L)(s) on Re s = 3/2.
The book's (9.4) in Lemma 9.1.1's proof: S = (1/2π)∫(−L′/L)(3/2+it)M(3/2+it)x^{3/2+it}dt, via TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.tsum_Fterm_eq.
The same Mathlib lemma (line 743) bounds |L′/L(3/2+iy, χ)| by Σ Λ(n)n^{−3/2}.

items.label: eq:holo
items.book_statement: Defines the smoothed prime exponential sum S_η(α,x) = Σ_n Λ(n)e(αn)η(n/x) for a fast-decaying weight η. Using Λ(n) instead of log p over primes simplifies matters.
items.note: Lean applies S to η₊ and η_* (the circle-method integrand at x = xOf N). It also applies S to η₂ at many scales in the minor arcs: there are 33 occurrences of 'S eta2', e.g. TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.S_etaStar_eq, TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.norm_S_eta2_le_of_not_mem and TernaryGoldbach.MinorArcs.norm_S_eta2_le_trivial. The cites index wrongly links (1.6) to TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.buthe_psi and to TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.large_sieve_weighted / TernaryGoldbach.Prelim.LS.large_sieve_weighted. Those docstrings cite Büthe's (1.6) and [MV73, (1.6)].

lean.note: S η x α = Σ' n:ℕ, Λ(n)η(n/x)·e(nα), with the arguments in the order η, x, α. Here η : ℝ → ℝ, against the book's ℝ → ℂ, but every weight used is real. The n = 0 term vanishes since Λ(0) = 0. A tsum is 0 on a non-summable series, which is harmless: every weight used gives an absolutely convergent series.
The generic series Σ' a(n)e(nα). S_η is expTsum with a(n) = Λ(n)η(n/x), definitionally (e.g. TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.S_etaPlus_eq_expTsum, ArcChars.lean:35, proved by rfl).
[H, (11.9)]: S_{η_*}(α,x) = ∫₀^∞ S_{η₂}(α, wx/κ)φ(w)dw/w. The definition is also instantiated for η₂ at every scale in the minor arcs.

items.label: eq:battle
items.book_statement: Defines the character-twisted sum S_{η,χ}(δ/x,x) = Σ_n Λ(n)χ(n)e(δn/x)η(n/x); its phase e(δn/x) winds only boundedly often while η(n/x) is non-negligible.
items.note: Lean evaluates χ at (n : ZMod q), so χ(n) = 0 when (n,q) > 1, as for the book's lifted characters.

lean.note: Schar χ a β = Σ' a(n)χ(n)e(nβ); with a(n) = Λ(n)η(n/x) and β = δ/x it is S_{η,χ}(δ/x,x). TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.cor_7_1_3', thm_7_1_4_odd/even/one and prop_9_3_2 are stated in this form.

items.label: eq:narimsi
items.book_statement: F_δ, the Mellin transform of e(δt)η(t), is ∫₀^∞ e(δt)η(t)t^s dt/t; stationary phase places its main contribution at t = −τ/2πδ, where it is of size about η(−τ/2πδ).
items.note: Ch. 8 fixes η = e^{−t²/2} (F_δ = M(e^{−t²/2}e(δt))); Ch. 9 writes G_δ for a general η. Only the k = 2 twist is formalized. Stationary point checked: d/dt(2πδt + τ log t) = 0 at t = −τ/(2πδ), which is positive iff sgn τ ≠ sgn δ.

lean.note: −L′/L(s)·mellin φ s·x^s, where Mathlib's mellin φ s = ∫_{t>0} t^{s−1}φ(t)dt is (1.9) for φ(t) = η(t)e(δt), any weight.
The twist actually used, t²e^{−t²/2}e(δt) (k = 2). Its Mellin transform G_δ(s) = Gr s δ 0 (TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.mellin_fδ) is the book's F_δ(s+2) for the Gaussian of Ch. 8.
Gr s δ 0 = ∫_{t>0} t^{s−1}·t²e^{−t²/2}e(δt)dt, i.e. (1.9) written out for η = t²e^{−t²/2}.

erratum.description: The left side is printed F_δ(t); it should be F_δ(s). Here t is the integration variable, the right side depends on s, and the next sentences evaluate F_δ(σ+iτ).

So the k = 0 and k = 1 cases of Cor 8.0.2 are not needed. Lean's per-term constants differ from Cor 8.0.2's pair constants; see that item.

lean.note: k = 2 analogue of the first case, one term: for −1 ≤ σ ≤ 1 and 10π|δ| ≤ |τ| < (3/2)(πδ)², |G_δ(s)| = |F_δ(s+2)| ≤ 0.588y²e^{−0.1065y²}, y = |τ|/(π|δ|) = 2|τ|/|ℓ|.

k = 2, single term |F_δ(s+2)|, constant 0.588y² instead of 3.001; same exponent 0.1065.
k = 2, single term, 0.892|τ|e^{−0.1598|τ|}; same exponent as (1.10).

erratum.description: The sentence after (1.12), 'η̂(−δ) is just √(2π)e^{−2π²δ²} (self-duality of the Gaussian)', is false. The book's weights are one-sided (expform.tex:927 sets η♥(t) = 0 for t < 0), and the main term of Lemma 9.1.1 is x∫₀^∞e(δt)η(t)dt. The correct value is √(π/2)e^{−2π²δ²} + i√2·D(√2πδ), where D is Dawson's integral. (1.11)–(1.12) can hold only with this one-sided transform: read with the two-sided value, the q = 1 case fails.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: the book's one-sided transform is sqrt(pi/2)e^{-2pi^2 d^2} + i sqrt2 D(sqrt2 pi d), half the remark's real value plus an imaginary part, and with the remark's two-sided value (1.11)-(1.12) fail at q=1, delta=0 for x > 2.694e11.
check.note: After (1.12) the book says η̂(−δ) is just √(2π)e^{−2π²δ²}, but its weights are one-sided (η♥(t) = 0 for t < 0, and the main term of Lemma 9.1.1 is ∫₀^∞η(t)e(δt)dt), so η̂(−δ) = √(π/2)e^{−2π²δ²} + i√2·D(√2πδ): 1.028806 + 0.551811i at δ = 0.1, against the remark's 2.057613. Read with the remark's two-sided value, (1.11)–(1.12) fail at q = 1, δ = 0, since (1/x)ΣΛ(n)e^{−(n/x)²/2} → √(π/2) and |E| → 1.2533 exceeds the bound for x > 2.694·10¹¹ (asymptotic threshold); the claim survives, and the remark is used nowhere.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: the book's one-sided transform is sqrt(pi/2)e^{-2pi^2 d^2} + i sqrt2 D(sqrt2 pi d), half the remark's real value plus an imaginary part, and with the remark's two-sided value (1.11)-(1.12) fail at q=1, delta=0 for x > 2.694e11.

items.label: eq:rada1
items.book_statement: The first type I sum, Σ_{m≤U} μ(m) Σ_n (log n) e(αmn) η(mn/x). It comes from the μ_{≤U}∗log term of Vaughan's identity (1.15). This overview puts no coprimality condition on m or n.
items.note: The f ≡ 1 sum (1.17) is neither formalized nor needed. The difference is the book's own choice: Ch. 3 inserts f = 1_{(n,v)=1} with v = 2 ((3.9)–(3.10)). So m and n run over odd integers, and Lemmas 4.2.2–4.2.4 approximate 2α rather than α (Lean: Approx2). Lean's bound on typeILog is lemma_4_2_3 (TypeILogProof.lean:1244-1253); see the Lemma 4.2.3 entry.

lean.note: Σ_{m≤D odd} μ(m) Σ_{n≤x odd} (log n) e(αmn) η₂(mn/x). This is the book's S_{I,1} of (3.9) with f = 1_{(·,2)=1}, η = η₂ and D = U (equivalently (4.39) for η₂), not the unrestricted (1.17). Cutting n at ⌊x⌋ is harmless because supp η₂ ⊆ [1/4,1]. Empty hypothesis mask; in the cone.
Σ_{n≤M odd} (μ_{≤U}∗log)(n) e(αn) η₂(n/x) = typeILog α x U, so the odd-n part of the μ_{≤U}∗log term of Vaughan's identity is typeILog. Empty mask; in the cone.

typeILog α x D = Σ_{m≤D odd} μ(m)·ToddG (eta2log (x/m)) α x m. Each inner sum becomes T_{m,∘} with the m-dependent smoothing η_(x/m)(t) = log((x/m)t)·η₂(t), via innerLog_eq_ToddG (lines 17-59). For the odd/η₂ sum this is the formal content of the text's remark that (1.17) is of the same kind as (1.19). It is also the opening step of the book's proof of Lemma 4.2.3, and Lean uses it there (TypeILogProof.lean:913). Empty mask; in the cone.

lean.note: R_{x,t} verbatim (x^{1/3} as rpow).

items.label: eq:vaughin

Pointwise form for n > V (where Λ_{≤V}(n) = 0); not in the main theorem's cone.

items.label: eq:mobinv
items.book_statement: Möbius inversion: convolving the constant function 1 with μ gives the unit of Dirichlet convolution, equal to 1 at n = 1 and 0 for n > 1.
items.note: Classical; supplied by Mathlib rather than proved in the repo.

lean.note: Mathlib: (ζ∗μ : ArithmeticFunction R) = 1 over any ring; with ArithmeticFunction.one_apply, 1(n) = [n = 1]. Exactly (3.7).
Mathlib, commuted form μ∗ζ = 1; the form invoked in the proof of `vaughan`.
Derives Vaughan's identity from μ∗ζ = 1, as the book does.

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (new in the book; 2013 cited [IK, §13.4] instead)

items.label: eq:bob
items.book_statement: For completely multiplicative f, any η and cut-offs U, V, Vaughan's identity turns Σ Λ(n)f(n)e(αn)η(n/x) into S_{I,1} − S_{I,2} + S_{II} + S_{0,∞}.
items.note: The general statement (any completely multiplicative f, any η) is not formalized; the book only uses f = 1_{(n,2)=1} and η = η₂, which Lean covers. 'Any η' tacitly needs convergence (η₂ has compact support). Checked numerically for x ≤ 5000 and several α, U, V: error ≤ 1.4e-11.

lean.note: Only for f = 1_odd, η = η₂: pointwise Vaughan (hV), split of the odd-n sum into four sums (hodd), then odd_part_a–d identify S_{0,∞}, S_{I,1}, S_{I,2}, S_{II}.
Σ_{n odd}(f∗g)(n)w(n) = Σ_{a,b odd} f(a)g(b)w(ab) for w vanishing beyond M: the step that uses complete multiplicativity of f (Nat.odd_mul).
Λ_{≤V} term = S_{0,∞} (S0inf).
μ_{≤U}∗log term = S_{I,1} (typeILog).
μ_{≤U}∗Λ_{≤V}∗1 term = S_{I,2} (typeI2).
μ_{>U}∗Λ_{>V}∗1 term = S_{II} (typeII), using (μ_{>U}∗1)(m) = Σ_{d|m, d>U} μ(d).

items.label: eq:nielsen
items.book_statement: Defines the four sums: type I S_{I,1} (μ(m) against log n) and S_{I,2} (Λ(d), μ(m) against 1), type II S_{II} (Σ_{d|m, d>U} μ(d) against Λ(n), n > V), and the short sum S_{0,∞} over n ≤ V.
items.note: Lean defines the sums only for the book's final choice f = 1_{(n,2)=1}, η = η₂; general f and η are not needed. As the book says for its parameters, S0inf vanishes when V ≤ x/4 (S0inf_eq_zero, Assembly.lean:26).

lean.note: S_{I,1} for f = 1_odd, η = η₂: m ≤ ⌊D⌋ odd (D = U), n ≤ ⌊x⌋ odd; the n-cut is harmless since η₂(mn/x) = 0 once mn ≥ x. Docstring cites (4.39), the same sum.
S_{I,2} = Σ_{v≤V odd} Λ(v) Σ_{u≤U odd} μ(u) Σ_{n odd} e(αvun)η₂(vun/x); docstring cites (4.49).
S_{II}; sums over all odd m ≤ ⌊x⌋ instead of m > U, harmless because Σ_{d|m, d>U} μ(d) is an empty sum for m ≤ U.
S_{0,∞} = Σ_{n≤V odd} Λ(n)e(αn)η₂(n/x).

items.label: eq:joroy
items.book_statement: Chooses f(n) as the indicator that n is coprime to a small square-free v; it is completely multiplicative, and the book eventually fixes v = 2, i.e. odd n.
items.note: Only v = 2, the book's final choice, is formalized; general square-free v is unused generality.

lean.note: No standalone f: for v = 2, 1_{(n,2)=1} appears as the guards `Odd m`, `Odd n` here, and likewise in typeILog, typeI2 and S0inf.
Uses complete multiplicativity of 1_odd (Odd(ab) ↔ Odd a ∧ Odd b, via Nat.odd_mul).

items.label: eq:sofot
items.book_statement: With f = 1_{(n,v)=1}: S_η(α,x) = S_{I,1} − S_{I,2} + S_{II} + S_{0,∞} + S_{0,v}, the last a remainder over n not coprime to v.
items.note: Lean proves the identity for v = 2 with remainder Σ_{n even, n≤x} Λ(n)e(αn)η₂(n/x); the printed Σ_{n|v} omits the prime powers p^k, k ≥ 2, p | v.
items.evidence: Lean: S = typeILog − typeI2 + typeII + S0inf + S0two with S0two = Σ_{n even}; book: remainder Σ_{n|v}.

lean.note: S η₂ x α = typeILog − typeI2 + typeII + S0inf + S0two for x > 0, U, V ∈ ℕ; v = 2, η = η₂. No hypotheses.
Remainder over all even n ≤ x (powers of 2), not the book's Σ_{n|2}.
|S| ≤ |S_{I,1}| + |S_{I,2}| + |S_{II}| + 3 log x for V ≤ x/4; now hypothesis-free.
Applies norm_S_le_parts and absorbs 3 log x into 0.0001x^{5/6}.

Reading n|v as n | v^∞ instead makes §6.3.1's 'S_{0,w} = 0' (p. 125) false. Harmless: |S_{0,2}| ≤ 4(log 2)² ≈ 1.92. Also misprints S_{0,w} for S_{0,v} and S_η(x,α) for S_η(α,x).

check.note: With the printed S_{0,v} = Σ_{n|v} Λ(n)e(αn)η(n/x), (3.11) is false: the remainder must be Σ_{(n,v)>1} Λ(n)e(αn)η(n/x), which also contains the prime powers p^k, k ≥ 2, p | v; for η = η₂, v = 2, α = 0 the omitted terms total 4(log 2)² ≈ 1.92 (e.g. x = 100: S_η = 99.1255 against 97.2037 + 0). The claim survives; it is harmless, and (3.11) also misprints S_{0,w} for S_{0,v} and S_η(x,α) for S_η(α,x).

items.label: eq:f3V
items.book_statement: Defines F_{3,V} = −Λ_{>V}∗Λ∗Λ + 2Λ_{≤V}∗Λ∗Λ, the trilinear part of (3.15), and lists its values on square-free n = p1p2p3 according to how many p_i exceed V.

Also '−Λ∗Λ∗Λ(n) is −6' omits the log factors. Harmless: unused route.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: F_{3,V}(p1p2p3) = (12-6k) log p1 log p2 log p3, so the printed case list swaps the values 0 and 6 log p1 log p2 log p3 of its two middle cases.

items.label: eq:sult
items.book_statement: Final alternative decomposition Λ·log² = F_{I,1,u} − 3F_{I,2,V,u} − 3F_{II,V,u} + F_{3,V} + F_{0,V,u}, isolating in F_{0,V,u} the pieces with a variable ≤ u (e.g. u = 3) to be bounded trivially.

items.label: lem:gotog
items.book_statement: For α = a/q + β/(qQ), (a,q) = 1, |β| ≤ 1, q ≤ Q and A, C ≥ 0: over any q consecutive integers n, Σ min(A, C/sin²(παn)) ≤ min(2A + 6q²C/π², 3A + (4q/π)√(AC)).
items.note: Only the second bound 3A + (4q/π)√(AC) is used downstream (book: proof of Lemma 4.2.1; Lean likewise); the first bound's method is reused for Lemma 4.1.2. Lean bounds each decreasing run of min(A, C/sin²) by (q/π)∫₀^{π/2}min(A, C/sin²v)dv ≤ (2q/π)√(AC) instead of counting A-terms via arcsin. The 3/2 inequality is proved on (0, π/6] (book [0, π/4]); q ≤ 2 by cases. Unconditional (empty hypothesis mask).

lean.note: Book's statement. Summand minA A C (sin²παn) is A where sin(παn) = 0 (the book's C/0 = ∞ reading); Ioc ⌊y⌋ ⌊y+q⌋ is exactly y < n ≤ y+q. In cone; only its second bound is used (TypeIProof.block_R3, TypeILogProof.sum_R3L).
Same bound for min A (C/sin²) with Lean's C/0 = 0, so a term with sin(παn) = 0 counts 0 instead of A. Not in cone; it is the form the TypeI.lean:105 blueprint example restates.
Hypothesis bundle 1 ≤ q, IsCoprime a q, ∃β with |β| ≤ 1, α = a/q + β/(qQ), q ≤ Q: the book's hypotheses (q ≥ 1 implicit there).
The book's m₀, j, δ₁, δ₂ step: the q terms become Φ(sin²(π(R+τ_R)/q)), R = 0..q−1, τ_R ∈ [s−½, s+½], 0 ≤ s ≤ ½ (s plays qδ₂).
First bound as in the book: R = 0, q−1 by A; pairs (k, q−1−k) by convex majorization; Σ ≤ (q/π)cot(π/q) (sum_fq_le); fq_half_add_le uses t²/sin²t + t cot 2t ≤ 3/2 on (0, π/6] (q ≥ 3; q ≤ 2 by cases).
Second bound: R = 0, q−1, 1 by A and the two monotone families of (4.4); the book's arcsin count of A-terms is replaced by sum_G_le (each family ≤ (2q/π)√(AC)).

erratum.description: Misprints in the proof: 'each residue class mod p' should read mod q; 'the terms with r ≠ 0, 1' should read r ≠ 0, −1 (r = 0, −1 are the two terms bounded by A); x ↦ 1/sin²x is convex on (0, π), not on '(0, ∞)'. Harmless: no estimate changes.

items.label: eq:betblu

items.label: eq:pordo1
items.book_statement: Series quoted from Abramowitz–Stegun: t/sin t = 1 + Σ a_{2k+1}t^{2k+2} = 1 + t²/6 + … and t cot t = 1 − Σ b_{2k+1}t^{2k+2} = 1 − t²/3 − t⁴/45 − … on (−π, π), with all a_{2k+1}, b_{2k+1} ≥ 0.
items.note: Checked: t/sin t = 1 + t²/6 + 7t⁴/360 + …, t cot t = 1 − t²/3 − t⁴/45 − 2t⁶/945 − …, coefficient signs as stated. Lean never states the series, only finite one-sided truncations on (0, π/3] and (0, π/2], which suffice because q ≤ 2 is handled separately.

lean.note: x cot x ≤ 1 − x²/3 − x⁴/45 on (0, π/3]: the truncation of (4.2) used for T2 (x = 2t), proved from the degree-7 sin and degree-8 cos Taylor bounds.
x cot x ≤ 1 − x²/3 on (0, π/2], used for T3 with x = 3t/2 (the book also keeps the −x⁴/45 term there).
Core of Lemma 4.1.1's t²/sin²t + t cot 2t ≤ 3/2 (t ≤ 0.5236), using only t − t³/4 < sin t ≤ t and cos t ≥ 1 − t²/2; no series.

items.label: eq:pordo2
items.book_statement: (t/sin t)² = 1 + t²/3 + c₀(t)t⁴ with c₀ increasing (by (4.2)), hence ≤ 1 + t²/3 + c₀(t₀)t⁴ on [0, t₀]; the book takes t₀ = π/4 (c₀ ≤ 0.074807) and later t₀ = π/2.
items.note: Numerically c₀(π/4) = 0.0738068 (the printed bound 0.074807 is valid; 0.073807 was probably meant) and c₀(π/2) = 0.105934; the needed signs hold: c₀(π/4) − 4/45 = −0.0151 and −1/6 + (c₀(π/2) − 27/360)(π/2)² = −0.0903. Lean replaces c₀ by explicit polynomial majorants on narrower ranges. c₀(t) is unrelated to the §4.2 constant c₀ (Lean's MinorArcs.c₀ = 32).

lean.note: (t/sin t)² ≤ 1 + t²/3 + t⁴/15 + t⁶/20 on (0, π/6], used in trig_T2 (book: 1 + t²/3 + c₀(π/4)t⁴ on [0, π/4]).
(t/sin t)² ≤ 1 + t²/3 + t⁴/10 on (0, π/3], used in trig_T3 (book: c₀(π/2) ≈ 0.10593 on [0, π/2]; here c₀(π/3) ≈ 0.08035 ≤ 0.1).
t²/sin²t + t cot 2t ≤ 3/2 on (0, π/6] for Lemma 4.1.1, proved via trig_core without c₀ (book: via c₀(π/4) − 8/45 < 0 on [0, π/4]).

items.label: eq:cloison
items.book_statement: Second approach in Lemma 4.1.1: with r = 0, ±1 bounded by A, the sum is ≤ 3A + Σ_{2≤r'≤q/2}[min(A, C/sin²((π/q)(r'−½−qδ₂))) + min(A, C/sin²((π/q)(r'−½+qδ₂)))].
items.note: For even q, r' = q/2 occurs in both sums though r = ±q/2 is one residue; harmless, since the '−qδ₂' term alone bounds it. Lean's families are exactly those of (4.4), but each is then bounded by monotonicity rather than the book's count of A-terms.

lean.note: hpeel, hhigh, hlow: R = 0, q−1, 1 bounded by A; residues r' and q−r' (2 ≤ r' ≤ q/2) bounded by min(A, C f_q) at r' − ½ + s and r' − ½ − s (fq_low, fq_high; s plays qδ₂). This is (4.4), without double-counting r' = q/2.
Bounds each family of (4.4) by (2q/π)√(AC) via monotonicity and ∫₀^{π/2}min(A, C/sin²v)dv ≤ 2√(AC) (integral_minInvSin_le), replacing the book's arcsin count and its arcsin inequality.

erratum.description: In bounding (4.4) the book writes 'arcsin x + x(1 − x²) ≤ 2x … Setting x = C/A'; the step needs arcsin x + x√(1 − x²) ≤ 2x with x = √(C/A). Also 'the integral of C/sin²(πα/q)' should read C/sin²(πt/q). The resulting bound 3A + (4q/π)√(AC) is unaffected.

items.label: lem:couscous
items.book_statement: For α = a/q + β/(qQ) with (a,q) = 1, |β| ≤ 1, q ≤ Q, and 0 ≤ y₁ < y₂ ≤ Q/2, y₂ − y₁ ≤ q, A, C ≥ 0: Σ_{y₁<n≤y₂, q∤n} min(A, C/sin²(παn)) ≤ min(20Cq²/(3π²), 2A + (4q/π)√(AC)).
items.note: Only the first bound 20Cq²/(3π²) is used downstream. In the book: (4.16) and (4.24) in the proof of Lemma 4.2.1. In Lean: block_R2 and sum_A1 (TypeIProof.lean) and sum_R2L (TypeILogProof.lean), all via min_le_left. Lean follows the book's route (T2 at t = π/2q, T3 at t = π/q), with Taylor-polynomial proofs on narrower ranges. Its proof of the unused second bound gives one A fewer than stated. The book's T2 and T3 inequalities hold on its stated ranges: the sups 5/4 and 5/3 are approached only as t → 0. This is classed as a proof-gap, not a typo, because a link of the printed chain is false for q = 2, 4, 6. The repair is a one-index fix. Unconditional.

lean.note: Exact. Approx α a q Q packs 1 ≤ q, (a,q) = 1, |β| ≤ 1, α = a/q + β/(qQ), q ≤ Q. Other hypotheses: 0 ≤ y₁ < y₂, y₂ − y₁ ≤ q, y₂ ≤ Q/2, A, C ≥ 0. Sum over Ioc ⌊y₁⌋ ⌊y₂⌋ with the q ∣ n terms set to 0. sin(παn) ≠ 0 for q ∤ n here (sin_ne_zero_of_approx), so Lean's C/0 = 0 never applies. In cone; unconditional.
The book's first step: for q ∤ n ≤ Q/2 the terms sit at distinct residues R ∈ [1, q−1] with one-signed shifts τ_R ∈ [0, ½].

Rest of the proof. Low residues r ≤ (q−1)/2 go to integer points and high ones q − k (k ≤ q/2) to half-integers. First bound: sum_fq_le and sum_fq_int_le, then T2, T3. Second bound: sum_G_le per family. q ≤ 2 by hand. The second-bound argument in fact gives A + (4q/π)√(AC).
The correct residue split (r ≤ (q−1)/2, and q − k with k ≤ q/2). It is what repairs the book's display (see erratum).
Σ_{r=2}^{L} csc²(πr/q) ≤ (q/π)cot(3π/2q), assuming 2L + 1 ≤ q. So it holds only with the corrected upper limit (q−1)/2.
Half-integer family: Σ_{j=2}^{K} csc²(π(j−½)/q) ≤ (q/π)cot(π/q) for K ≤ q/2.
t²/sin²t + (t/2)cot 2t ≤ 5/4 on (0, π/6] (book: [0, π/4]), applied at t = π/2q with q ≥ 3.
t²/sin²t + t cot(3t/2) ≤ 5/3 on (0, π/3] (book: [0, π/2]), applied at t = π/q with q ≥ 3.
Second bound: each unit-spaced family of min(A, C f_q) terms is at most (2q/π)√(AC). This replaces the arcsin count of Lemma 4.1.1's second approach, which the book cites.

erratum.description: The proof's first display sums the integer-distance terms min(A, C/sin²(πr/q)) up to r = q/2, but only r ≤ (q−1)/2 occur. For even q the residue q/2 lies at distance ≥ q/2 − ½ and is already in the half-integer sum. The next claimed bound, C·N(q) with N(q) = csc²(π/2q) + csc²(π/q) + (q/π)(cot(π/q) + cot(3π/2q)), leaves the extra term out. For q = 2, 4, 6 the bound is false for the printed display, which there even exceeds 20Cq²/(3π²). For every even q, the cited midpoint-convexity step gives more than 20Cq²/(3π²). The lemma is true: with upper limit (q−1)/2 the printed proof works unchanged.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: for even q the printed display includes the extra term r = q/2; it exceeds C N(q) at q = 2, 4, 6, the midpoint step overshoots 20Cq^2/(3pi^2) for every even q, and with limit (q-1)/2 the proof works.
check.note: The proof's first display runs the integer-distance sum to r = q/2, but only r ≤ (q−1)/2 occur; for even q the extra term makes the display (2q²+1)C/3, which exceeds the next bound C·N(q) at q = 2, 4, 6 (3 > 2.363, 11 > 10.629, 24.333 > 24.146) and there even exceeds 20Cq²/(3π²). With upper limit (q−1)/2 the display is 2(q²−1)C/3 ≤ C·N(q) ≤ 20Cq²/(3π²) and the printed proof works; the lemma is true and the claim survives.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: for even q the printed display includes the extra term r = q/2; it exceeds C N(q) at q = 2, 4, 6, the midpoint step overshoots 20Cq^2/(3pi^2) for every even q, and with limit (q-1)/2 the proof works.

items.changes_since_2013: notation only (gcd → (a,q)); a motivating paragraph was added before the lemma. Statement and proof are otherwise identical to 1205.5252v4 Lemma 3.2, so the slip dates from 2013.

items.label: eq:dijkre
items.book_statement: The displayed bound of Lemma 4.1.2: Σ_{y₁<n≤y₂, q∤n} min(A, C/|sin παn|²) ≤ min(20Cq²/(3π²), 2A + (4q/π)√(AC)).
items.note: Same content as Lemma 4.1.2. The statement is true; the summation-limit slip in its proof is recorded under Lemma 4.1.2.

lean.note: Same constants and hypotheses.

items.label: lem:thina
items.book_statement: Under Lemma 4.1.2's hypotheses, for B, C ≥ 0: Σ_{y₁<n≤y₂, q∤n} min(B/|sin παn|, C/sin² παn) ≤ (2Bq/π)·max(2, log(Ce³q/(Bπ))). The bound (2Bq/π)·log(2e²q/π) also holds.
items.note: Further slips in the proof. (1) The integrand of ∫_{(q/π)arcsin(C/B)}^{q/2} 1/sin²(πt/q) lacks the factor C; the next line has C cot. (2) min(B/sin, C/sin²) has a concave kink at arcsin(C/B), so 'by convexity' fails for the term straddling it: single-term excess up to ≈2.6% (2.58% at q = 50). The main-range total still holds (at least ≈0.24% to spare). (3) 'For any t > 0, B/t ≤ min(B/t, B/t²)' needs t ≤ 1, which is harmless since t = |sin|. The repo docstring's '≈2.55' is only the q = 2 (smallest) value of the relaxed factor. The 'also valid' log(2e²q/π) bound is used nowhere downstream; the book uses (4.6) at (4.23). The companion's formal transcription Companion.Book.lemma_4_1_3 (Companion/Book/Lemma_4_1_3.lean, not indexed by tool.py) is proved equivalent to the Lean statement by lemma_4_1_3_iff_formal. Unconditional.

lean.note: Both bounds as a conjunction, with the book's hypotheses and constants. Lean's log 0 = 0 gives max(2, ·) = 2 at C = 0, as the book's reading does. At B = 0 both sides are 0. In cone; unconditional. Only the max(2, …) conjunct is used downstream (sum_R1 in TypeIProof.lean, sum_R1L in TypeILogProof.lean).
Reduction for any nonnegative summand Φ(sin²): distinct residues R ∈ [1, q−1], shifts τ_R ∈ [0, ½].
Merges low residues r (at integers) and high q − k (at k − ½) into the points j/2, j = 1, …, q−1.

At most one point per half-integer: Σ_{j=1}^{q−1} h(j/2) ≤ h(½) + 2∫_{½}^{q/2} h, using that h is decreasing (no convexity needed). Replaces the book's majorant 2Σ_{r≤q/2} h(r−½) and its convexity step.

Bounds h(½) + (2q/π)∫_{π/2q}^{π/2} min(B/sin, C/sin²) in three cases. C ≥ B. B sin(π/2q) ≤ C < B: split at arcsin(C/B); the role of (4.7) is played by log(1+y) ≥ y log 2. C < B sin(π/2q): a/sin a + cos a ≤ 2 with a = π/2q gives the factor 2.

erratum.description: The proof first bounds the sum by X = 2Σ_{r≤q/2} min(B/sin(π(r−½)/q), C/sin²(π(r−½)/q)), which moves the integer-distance residues to half-integers. For small C, X itself exceeds the stated (2Bq/π)max(2, log(Ce³q/(Bπ))), worst at C = B sin(π/2q) ≈ Bπ/(2q). So no argument from X can give (4.6) there. For C < B sin(π/q) the proof relaxes C to B sin(π/q). This gives the constant factor 3 + log((q/π)sin(π/q)) ∈ [2.548, 3), which is above max(2, log(Ce³q/(Bπ))) for every such C. Even before the last simplification the factor is π/(q sin(π/2q)) + cos(π/q) ≥ 2.221 > 2, so C ≤ Bπ/(eq), where (4.6) claims factor 2, is not covered. The statement is true. The main range B sin(π/q) ≤ C ≤ B and the log(2e²q/π) bound are unaffected.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: for C near B sin(pi/2q) the proof's majorant X exceeds the right side of (4.6) (ratio up to 1.0696), and the relaxation to C = B sin(pi/q) gives a factor >= 2.221 > 2, so the small-C range is not proved; the main range holds.
check.note: For C < B sin(π/q) the proof's majorant X already exceeds the right side of (4.6) near C = B sin(π/2q) (ratio 1.0696 at q = 140, above 1 for every q ≤ 400 except q = 3), and the printed relaxation to C = B sin(π/q) gives the factor 3 + log((q/π)sin(π/q)) ≥ 2.548, so the range C ≤ Bπ/(eq), where (4.6) claims the factor 2, is not proved. The statement itself is true (direct evaluation stays below the bound) and the main range B sin(π/q) ≤ C ≤ B is unaffected; the claim survives.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: for C near B sin(pi/2q) the proof's majorant X exceeds the right side of (4.6) (ratio up to 1.0696), and the relaxation to C = B sin(pi/q) gives a factor >= 2.221 > 2, so the small-C range is not proved; the main range holds.

items.changes_since_2013: notation only (gcd → (a,q)); proof unchanged from 1205.5252v4 Lemma 3.3, so the gap dates from 2013

items.label: eq:shtru
items.book_statement: The displayed bound of Lemma 4.1.3: Σ_{y₁<n≤y₂, q∤n} min(B/|sin παn|, C/sin²παn) ≤ (2Bq/π)·max(2, log(Ce³q/(Bπ))).
items.note: The inequality is true (proved in Lean by a sharper argument); the book's proof does not establish it for C < B sin(π/q). That proof gap is recorded under Lemma 4.1.3.

lean.note: First conjunct; the one used downstream (TypeIProof.sum_R1, TypeILogProof.sum_R1L).

items.label: eq:somos
items.book_statement: For t ≥ 1, t log(t − √(t²−1)) + √(t²−1) < −t log 2t + t; with t = B/C it bounds the arcsin-split integral term in Lemma 4.1.3's range B sin(π/q) ≤ C ≤ B.
items.note: Checked: with y = √(1 − t⁻²) (the book's δ = 1 − y), (4.7) ⟺ y − log(1+y) < 1 − log 2; LHS − RHS = −0.3069 at t = 1 and ≈ −1/(4t) as t → ∞ (max on [1, 201]: −0.00124). Lean proves it via concavity of log instead of the book's change of variables.

lean.note: Middle case B sin(π/2q) ≤ C < B: hconc and hy2 give y − log(1+y) ≤ 1 − log 2 for y = √(1 − (C/B)²), i.e. (4.7) non-strictly with t = B/C, applied to the same term B(log x − log(1+y) + y), x = C/B.
log(1+y) ≥ y log 2 on [0, 1] (concavity of log), the key fact of the inline (4.7).

items.label: lem:bosta1
items.book_statement: Template Type I bound: for α = a/q + δ/x, |δ/x| ≤ 1/qQ₀, q ≤ Q₀, it bounds Σ_{m≤D} μ(m) Σ_n e(αmn)η(mn/x) by a main term from the m with q | m ≤ M plus error terms. The cases |δ| ≤ 1/2c₂ and |δ| ≥ 1/2c₂ are treated separately.
items.note: The book calls this lemma a 'theme' and never applies it: Lemmas 4.2.2–4.2.4 are proved by listing changes to this proof. Lean likewise does not state it (TypeI.lean header). It carries out the argument for odd m, n and η₂ in TypeIProof.lean, with Lemma 4.2.2's c₂ = 6π/5√c₀. Case (b) relies on Lemma 4.1.3, whose printed proof has a known gap; the statement is true and Lean proves it by another argument (TrigSums.lean). Slip (iv) and the (4.11) gap share a cause: ⌊x/|δq|⌋ can be below Q₀ when Q₀ ∉ ℤ. This happens in the main line, since Ch. 6, and Lean's typeI2_le_sum (TypeI2Total.lean:111), apply the odd version with Q₀ = Q/v. Slip (v) sits in batch C11's range at (4.28).

lean.note: Lemma 4.2.2 (odd m and n) for η = η₂, c₀ = 32, |η'|₁ = 8 log 2. Its proof in TypeIProof.lean redoes this lemma's argument with the changes the book lists. Uses none of the five hypotheses.

The proof's second approximation, taken with a real Q and |ξ − a/q| = 1/qQ exactly. Dirichlet (Mathlib) at ⌊(1+ε)Q⌋ gives q' ≤ (1+ε)Q, |ξ − a'/q'| ≤ 1/(q'(1+ε)Q) and q' ≥ εQ/(1+ε). The book has Q = ⌊x/|δq|⌋, Q' = ⌈(1+ε)Q⌉.
M = min(Q/2, D) with the unrounded Q = x/|δq| (M = D if δ = 0). Since x/|δq| ≥ Q₀, it lies in [min(Q₀/2, D), D], as the statement requires. The book's rounded M need not (slip (iv)).
Lemma 4.2.2: odd m, n, η = η₂, c₀ = 32.
Proves (4.30)+(4.31) for |δ| ≤ 1/2c₂ or D ≤ Q₀/2.

erratum.description: Harmless slips in the proof text; the lemma itself holds. (i) Case (b) asserts min(c₂x/q, D) ≤ Q/2 for Q = ⌊x/|δq|⌋. This can fail by < 1/2, but every integer m ≤ min(c₂x/q, D) still has m ≤ Q/2. (ii) The proof says '(ε/(1+ε))Q ≥ (2|δq|/x)⌊x/δq⌋ > 1, so q' ≥ 2'. This needs ε/(1+ε) ≥ 2|δq|/x, which Q₀ ≥ 16 guarantees only for ε ≥ 1/7, and Ch. 6 uses ε = 0.07 and 0.01. For smaller ε it can fail and q' = 1 can occur; the claim is never used. (iii) 'D ≤ (Q+1)/2 ⇒ M ≥ ⌊D⌋' fails at D = (Q+1)/2 when Q is odd. (iv) For non-integer Q₀, the proof's M = min(⌊x/|δq|⌋/2, D) can lie below min(Q₀/2, D), outside the range the statement gives. The sum over m ≤ M/q is the same as for M = min(Q₀/2, D). (v) In case (b), after (4.28), 'we have R ≥ D' should read R ≥ D'.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: all five printed assertions in the proof of Lemma 4.2.1 fail at admissible points while the stated local repairs hold.
check.note: Five slips in the proof, all harmless; the lemma holds. Each was reproduced at an admissible point (c0 = 31.521). (i) With Q = floor(x/|delta q|), case (b)'s min(c2x/q, D) <= Q/2 fails: q = 2, x = D = 1000, |delta| = 1/2c2 gives 517.317 > 517. No integer lies in between. (ii) (eps/(1+eps))Q >= (2|delta q|/x)Q holds only for eps >= 1/7. At eps = 0.01, q = 16, x/|delta q| = 16.5 it reads 0.158 < 1.939, and a'/q' = 1/1 is a valid choice, so q' = 1 occurs; q' >= 2 is never used. (iii) 'D <= (Q+1)/2 implies M >= floor(D)' fails at Q = 17, D = 9; the j = 0 block of (4.17)-(4.19) covers m = 9. (iv) At Q0 = 16.5 the proof's M = 8 is below the stated range min(Q0/2, D) = 8.25, but the m-sums are the same. (v) After (4.28), 'R >= D' should read 'R >= D''; at the (i) point R = D' = 517.3 < D.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: all five printed assertions in the proof of Lemma 4.2.1 fail at admissible points while the stated local repairs hold.

items.label: eq:gorio
items.book_statement: The basic Type I sum Σ_{m≤D} μ(m) Σ_n e(αmn) η(mn/x), with m running over the positive integers up to D and n over all integers.
items.note: The all-n sum has no Lean definition. Only odd sums enter the main line. (4.29) enters through Lemma 4.2.2, applied to each inner sum of S_{I,2} when qV ≤ Q (§6.2; Lean typeI2_le_sum, TypeI2Total.lean:111). Its log-weighted form (4.39) enters S_{I,1}, and (4.49) enters the rest of S_{I,2}. Lemma 4.2.2's case-(a) sentence cites (4.8) where it means (4.29). The repo records this (NOTES.md:1250), and the erratum belongs to that lemma's entry.

lean.note: Defines the odd analog (4.29), not (4.8): odd m ≤ ⌊D⌋, odd n ≤ ⌊x⌋ (enough, since supp η₂ ⊆ [1/4, 1]), weight η₂. typeI_eq_sum_Todd rewrites it with T_{m,∘} (Todd, (4.35)).
Odd analogue (4.29) of the sum (4.8), weight η₂.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(4.8)', 'gorio'; index types with moebius and tsum over ℤ n; defs in MinorArcs/TypeI (typeI, typeILog, typeI2 are odd/η₂ only)

items.label: eq:cupcake
items.book_statement: Main-term part of the bound: (x/q)·min(1, c₀/(2πδ)²)·|Σ_{m≤M/q, (m,q)=1} μ(m)/m| plus an error O*(c₀(1/4 − 1/π²)(D²/2xq + D/2x)), for some M ∈ [min(Q₀/2, D), D].
items.note: Not needed: the main line uses (4.30). Checked: the error is Σ_{m'≤M/q} qm'/x ≤ M²/2xq + M/2x times c₀(π² − 4)/4π² = c₀(1/4 − 1/π²). The remark after the lemma holds since (3/5)(1 + √(13/3)) = 1.849 > 1. The docstring of bound_4_40 (TypeI.lean:164) rightly calls (4.9)'s form the all-n value.

lean.note: Odd analog (4.30): x/2q, minInv c₀ (πδ) = min(1, c₀/(πδ)²), (m, 2q) = 1, error (c₀q/x)(1/8 − 1/2π²)(D/q + 1)², with the specific M = Mof.
Proves that bound for the terms with q | m ≤ M (m odd), via Todd_main, moebius_odd_term and Σ_{m' odd ≤ N} m' ≤ ((N+1)/2)² (sum_odd_le).
|η̂₂(−δ/2)| ≤ min(1, c₀/(πδ)²), the odd counterpart of bounding |η̂(−δ)| by min(1, c₀/(2πδ)²) via (2.1).
Odd analogue (4.30) of (4.9).

items.label: eq:kuche1
items.book_statement: Error terms for |δ| ≤ 1/2c₂ (or D ≤ Q₀/2): (2√(c₀c₁)/π)D + 3c₁(x/q)log⁺(Dq/c₂x) + (√(c₀c₁)/π)q log⁺(2D/q) + (|η'|₁/π)q·max(2, log(c₀e³q²/4π|η'|₁x)) + (2√(3c₀c₁)/π + 3c₁/c₂ + 55c₀c₂/12π²)q.
items.note: Not needed: the main line uses (4.31). Consistent with the proof: (4.10) is (4.28) after 3c₁ min(q/c₂, 2x/q) ≤ 3c₁q/c₂. The max(2, …) term is Lemma 4.1.3 with B = |η'|₁/2 and C = c₀q/8x. That lemma's printed proof has a gap, but its statement is true and proved in Lean.

lean.note: Odd analog (4.31): (3c₁/2)(x/q)log⁺, (2|η'|₁/π)q·max(1, …), 3c₁/2c₂, 55c₀c₂/6π², with c₁ = 1 + |η'|₁/(x/D) and c₂ = 6π/5√c₀.
Proves (4.30) + (4.31) when |δ| ≤ 1/2c₂ or D ≤ Q₀/2, via norm_restPart_le_caseB (sum_R1, sum_R2, sum_R3, Lean's versions of (4.23)–(4.27)).
Odd analogue (4.31) of (4.10).
Proves (4.30)+(4.31) for |δ| ≤ 1/2c₂ or D ≤ Q₀/2.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(4.10)', 'kuche1', 'c₂ = (3π/5√c₀)(1+√(13/3))'; MinorArcs/TypeI, TypeIProof

items.label: eq:kallervo
items.book_statement: Error terms for |δ| ≥ 1/2c₂ and any ε ∈ (0,1]: (2√(c₀c₁)/π)(D + (1+ε)min(⌊x/|δ|q⌋+1, 2D)(ϖ_ε + ½log⁺(2D|δ|q/x))) + 3c₁(2 + ((1+ε)/ε)log⁺(2D|δ|q/x))x/Q₀ + (35c₀c₂/6π²)q.
items.note: Not needed: the main line uses (4.32), whose book proof takes the same x/Q → x/Q₀ step. The other replacements in the closing step are valid: (1+ε)(Q+1) → (1+ε)min(⌊x/|δ|q⌋+1, 2D), and log⁺(2D/(Q+1)) ≤ log⁺(2D|δ|q/x).

lean.note: Odd analog (4.32): √(3+2ε) for ϖ_ε, (3/2)c₁ in the x/Q₀ term, 35c₀c₂/3π², and Lemma 4.2.2's c₁, c₂. Keeps min(⌊x/|δ|q⌋₊ + 1, 2D), log⁺ and x/Q₀.
Proves (4.30) + (4.32) for |δ| ≥ 1/2c₂ and any ε > 0, via norm_restPart_le_caseA. lemma_4_2_2 adds the statement's ε ≤ 1.
Odd analogue (4.32) of (4.11).

items.label: eq:crinfo
items.book_statement: Poisson summation for a term with q | m ≤ M: Σ_n e(αmn)η(mn/x) = (x/m)η̂(−δ) plus the other frequencies. These are at most (m/x)(c₀/4π²)·max_{|r|≤1/2}Σ_{n≠0}(n−r)⁻², and the maximum is π² − 4.
items.note: Checked numerically: Σ_{n≠0}(n − r)⁻² = 3.2899, 3.7392 and 5.8696 at r = 0, 1/4 and 1/2, and π² − 4 = 5.8696. The all-n computation itself is not in Lean. The main line needs only its odd version, which the book derives the same way ((4.33)–(4.34)).

lean.note: Odd-n analog (4.33)–(4.34) for η₂: T_{m,∘} = κ'((x/2m)η̂₂(−δ/2) + E) with |E| ≤ (m/x)(c₀/2π²)(π² − 4) when |δm/x| ≤ 1/2. Uses Mathlib's Poisson formula after n = 2r + 1.
For |r| ≤ 1/2, Σ_{n≠0}(n − r)⁻² ≤ π² − 4 (and the series is summable). This is the bound behind (4.12)'s last O* and the next display. Proved by pairing ±n (pair_le_half), not by convexity.
The value π² − 4 at r = 1/2, from Σ_{n∈ℤ}(n − s)⁻² = π²/sin²(πs) (hasSum_inv_sq_sub, via Parseval).
(2.1) with k = 2 for η₂: |η̂₂(t)| ≤ c₀/(2πt)², c₀ = 32.

items.label: eq:aoro
items.book_statement: Pointwise bound for T_m(α) = Σ_n e(αmn)η(mn/x): |T_m(α)| is at most the least of x/m + |η'|₁/2, (|η'|₁/2)/|sin πmα| and (c₀m/4x)/sin²(πmα). It follows from (2.2) and Lemma 2.3.1.
items.note: Lean writes T_{m,∘} = e(αm)Σ_r f(r)e(2αmr) with f(u) = η₂((2m/x)u + m/x) (Todd_eq). Then |f|₁ = x/2m, |f̂''|_∞ ≤ 2c₀m/x (fourier_bound_fodd) and the variation is at most 8 log 2. This is the book's own route from (4.13) to (4.36).

lean.note: (4.36), the odd-n analog for η₂: x/2m + |η'|₁/2, (|η'|₁/2)/|sin 2πmα| and (m/x)(c₀/2)/sin²(2πmα).
Lemma 2.3.1; gives the third bound.
First bound of (2.2), with the total variation in place of |f'|₁; gives the first bound.
Second bound of (2.2), by summation by parts; gives the second bound.

items.label: eq:gowo
items.book_statement: On a block y₁ < m ≤ y₂ (length ≤ q, y₂ ≤ Q/2): Σ_{q∤m}|T_m| ≤ Σ_{q∤m} min(A, C/sin²(πmα)) with A = x/y₁ + |η'|₁/2 and C = (c₀/4)y₂/x. This is the form Lemma 4.1.2 takes as input.
items.note: As the book's proof of 4.2.2 says, for odd n C doubles and A halves, which gives c₁ = 1 + |η'|₁/(x/D). sum_A1's cruder A = x/2 + |η'|₁/2 is harmless there, because only Lemma 4.1.2's first bound, which does not involve A, is used. The conditions y₂ − y₁ ≤ q and y₂ ≤ Q/2 serve Lemma 4.1.2, not (4.14) itself.

lean.note: Odd-n pointwise form: |T_{m,∘}| ≤ min(A, C/sin²) whenever A ≥ x/2m + |η'|₁/2, C ≥ (m/x)(c₀/2) and sin ≠ 0.
The same with minA (value A where sin = 0). Used with lemma_4_1_1' for blocks that contain multiples of the denominator.
Per-block step (hterm) in case (a): on block j, A = x/2 + |η'|₁/2 and C = (c₀/2)(j+1)q/x, followed by lemma_4_1_2.
Per-block step for range R3 and the a'/q' blocks: A = c₁x/2y, C = (c₀/2)(y + q)/x, over all n (no condition q ∤ m).

items.label: eq:esthel
items.book_statement: What remains after the main term: Σ_{m≤M, q∤m}|T_m(α)| + Σ_{Q/2<m≤D}|T_m(α)|. Together the two sums cover every m ≤ D except the multiples of q up to M.
items.note: The bookkeeping is exact. Lean's split depends only on M, never on (Q+1)/2.

lean.note: ‖restPart‖ ≤ Σ_{0<n≤D, ¬(q∣n ∧ n≤M)} |T_{n,∘}|: the odd analog, using |μ| ≤ 1 to drop μ.
typeI = mainPart (odd m ≤ M with q | m) + restPart.
hsplit splits the range at M into Σ_{n≤M, q∤n} + Σ_{M<n≤D}. This equals the book's split, since M < D forces M = Q/2.

items.label: eq:jenuf
items.book_statement: Case (a), |δ| ≥ 1/2c₂: blocks of length q and Lemma 4.1.2's first bound give Σ_{m≤M, q∤m}|T_m| ≤ (5c₀c₂/6π²)M + (35c₀c₂/6π²)q, using qM²/x ≤ c₂M and q² ≤ 2c₂x.
items.note: Algebra checked: Σ_{0≤j≤M/q}(j+1) ≤ ½(M/q)² + (3/2)(M/q) + 1. Also q ≤ 2c₂x/Q₀ and q ≤ Q₀ give q² ≤ 2c₂x. The sentence after (4.16), 'D ≤ (Q+1)/2 ⇒ M ≥ ⌊D⌋', has a boundary slip, recorded under Lemma 4.2.1.

lean.note: Twice the bound as it stands before the last two steps: (5c₀/3π²)(qM²/x + 3q²M/x + 2q³/x) for M ≤ Q/2 (odd n doubles C). Proved with Lemma 4.1.2 on q-blocks.
hqM (qM/x ≤ c₂), hq2 (q² ≤ 2c₂x) and hA1' give (2√c₀/π)M + (35c₀c₂/3π²)q. That is twice (4.16)'s last line, rewritten with (4.37).

items.label: eq:tenda
items.book_statement: Integral comparison for the blocks built on the second approximation a'/q': Σ_j x/(jq' + (Q+1)/2) ≤ 2x/Q + ((1+ε)x/εQ)log⁺(2D/(Q+1)), using q' ≥ εQ/(1+ε).
items.note: Correct as printed. Lean reaches x/Q₀ at once because Qr ≥ Q₀. The book's 2x/Q and (1+ε)x/εQ, with Q = ⌊x/|δq|⌋, are where the gap recorded at (4.11) begins.

lean.note: Σ_{j<J} 1/(R + jq) ≤ 1/R + (1/q)log(D/R) when R + (J−1)q ≤ D: the first inequality, for general R and q.
Here R = M = Qr/2, with Qr = x/|δq| real. hxM gives x/M ≤ 2x/Q₀, and hxq' gives x/q' ≤ ((1+ε)/ε)x/Q₀ from second_approx.

items.label: eq:beatri
items.note: Correct as printed; each step checked. The first term uses 2((1+ε)Q+1)/(Q+1) ≤ 2(1+ε), and the j ≥ 1 terms are compared with the integral of a decreasing function.

lean.note: Σ_{j<J}√(1 + q/(R + jq)) ≤ √(1 + q/R) + (D − R)/q + ½log(D/R): the general form.
hsqrt: √(1 + q'/M) ≤ √(3+2ε), since q' ≤ (1+ε)Qr and M = Qr/2. hq'min: q' ≤ (1+ε)min(⌊Qr⌋₊ + 1, 2D), in place of the book's q' ≤ (1+ε)(Q+1).

items.label: eq:sauna
items.note: For odd n the 3c₁ line is halved (book's proof of 4.2.2), as in sum_R3'. Lean keeps D − M rather than expanding D − (Q+1)/2.

lean.note: For any approximation a/q and 0 < R < D: Σ_{R<m≤D}|T_{m,∘}| ≤ (3c₁/2)(x/R + (x/q)log(D/R)) + (2√(c₀c₁)/π)q(√(1+q/R) + (D−R)/q + ½log(D/R)). Applied with a'/q' and R = M (hA2, line 1235).
Bounds one block via lemma_4_1_1': the per-block display just before (4.17).
hpart1 and hpart2 insert the bounds on q', giving the odd analog of (4.19).

items.label: eq:kullervo
items.book_statement: Adding (4.16) with M = Q/2 to (4.19) bounds all of (4.15) by (2√(c₀c₁)/π)(D + (1+ε)(Q+1)(ϖ_ε + ½log⁺(…))) + 3c₁(2 + ((1+ε)/ε)log(…))x/Q + (35c₀c₂/6π²)q.
items.note: Apart from the typo the combination checks out: ((1+ε)√(3+2ε) − ½) + (1/8)(1 + √(13/3)) = (1+ε)ϖ_ε, using (4.21) and Q ≤ Q + 1.

lean.note: Odd analog. The (2√c₀/π)M from sum_A1 cancels the −(2√(c₀c₁)/π)M from D − M (via (4.37)), so √(3+2ε) replaces ϖ_ε. The case D ≤ M is treated directly (lines 1207–1216).
The resulting odd-n bound (4.32), with logPlus in both places.

erratum.description: The second line prints log D/((Q+1)/2) where (4.19) and the statement (4.11) have log⁺. The display is still correct where it is derived (D > (Q+1)/2, so log = log⁺). The next remark, that (4.20) 'is valid also when D ≤ Q/2', is false with log: the term 3c₁((1+ε)/ε)log(2D/(Q+1))x/Q is then negative and can dominate.

items.label: eq:semin1
items.book_statement: Constant identity that lets the M-term of (4.16) be absorbed into ϖ_ε: 5c₀c₂/6π² = (√c₀/2π)(1+√(13/3)) ≤ (2√(c₀c₁)/π)·¼(1+√(13/3)), since c₁ ≥ 1.
items.note: Checked: for c₀ = 31.521 all three expressions equal 2.75363 at c₁ = 1. The inequality only needs c₁ ≥ 1. Neither 1 + √(13/3) nor ϖ_ε occurs anywhere in the Lean sources.

lean.note: (4.37): 5c₀c₂/3π² = 2√c₀/π for Lean's c₂, which is what the book's proof of 4.2.2 prescribes in place of (4.21). In case (a) it is used in hA1' of norm_restPart_le_caseA (TypeIProof.lean:1181–1195, rewrite at 1195), where it gives (2√c₀/π)M, cancelled exactly against −(2√(c₀c₁)/π)M. In case (b) it is used in hB2 of norm_restPart_le_caseB (line 943) and, via c₂_identity', at line 959.

items.label: eq:semin2
items.book_statement: Defines ϖ_ε = √(3+2ε) + ((1+√(13/3))/4 − 1)/(2(1+ε)). This constant absorbs the M-term of (4.16) into the (Q+1)-term of Lemma 4.2.1's case-(a) bound (4.20)/(4.11). ϖ_ε < √3 for ε < 0.1741.
items.note: ϖ_ε occurs only in Lemma 4.2.1 ((4.11), (4.20)), which Lean does not state. Lemma 4.2.3's proof says it uses (4.21)–(4.22) 'as before', but its case-(a) bound (4.42), which Lean omits, also has √(3+2ε). Checked numerically: ϖ_ε = √3 at ε = 0.174119, so the remark 'ϖ_ε < √3 for ε < 0.1741' is correct.

lean.note: In the odd-n Lemma 4.2.2, (4.37) gives 5c₀c₂/3π² = 2√c₀/π, so the correction term vanishes. (4.32), and therefore bound_4_32, has √(3+2ε) where (4.11) has ϖ_ε.

items.label: eq:prokof
items.book_statement: Case (b) of Lemma 4.2.1's proof: the terms with m ≤ q/2 satisfy Σ|T_m(α)| ≤ (|η'|₁/π)q·max(2, log(c₀e³q²/(4π|η'|₁x))). This follows from the bounds (4.13) on T_m and Lemma 4.1.3.
items.note: The all-n (4.23) is a step in the proof of Lemma 4.2.1, which Lean does not formalize; only the odd-n analogue exists. Its input, Lemma 4.1.3, has a gap in its printed proof. The lemma's statement is true (TrigSums.lean proves it by another argument), so (4.23) stands. sum_R1 is reused for Lemma 4.2.4 (TypeI2Rest.lean:118).

lean.note: The odd-n form that Lemma 4.2.2 uses (η = η₂, 2α = a/q+δ/x): Σ_{0<m≤q/2}|T_{m,∘}| ≤ (2|η'|₁/π)q·max(1, log(c₀e³q²/(4π|η'|₁x))). This is (4.23) with the second term of the max doubled, as the book prescribes.
Applied with B = |η'|₁/2 and C = c₀q/(4x); C is doubled for odd n.
max(2, log 2X) ≤ 2·max(1, log X). This turns the doubled C inside the log into the book's 'doubled second term of the max'.

items.label: eq:martinu
items.book_statement: Case (b), when q² < 2c₂x: the terms q/2 < m ≤ D' = min(c₂x/q, D) with q∤m are bounded in blocks of length q by the first bound of Lemma 4.1.2. The total is at most (5c₀c₂/6π²)(D' + 11q/2).
items.note: (4.24) itself is an all-n step of Lemma 4.2.1. Lean has only the doubled odd-n form that the proof of Lemma 4.2.2 requires. block_R2 is reused for Lemma 4.2.4 (TypeI2Rest.lean:143).

lean.note: Odd n, doubled: Σ_{q/2<m≤D', q∤m}|T_{m,∘}| ≤ (5c₀/3π²)(qD'²/x + 3q²D'/x + 5q³/4x) for D' ≤ Q/2. This is twice (20/3π²)(c₀q³/4x)·Σ_{1≤j≤D'/q+1/2}(j+½), evaluated before D' ≤ c₂x/q is used.
One block: Lemma 4.1.2 with C = (c₀/2)(j+3/2)q/x.
Step hB2. D' ≤ c₂x/q and q² < 2c₂x (from q/2 < D') give (5c₀c₂/3π²)(D'+11q/2), which c₂_identity turns into (2√c₀/π)(D'+11q/2). This is (4.24) doubled. The range is empty when D' ≤ q/2.
Its first bound, (20/3π²)Cq².

erratum.description: Case (b) opens with min(c₂x/q, D) ≤ Q/2, and (4.24) applies Lemma 4.1.2 because min(c₂x/q, D) < Q/2, where Q = ⌊x/|δq|⌋. Because of the rounding, this can fail by less than 1/2 in both sub-cases of case (b). In sub-case (i), |δ| ≤ 1/2c₂ is close to 1/2c₂ and c₂x/q > Q/2. In sub-case (ii), D ≤ Q₀/2 with Q₀ not an integer: ⌊x/|δq|⌋ can be below Q₀, so D > Q/2. §6.2.2 uses Q₀ = Q/v. The gap is harmless. In both sub-cases min(c₂x/q, D) ≤ X/2 with X = x/|δq|, and m is an integer, so ⌊D'⌋ ≤ ⌊X/2⌋ ≤ ⌊X⌋/2 = Q/2 and the last block can end at ⌊D'⌋. Separately, the first line has |η₁'|/2 for |η'|₁/2. This is a typo, and that argument of the min is unused.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: min(c2x/q,D) exceeds Q/2 = floor(x/|delta q|)/2 by less than 1/2 at admissible points of both sub-cases of case (b), while floor(D') <= Q/2 always holds.
check.note: With Q = floor(x/|delta q|), case (b)'s 'min(c2x/q, D) < Q/2', used to apply Lemma 4.1.2 in (4.24), can fail by less than 1/2. Sub-case (i) fails at q = 2, x = D = 2000, |delta| = 1/2c2 (1034.634 > 1034.5). Sub-case (ii) fails at Q0 = 16.5, x/|delta q| = 16.7, D = 8.25 (8.25 > 8), for Lemma 4.2.1 and for Lemma 4.2.2, including q >= 2. The gap is harmless because floor(D') <= Q/2 in every case. The |eta_1'|/2 in the first line, for |eta'|_1/2, is a typo in an unused argument and was not checked numerically.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: min(c2x/q,D) exceeds Q/2 = floor(x/|delta q|)/2 by less than 1/2 at admissible points of both sub-cases of case (b), while floor(D') <= Q/2 always holds.

items.changes_since_2013: notation only (alignment) vs 1205.5252v4 (3.24), including the same rounding claim and the |η₁'| typo. The tool's second match, 1312.7748v2 (5.21), is an unrelated equation (a G_q ratio in lem:paniz) that reuses the label eq:martinu.

items.label: eq:caron
items.book_statement: Case (b), range R < m ≤ D with R = max(c₂x/q, q/2): split into blocks of length q and apply the second bound of Lemma 4.1.1 with A = c₁x/(jq+R) and C = (c₀/4)((j+1)q+R)/x. Result: Σ_j[3c₁x/(jq+R) + (4q/π)√((c₁c₀/4)(1+q/(jq+R)))].
items.note: All m in (R, D] are kept, including q | m (since |T_m| ≥ 0), so no Q/2 restriction is needed, in Lean as in the book. The book's '(4.26) gets halved' for Lemma 4.2.2 is the coefficient 3c₁/2 in block_R3.

lean.note: Odd-n block bound: ≤ (3c₁/2)x/(R+jq) + (2q√(c₀c₁)/π)√(1+q/(R+jq)), with c₁ = 1+|η'|₁/(x/D). A halves and C doubles, so √(AC) is unchanged.
Sums the J = ⌈(D−R)/q⌉ blocks (sum_Ioc_le_blocks) and applies (4.26)–(4.27). Holds for any R > 0 and is also used in case (a) with a'/q'.
Lemma 4.1.1 with the honest summand minA, which handles sin = 0.

items.label: eq:kosto
items.book_statement: Bounds Σ_{0≤j≤(D−R)/q} x/(jq+R) first by x/R + (x/q)∫_R^D dt/t. Since R = max(c₂x/q, q/2), this is at most min(q/c₂, 2x/q) + (x/q)log⁺(D/(c₂x/q)).
items.note: The min(q/c₂, 2x/q) of (4.26)/(4.28) enters (4.31) only as q/c₂, so the weaker Lean form loses nothing downstream. sum_inv_le is reused for Lemma 4.2.4 (TypeI2Rest.lean:288).

lean.note: First inequality only (divided by x), for any R, q > 0: Σ_{j<J} 1/(R+jq) ≤ 1/R + (1/q)log(D/R) when R+(J−1)q ≤ D.
Yields (3c₁/2)(x/R + (x/q)log(D/R)), i.e. (4.26) halved for odd n.
Second inequality, weakened. hxR proves only x/R ≤ q/c₂; the 2x/q branch of the min is dropped. hl1 gives log(D/R) ≤ log⁺(D/(c₂x/q)).

items.label: eq:kostas
items.book_statement: Bounds Σ_{0≤j≤(D−R)/q} √(1+q/(jq+R)) first by √(1+q/R) + (1/q)∫_R^D √(1+q/t)dt. Since R ≥ q/2, this is at most √3 + (D−R)/q + ½log⁺(D/(q/2)).
items.note: With R ≥ q/2, sum_sqrt_le implies the final bound of (4.27); the book's middle (integral) expression is not stated in Lean. The −R/q part is what absorbs the D'-term of (4.24) (hcancel, TypeIProof.lean:994).

lean.note: For any R, q > 0 with R+(J−1)q ≤ D: Σ_{j<J}√(1+q/(R+jq)) ≤ √(1+q/R) + (D−R)/q + ½log(D/R). The integral form is skipped; Lean bounds directly via √(1+u) ≤ 1+u/2.
hl2: log(D/R) ≤ log⁺(D/(q/2)).

items.changes_since_2013: notation only (the display is split into aligned lines) vs 1205.5252v4 (3.27)

items.label: eq:kabanova
items.book_statement: Case (b) of Lemma 4.2.1: summing (4.23), (4.24) and (4.25)–(4.27) bounds the sum (4.15); the D′-term of (4.24) is absorbed by the −R/q term of (4.27). Weakening the min yields (4.10); its odd-n analogue, weakened likewise, is (4.31).
items.note: Lemma 4.2.1 is not stated in Lean (TypeI.lean module docstring). (4.28) enters only as the template for case (b) of Lemma 4.2.2, whose proof the book says carries over with the listed changes. The status is 'variant' rather than 'inlined' because a standalone theorem, norm_restPart_le_caseB, states the odd-n analogue. erratum.description: (6.53) inherits the misprinted main term of (4.40) through (6.3)/(6.4). It has prefactor (x/q)min(1,c₀'/δ²) with c₀' ≈ c₀/(2π)², and μ-sums over (m,q)=1. Those are the values for a sum over all n. For S_{I,1} (m, n odd), Poisson summation over odd n gives a main term of (x/2q)μ(q)[η̂(−δ/2)Σ_{(m,2q)=1}μ(m)/m·log(x/mq) + (log·η)^(−δ/2)Σ_{(m,2q)=1}μ(m)/m]. Lemma 4.2.3's own computation (f̂ at (x/m)t − δ/2) and (4.30) give the same. |η̂(−δ/2)| can nearly reach c₀/(πδ)², four times the printed decay. A counterexample shows the printed (6.53) is false: at x = 2.16·10^20, q = 101, a = 1, δ = 10.8, its RHS is 3.07·10^16 but |S_{I,1}| ≥ 5.88·10^16. As bounds, the corrected first line exceeds the printed one by 2× to ≈5.7× for large |δ|; the c_{4,I} term alone is 4×. For |δ| ≤ 0.894 the excess is up to ≈1.43×. Thm 3.1.1 is not affected. Redo (6.54)–(6.55) on the corrected first line, with [H]'s 4/5 and 1.00303 at modulus 2q and min(1,c₀/(πδ)²) ≤ 2/δ₀. The result is ≤ (2x/(δ₀φ(q)))(0.875 log δ₀q + 3.9332), which fits inside the (7/4)log δ₀q + 6.11676 slot [H] uses for (6.56) and L_{x,t,q}.

Only consumer: Σ|a₁|² ≤ σ(x)x in the minor-arc total ((14.30) analogue).

With the factor, the same argument gives (9.94) with ≈3.89·10⁻⁶ log x + 1.26·10⁻⁶, and hence only |E₂| ≲ 3.94·10⁻⁶ + 366.91/√x at x = 10¹², not 2·10⁻⁶ + 366.91/√x. items.label: eq:manon
items.book_statement: Heuristic shape of an explicit formula: S_{η,χ}(δ/x,x) = [q=1]η̂(−δ)x − Σ_ρ F_δ(ρ)x^ρ + small error, summing over non-trivial zeros of L(s,χ), with F_δ the Mellin transform of e(δt)η(t).
items.note: Its rigorous form in the book is Lemma 9.1.1 (lem:agamon). Here F_δ is Chapter 9's G_δ (Lean: mellin φ); Chapter 8's F_δ denotes the twisted-Gaussian transform. Status 'variant': the schematic 'small error' cannot be stated, but precise explicit formulas playing this role are proved. The book's Lemma 9.1.1 error terms are replaced in Lean by Jensen/Landau-based bounds.

lean.note: Rigorous form for primitive χ ≠ 1 and any GoodSmoothing φ (e.g. φ = e(δ·)η). The zero sum over (−1/2, 3/2)×(−T_k, T_k), along T_k → ∞, tends to −S − (1/2π)∫(L'/L)G x^s over Re s = −1/2. That line integral is the 'small error'; the trivial zero s = 0 of even χ is inside the sum. Its docstring says 'for η = t²e^{−t²/2}', but the statement is general.
q = 1: the main term M(1)x = x∫₀^∞e(δt)η(t)dt = η̂(−δ)x appears explicitly.
Generic contour identity for an entire L-datum f, from which both are derived.

items.label: thm:princo
items.book_statement: Explicit bounds for the Mellin transform F_δ(s) of e^{−t²/2}e(δt), σ ≥ 0, τ ≠ 0: for sgn δ ≠ sgn τ a saddle-point bound |Γ(s)|e^{πτ/2−E(ρ)τ}·(c₁τ^{−σ/2} or c₂ℓ^{−σ}), ρ = 4τ/ℓ²; otherwise the bound (8.3), which carries a factor e^{−ℓ²/2}.
items.note: The book uses this theorem only through Cor 8.0.2; Ch. 9 (expform l.606, l.794) mentions direct use as an option. Lean replaces the theorem and its proof by MellinRotate.lean. Maximizing Lean's exponent θ − (2/ρ)sin²θ/cos2θ over θ gives exactly E(ρ), at cos2θ = 1/υ(ρ); there θ* = ½arccos(1/υ) is the argument of the t-plane saddle point. So the rotation reaches the saddle-point exponent; Lean fixes θ = 0.28 or 0.1866ρ. (8.1) checked numerically for τ > 0: |F|/bound ≤ 0.80 for both forms, |δ| up to 20. Two further errata belong to sub-items: the c₂ derivation gap (Eq 8.2) and the conservative coefficient 1 + π/2^{3/2} in (8.3), where the proof gives 1 + π/2^{5/2}.

lean.note: Rotates the ray, t = re^{iθ} with 0 ≤ θ < π/4, for G_δ(s) = F_δ(s+2), −1 ≤ Re s ≤ 1, either sign of δτ. Bound: |G_δ(s)| ≤ e^{−θ|τ|+(2π|δ|sinθ)²/(2cos2θ)} times an explicit Gaussian-moment constant. No Γ(s) factor, no saddle point.
The rotated integral does not depend on θ for |θ| < π/4 and Re s > −2: ∂_θ of the integrand equals i∂_r of r·integrand. Replaces the book's contour shift through Temme's identity (8.10)–(8.11).
∫₀^∞ r^p e^{−cr²/2+br} dr ≤ e^{b²/2c}((1+(b/c)²)√(2π/c)+√π/(c√(c/2))) for 0 ≤ p ≤ 2 and c > 0. Replaces the book's estimates of the contour pieces I₁, I₂, I₃.

erratum.description: (i) New: the good-sign bound (8.3) is false when ρ = 4|τ|/ℓ² is small. For large ℓ it fails for every ρ < 0.8137, the root of ρ² + 6πρ = 16. The proof (book p. 158) bounds the L₃ piece {iy : y ≤ −x₀} using ∫_{−∞}^{−ℓ}e^{−t²/2}dt ≤ √(π/2)e^{−ℓ²/2} ([AS64, 7.1.13]). That step needs ℓ ≥ 0, but in this case ℓ < 0 (taking τ > 0). The Gaussian e^{−(y−ℓ)²/2} peaks at y = ℓ, inside the range when |ℓ| > x₀, so the piece has size x₀^{−σ}e^{ℓ²/2−π|τ|/2}, and the last term of (8.3) wrongly keeps the factor e^{−ℓ²/2}. (ii) The first case of (8.4), |x₀| ≥ 0.51729√τ 'for ρ arbitrary', holds only for ρ ≥ 3/2. (iii) For τ < 0, τ, ℓ and ρ in (8.1) and (8.4) need absolute values, as the proof says after (8.42).

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: (8.3) is false for small rho (|F(1+i)|=0.01747 with delta=1 against 4.2e-8; at tau=400 it fails at rho=0.813 and holds at rho=0.82), the first case of (8.4) fails for rho<1.49997, and (8.1) holds for tau<0 only with absolute values.
check.note: The good-sign bound (8.3) is false for small rho=4|tau|/ell^2 (s=1+i, delta=1: |F|=0.017470 against 4.16e-8; asymptotically it fails for rho below about 0.8156, the claim's 0.8137 being the approximation rho^2+6pi rho=16), because the L_3 step on p.158 uses a Gaussian tail bound that needs ell>=0 while ell<0. Also the first case of (8.4) holds only for rho>=1.49997 (not for all rho), and (8.1) for tau<0 holds only with |tau|, |ell|, |rho| (s=1-20i, delta=1: |F|=0.02488, literal bound 1.26e-21, with absolute values 0.0612); the claim survives.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: (8.3) is false for small rho (|F(1+i)|=0.01747 with delta=1 against 4.2e-8; at tau=400 it fails at rho=0.813 and holds at rho=0.82), the first case of (8.4) fails for rho<1.49997, and (8.1) holds for tau<0 only with absolute values.

items.changes_since_2013: 2013 Thm 3.1: the bad-sign bound was a three-term sum C₀e^{−E(|τ|/(πδ)²)|τ|} + C₁e^{−0.4798|τ|} + C₂e^{−min(τ²/8(πδ)², 25|τ|/32)}. The good-sign bound was C′e^{−π|τ|/4} for |τ| ≥ 2, with no e^{−ℓ²/2} factor. Book: one factorized bound |Γ(s)|e^{πτ/2}e^{−E(ρ)τ}(c₁/τ^{σ/2} or c₂/ℓ^σ). The new good-sign bound (8.3)–(8.4) carries |x₀|^{−σ}e^{−ℓ²/2}|Γ(s)|, and the new factor e^{−ℓ²/2} is what fails for small ρ. 'δ ≠ 0' is added. The proof uses Temme's identity (8.10) instead of a direct saddle point on (8.8).

items.label: eq:wilen
items.book_statement: Bad-sign estimate: if sgn δ ≠ sgn τ and δ ≠ 0, |F_δ(s)| ≤ |Γ(s)|e^{(π/2)τ}e^{−E(ρ)τ} times c_{1,σ,τ}τ^{−σ/2} for every ρ, or c_{2,σ,τ}ℓ^{−σ} when ρ = 4τ/ℓ² ≤ 3/2.
items.note: My quadrature (about 250 points, σ ∈ [0.25,3], τ ∈ [2,200], δ < 0): |F_δ|/bound ≤ 0.70 for the c₁ form and ≤ 0.75 for the c₂ form, consistent with the claimed near-optimality. In Cor 8.0.2's proof |Γ(s)|e^{πτ/2} is bounded by Stirling ((8.52)); Lean's bound needs no Γ factor.

lean.note: Lean's exponent is −|τ|(θ−(2/ρ)sin²θ/cos2θ), ρ = 4|τ|/ℓ²; its maximum over θ is E(ρ), so (8.1)'s decay is reachable, but Lean uses only θ = 0.28 (0.1598|τ| for ρ ≥ 3/2) and θ = 0.1866ρ (0.1065ρ|τ|). Prefactor is Lean's Gaussian constant.
Triangle inequality on the rotated ray, sign of θ matched to sgn τ, δ-term bounded through |δ|: one bound for both sign cases.

erratum.description: Same finding as under Theorem 8.0.1: (8.1) is printed for τ > 0 (τ^{σ/2}, ℓ^σ, e^{(π/2)τ−E(ρ)τ}, ρ = 4τ/ℓ²) although τ < 0 is allowed; absolute values on τ, ℓ, ρ are needed, as the proof states after (8.42).

items.changes_since_2013: 2013 (3.1) was a three-term sum C_{0,τ,ℓ}e^{−E(|τ|/(πδ)²)|τ|} + C_{1,τ}e^{−0.4798|τ|} + C_{2,τ,ℓ}e^{−min(τ²/(8(πδ)²), 25|τ|/32)}; the book has one factorized bound with two prefactor options, adds δ ≠ 0, and writes τ where 2013 had |τ|.

items.label: eq:cormo
items.book_statement: Defines E(ρ) = ½(arccos(1/υ(ρ)) − 2(υ(ρ)−1)/ρ), with υ(ρ) = √((1+√(1+ρ²))/2), and the prefactors c_{1,σ,τ} (contour angle β = π/8) and c_{2,σ,τ} (β = π/6 or π/5, for ρ ≤ 3/2).

lean.note: No Lean definition of E, υ, c₁, c₂. Lean's exponent per unit |τ| at angle θ is θ − (2/ρ)sin²θ/cos2θ; its maximum on [0, π/4) equals E(ρ) exactly (cos2θ* = 1/υ(ρ)). Prefactors are Lean's own.

erratum.description: In deriving c₂ (before (8.41)), min(2^{σ+1/2}, √sec(2π/5)/sin(π/5)^σ) picks the contour angle β = π/5 when σ > 1.4875, but the third term e^{−τ/6}3^{σ/2} is the I₃ bound for β = π/6; that contour's printed I₃ bound is e^{−0.11803τ}/tan(π/5)^σ. Claim survives: y₀ = Im u₀,₊ ≥ ℓ improves I₃ to e^{−0.6295τ}/tan(π/5)^σ.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: for sigma > 1.48748 the printed c_2 mixes the beta=pi/5 I_2 bound with the beta=pi/6 I_3 bound (one contour gives c_2 = 5.05219 at sigma=3, tau=20, kappa_{2,0} = 8.0071 > 7.96), but y_0 >= ell gives an I_3 bound e^{-0.6295 tau}/tan(pi/5)^sigma that restores the printed c_2.
check.note: For sigma>1.48748 the printed c_2 takes the beta=pi/5 I_2 term but the beta=pi/6 I_3 term e^{-tau/6}3^{sigma/2}; with the book's beta=pi/5 I_3 estimate e^{-0.11803tau}/tan(pi/5)^sigma one gets c_2=5.05219 (not 5.02186) at tau=20, sigma=3, and kappa_{2,0}=8.007>7.96, kappa_{1,0}=4.958>4.903. Using y_0>=ell the I_3 bound becomes e^{-0.6295tau}/tan(pi/5)^sigma, which restores the printed c_2 and kappas; the claim survives as a proof gap, and |F| is at most 0.40 of the printed bound at the sampled points.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: for sigma > 1.48748 the printed c_2 mixes the beta=pi/5 I_2 bound with the beta=pi/6 I_3 bound (one contour gives c_2 = 5.05219 at sigma=3, tau=20, kappa_{2,0} = 8.0071 > 7.96), but y_0 >= ell gives an I_3 bound e^{-0.6295 tau}/tan(pi/5)^sigma that restores the printed c_2.

items.changes_since_2013: E(ρ), υ(ρ) unchanged (2013 wrote E(|τ|/(πδ)²), the same ρ); the 2013 constants C_{0,τ,ℓ}, C_{1,τ}, C_{2,τ,ℓ} (with P_σ) are replaced by c_{1,σ,τ}, c_{2,σ,τ}.

items.label: eq:octop
items.book_statement: Good-sign case (sgn δ = sgn τ, or δ = 0): |F_δ(s)| ≤ |x₀|^{−σ}e^{−ℓ²/2}|Γ(s)|e^{(π/2)|τ|}((1+π/2^{3/2})e^{−(π/4)|τ|} + ½e^{−π|τ|}), where x₀ is the real part of the saddle point.
items.note: Cor 8.0.2's proof turns (8.3)–(8.4) into (8.50) for |τ| ≥ 20. It uses (1+π/2^{3/2})e^{−5π} + ½e^{−20π} ≤ 7.8·10⁻⁶e^{−0.1598·20} (3.1809·10⁻⁷ ≤ 3.1922·10⁻⁷, rechecked) and e^{−ℓ²/2} = e^{−2τ/ρ}. The latter absorption is what the error invalidates for ρ < 3/2. (8.50) itself holds by about 20 orders of magnitude, since good-sign values are about |Γ(s)|e^{−π|τ|/2}|ℓ|^{−σ}. When δ ≠ 0, one of the two terms in Cor 8.0.2's pair always falls in this case. (8.3) holds at δ = 0 and on the tested grid for ρ ≥ 1.

lean.note: Lean's rotation bound uses |δ| and is the same for both signs of δτ. In Cor 8.0.2's pair the good-sign term gets the bad-sign-sized bound, so neither (8.3) nor its (false) extra decay e^{−ℓ²/2} is ever needed.

erratum.description: False for small ρ = 4|τ|/ℓ²: for large ℓ it fails for every ρ < 0.8137, including the range |τ| ≥ 20 used by Cor 8.0.2. In the proof (book p. 158, mellintran.tex l.1186–1198) the L₃ piece {iy : y ≤ −x₀} is bounded by x₀^{−σ}e^{ℓ²/2−τπ/2}∫_{−∞}^{−x₀}e^{−(y−ℓ)²/2}dy. The text then uses ∫_{−∞}^{−ℓ}e^{−t²/2}dt ≤ √(π/2)e^{−ℓ²/2} ([AS64, 7.1.13]), which needs ℓ ≥ 0, but here ℓ < 0. The Gaussian peaks at y = ℓ inside the range whenever |ℓ| > x₀ (ρ < √80), so e^{ℓ²/2} is not cancelled. A valid version: |x₀|^{−σ}|Γ(s)|e^{(π/2)|τ|}((1+π/2^{5/2})e^{−ℓ²/2}e^{−(π/4)|τ|} + e^{−π|τ|}), with e^{−ℓ²/2} on the first term only. Separately, the proof's own I₁ and I₂ bounds give the coefficient 1 + π/2^{5/2], not the printed 1 + π/2^{3/2}; the printed one is larger, so that slip is safe. Book impact: (8.3) is used only in Cor 8.0.2's proof, to get (8.50), and (8.50) still holds by a wide margin.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: (8.3) fails at points with sgn(delta)=sgn(tau) and small rho (e.g. s=1+i, delta=1: |F|=0.01747 against 4.2e-8; s=1+20i, delta=2: 1.29e-28 against 1.18e-40), because the L_3 tail bound is applied with ell<0, while the corrected form holds on the grid.
check.note: (8.3) is false for small rho when sgn(delta)=sgn(tau): s=1+i, delta=1 gives |F|=0.017470 against 4.16e-8, and s=1+20i, delta=2 (rho=0.507, inside Cor 8.0.2's range) gives 1.29e-28 against 1.18e-40, because the L_3 step applies int_{-oo}^{-ell}e^{-t^2/2}dt<=sqrt(pi/2)e^{-ell^2/2} with ell<0. A valid form is |x0|^{-sigma}|Gamma(s)|e^{pi|tau|/2}((1+pi/2^{5/2})e^{-ell^2/2}e^{-pi|tau|/4}+e^{-pi|tau|}) (max ratio 0.498 on the grid); the claim survives.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: (8.3) fails at points with sgn(delta)=sgn(tau) and small rho (e.g. s=1+i, delta=1: |F|=0.01747 against 4.2e-8; s=1+20i, delta=2: 1.29e-28 against 1.18e-40), because the L_3 tail bound is applied with ell<0, while the corrected form holds on the grid.

items.changes_since_2013: Replaces 2013 (3.3) (label eq:pieses): for |τ| ≥ 2, |F_δ(s)| ≤ C′e^{−π|τ|/4}, with C′ ≤ (e^{π/2}|τ|^{σ/2}/2)(1+2π^{3/2}|δ|/√|τ|) for σ ∈ [0,1], or Γ(σ/2). That form has no e^{−ℓ²/2} factor. The book's new form adds |x₀|^{−σ}e^{−ℓ²/2}|Γ(s)| (the e^{−ℓ²/2} is what fails) and drops the condition |τ| ≥ 2.

items.label: eq:pastafrola
items.book_statement: Lower bounds for x₀ = Re u₀,₊ appearing in (8.3): |x₀| ≥ 0.51729√τ (printed 'for ρ arbitrary') and |x₀| ≥ 0.84473|τ|/|ℓ| for ρ ≤ 3/2.
items.note: Also needs |τ| for τ < 0 (see Theorem 8.0.1). For ρ < 3/2 the book uses the second case ((8.45)) instead. Not needed in Lean because the good-sign case (8.3) is not used.

erratum.description: The first case is false for ρ < 3/2: x₀ = (|ℓ|/2)√((j(ρ)−1)/2), j = √(1+ρ²), so x₀/√τ = √((j(ρ)−1)/(2ρ)) increases from 0 and reaches 0.51729 only at ρ = 3/2. The proof ((8.46)) derives it for ρ ≥ 3/2 and Cor 8.0.2 uses it only there; harmless, should read 'for ρ ≥ 3/2'.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: x0/sqrt(tau) = sqrt((j(rho)-1)/(2rho)) is 0.34356 at rho=0.5 and reaches 0.51729 only at rho=1.49997, so the first case of (8.4) holds only for rho>=3/2 (as proved in (8.46)); the second case is correct.
check.note: The first case of (8.4), |x0|>=0.51729 sqrt(tau) 'for rho arbitrary', is false for rho<1.49997, since x0/sqrt(tau)=sqrt((j(rho)-1)/(2rho)) increases (0.34356 at rho=0.5); it should read 'for rho>=3/2', which is what (8.46) proves and the only case Cor 8.0.2 uses. The second case is correct; the claim survives as a harmless misstatement.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: x0/sqrt(tau) = sqrt((j(rho)-1)/(2rho)) is 0.34356 at rho=0.5 and reaches 0.51729 only at rho=1.49997, so the first case of (8.4) holds only for rho>=3/2 (as proved in (8.46)); the second case is correct.

items.label: cor:amanita1
items.note: Lean covers the k = 2 shape for each term G_δ(w) with −1 ≤ Re w ≤ 1, which also serves the book's k = 1 use for η₊. k = 0 is not formalized; its only use is Lemma 9.2.1 → Prop 9.2.2 → Thm 7.1.1, which nothing later cites. Lean bounds each zero separately rather than the pair ρ, 1−ρ. Hypothesis masks of all four declarations are empty (pure analysis). NOTES.md's 'Cor 8.0.2 — DONE' omits the missing k = 0 form and the narrower ranges.

lean.note: Per term: G_δ(w) = F_δ(w+2) with −1 ≤ Re w ≤ 1, |Im w| ≥ 50 (book: 20) and |τ| ≥ (3/2)(πδ)², bounded by 0.892|τ|e^{−0.1598|τ|}. Applied to w = s and w = 1−s, the pair sum is 1.784|τ|, against κ_{2,1} = 5.13.

Per term, with the extra hypothesis |τ| ≥ 10π|δ| (y ≥ 10) and |τ| < (3/2)(πδ)²: bounded by 0.588y²e^{−0.1065y²}, y = |τ|/(π|δ|) = 2|τ|/|ℓ|. The pair gives 1.176y², against the book's κ_{2,0}/4 = 1.99.
Combines both regimes above T₀ ≥ max(10π|δ|, 50). Feeds zero_sum_bound, the counterpart of the book's k = 2 use in Lemma 9.3.1.
For η₊: the same k = 2-shaped bounds at w = s−1+2πiξ (Re w ∈ (−1,0)), at height T₀−200. They replace the book's k = 1 use with T₀−H, H = 200 (Lemma 9.4.1), with |τ| instead of √|τ|.

erratum.description: The statement survives, but the printed proof has three defects. (i) New: for ρ < 3/2 the good-sign member of the pair is bounded through (8.3) → (8.50), and (8.3) is false for small ρ (see Eq 8.3). (8.50) is still true by a wide margin, since good-sign values are about |Γ(s)|e^{−π|τ|/2}|ℓ|^{−σ}; the step can be repaired, e.g. by bounding |u|^{−σ} on L₃ by (|ℓ|/2)^{−σ} near the Gaussian peak, but it is not justified as printed. (ii) κ_{1,0} and κ_{2,0} use c₂ ≤ 3.15692 and 5.02186. Those values mix contour angles (see Eq 8.2) and need the y₀ ≥ ℓ repair. (iii) The proof's final display has κ_{k,1}|τ|^k where the derivation (|τ|^{(σ−1)/2} ≤ |τ|^{k/2}) and the statement give |τ|^{k/2}; this one is a typo.
