check.rerun: CONFIRMED: the statement of Cor 8.0.2 holds on the grid (max ratio 0.412), but at s = 1+20i, delta = 2 the cited (8.3) is false (|F| = 1.292e-28 > 1.182e-40) though (8.50) holds (1.46e-8), and one-contour c_2 values give kappa_{1,0} = 4.9582 > 4.903, kappa_{2,0} = 8.0071 > 7.96.

items.changes_since_2013: 2013 Cor 3.2: |τ| ≥ max(100, 4π²|δ|), one constant per k (c₀ = 4.226, c₁ = 3.516, c₂ = 3.262). Book: |τ| ≥ 20, with regime-dependent κ_{k,0} (3.001, 4.903, 7.96) and κ_{k,1} (3.286, 4.017, 5.13). Exponents, the threshold (3/2)(πδ)² and the shape are unchanged (2π|δ| is written |ℓ|).

items.label: eq:madejap
items.book_statement: Writes the Mellin transform of a twisted smoothing, ∫₀^∞ e(δt)η(t)t^s dt/t, whose stationary-phase analysis in §8.1 motivates the Gaussian; the left side is misprinted as F_δ(t).
items.note: Mathlib's mellin f s = ∫ t in Ioi 0, t^(s−1) • f t has the book's normalization (dt/t, t^s). Lean never defines F_δ for the plain Gaussian e^{−t²/2}; it works with G_δ = F_δ(·+2) and with mellin (fP δ).

lean.note: t²e^{−t²/2}e(δt), the twisted smoothing for η = t²e^{−t²/2}.
Mathlib's mellin (fδ δ) s = Gr s δ 0 = ∫₀^∞ t^{s+1}e^{−t²/2}e(δt) dt, i.e. (8.5) for η = t²e^{−t²/2}; this is the book's F_δ(s+2) (Gr_zero_eq).
η₊(t)e(δt); its Mellin transform mellin (fP δ) is (8.5) for η = η₊.

erratum.description: The left side F_δ(t) should be F_δ(s): t is the integration variable and s the free variable (compare (8.8), F_δ(s) = ∫ e^{−t²/2}e(δt)t^s dt/t).

items.label: eq:rateda
items.book_statement: Heuristic: at the stationary point t = −τ/(2πδ) of the phase 2πδt + τ log t (meaningful when sgn τ ≠ sgn δ), the integrand η(t)e(δt)t^{s−1} equals η(−τ/2πδ)e^{−iτ}(−τ/2πδ)^{σ+iτ−1}.
items.note: Motivational stationary-phase computation in §8.1; the Lean proof needs no motivation for the choice of smoothing. Checked: e(δt₀) = e^{−iτ} at t₀ = −τ/(2πδ). The following width display writes (2πiδt + τ log t)″ with a stray i; the value 2π|δ|/√|τ| is unaffected.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(8.6)', stationary/saddle, 'eta (-τ', index docs; Explicit/MellinRotate.lean, GMellin.lean

items.label: eq:maloko
items.book_statement: Modulus of (8.6): η(−τ/2πδ)·|τ/2πδ|^{σ−1}. So fast decay of F_δ(σ+iτ) in |τ| requires fast decay of η at infinity, and decay of F₀ handles small δ.
items.note: (8.7) itself is correct. The following discussion (η = e^{−t}: decay e^{−t/2π|δ|}, e^{−8} = 0.00033 at height 50|δ|) checks out.

erratum.description: The sentence interpreting (8.7) says fast decay of F_δ(σ+iτ) as |τ| → ∞ 'amounts to asking that η(t) decay rapidly as t → 0'. Since the stationary point t₀ = |τ|/(2π|δ|) tends to ∞, it should say t → ∞, as the book's own list item 1 does.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(8.7)', stationary/saddle, decay-of-η heuristics; Explicit/MellinRotate.lean, GMellin.lean

items.label: eq:ivsnow
items.book_statement: Defines F_δ(s) = ∫₀^∞ e^{−t²/2} e(δt) t^{s−1} dt (δ real): the Mellin transform of the Gaussian twisted by an additive character, the function Chapter 8 bounds and Chapter 9 feeds into explicit formulas.
items.note: Match is up to the index shift s ↦ s+2: Lean defines only the k = 2 transform (η = t²e^{−t²/2}); the η₊ case reuses it as Gr(s−1+2πiξ) δ 0 = F_δ(s+1+2πiξ) (EtaPlusMellin.mellin_fP_eq), as in the book's §9.4. No k = 0 transform (Thm 7.1.1's smoothing) and no meromorphic continuation are formalized; Gr is a Lebesgue integral. Lean's Fhalf (doc 'F_δ(u)') is an unrelated log-coordinate function.

lean.note: Gr s δ θ = ∫_{(0,∞)} Jr s δ θ r dr (ray rotated by θ). At θ = 0 it is ∫ t^{s+1}e^{−t²/2}e(δt)dt = F_δ(s+2), the book's §9.3 G_δ; F_δ(s) = Gr (s−2) δ 0 for ℜs > 0.
Gr s δ 0 = ∫_{Ioi 0} t^{s−1}·(t²e^{−t²/2})·e^{2πiδt} dt, i.e. (8.8) with s replaced by s+2.
Mathlib mellin (fδ δ) s = Gr s δ 0, where fδ δ t = t²e^{−t²/2}e(δt) (GMellin.lean:18).

items.changes_since_2013: identical formula; an unnumbered display in MA13 (1305.2897v4) §3.2

items.label: eq:mosot
items.book_statement: Identifies F_δ with a parabolic cylinder function: F_δ(s) = e^{−π²δ²}Γ(s)U(s−½, −2πiδ), by matching (8.8) with the half-line integral defining U(a,z) for ℜa > −½; the second argument is purely imaginary.
items.note: Its second use, the remark after Cor 8.0.2 that Thm 8.0.1 gives explicit bounds for U(a,z) with z imaginary, is not formalized either (not needed for the main theorem).

lean.note: Lean never passes to U(a,z) or factors out Γ(s): it deforms the original t-ray, Gr s δ θ = Gr s δ 0 for |θ| < π/4, ℜs > −2, then bounds the rotated integral directly.

items.label: eq:hustadom
items.book_statement: Quotes the vertical-line integral for the parabolic cylinder function (DLMF 12.5.6, suggested by Temme): U(a,z) = e^{z²/4}(i√(2π))^{−1}∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞} e^{−zu+u²/2}u^{−a−½}du, any c > 0.
items.note: The book adopts this representation following a suggestion of N. Temme. The Lean route deforms the original t-contour inside |arg t| < π/4. That is closer to the 2013 MA13 setup, which also allowed shifting the contour within arg(u) ∈ (−π/4, π/4).

lean.note: No contour representation of U is used. The contour deformation is done on the t-integral itself, by the rotation t = re^{iθ}: Gr s δ θ = Gr s δ 0 for |θ| < π/4, ℜs > −2.
Mechanism of the deformation: ∂_θJr = Dr = i∂_r(r·Jr) (hasDerivAt_Jr_theta, hasDerivAt_Pr_r) and ∫₀^∞ Dr dr = 0, so Gr is constant in θ (hasDerivAt_Gr).

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (new in the book; MA13 applied the saddle-point method directly to (8.8))

items.label: eq:melis
items.book_statement: Combining (8.9) and (8.10): F_δ(s) = e^{−2π²δ²}Γ(s)(i√(2π))^{−1}∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞} e^{2πiδu+u²/2}u^{−s}du, the representation whose integral the book's saddle-point analysis estimates.
items.note: Constant check: e^{(πiδ)²}·e^{z²/4} with z = −2πiδ gives e^{−2π²δ²}; −zu = 2πiδu; u^{−a−½} = u^{−s}.

lean.note: The role of this formula (an integral representation suited to contour deformation) is filled by rotating the t-ray: Gr s δ θ = Gr s δ 0 for |θ| < π/4, ℜs > −2.
‖G_δ(s)‖ ≤ e^{−|θ||τ|}∫₀^∞ r^{σ+1}e^{−cos(2θ)r²/2 + 2π|δ||sin θ|r}dr for |θ| < π/4, σ > −2, θτ ≥ 0. There is no Γ(s) prefactor and no u^{−s} integral.

items.label: eq:fribar
items.book_statement: Defines the phase φ(u) = −u²/2 − 2πiδu + iτ log u (s = σ+iτ), so that the integrand of (8.11) is e^{−φ(u)}u^{−σ}.
items.note: The book's ℓ = −2πδ and ρ = 4τ/ℓ² have Lean counterparts only implicitly: Lean writes π|δ| and (πδ)² = ℓ²/4.

lean.note: Lean has no phase function. Jr = r^{s+1}e^{iθ(s+2)}exp(−r²e^{2iθ}/2 + 2πiδre^{iθ}) is the original t-integrand on the ray t = re^{iθ}; its modulus (norm_Jr) is bounded directly.

items.changes_since_2013: MA13 (3.9) had φ(u) = u²/2 − 2πiδu − iτ log u for the t-integral (8.8); signs of the u²/2 and iτ log u terms flipped since φ now serves (8.11)

items.label: eq:drogon
items.book_statement: Names I(s) = ∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞} e^{−φ(u)}u^{−σ}du, which equals the integral in (8.11); bounding I(s) through the saddle point is the task of the following sections.

lean.note: Lean's analogue is the rotated integral Gr s δ θ = ∫₀^∞ Jr dr, equal to G_δ(s) by Gr_eq; it is bounded by norm_Gr_le / norm_Gr_le_closed, not along a saddle-point contour.

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (MA13 instead wrote F_δ(s) = ∫₀^∞ e^{−φ(u)}u^{σ}du/u, unnumbered)

items.label: eq:arbre
items.book_statement: Saddle-point equation φ'(u) = 0, i.e. −u − 2πiδ + iτ/u = 0, equivalently u² − iℓu − iτ = 0 with ℓ = −2πδ.

lean.note: No saddle point: for |τ| ≥ (3/2)(πδ)² (ρ ≥ 3/2), |τ| ≥ 50, Lean fixes the rotation angle θ = 0.28, giving ‖G_δ(s)‖ ≤ 0.892|τ|e^{−0.1598|τ|}.

items.changes_since_2013: MA13 (3.10): u − 2πiδ − iτ/u = 0, i.e. u² + iℓu − iτ = 0 (for its φ); sign of the iℓu term flipped

items.label: eq:rooto
items.book_statement: Solves the quadratic (8.14): the two saddle points are u₀ = (iℓ ± √(−ℓ² + 4iτ))/2.

lean.note: Lean never locates a saddle point: for any fixed angle 0 ≤ θ < π/4 (sign matched to τ) it bounds ‖G_δ(s)‖ in closed form by completing the square in r, for −1 ≤ ℜs ≤ 1.

items.changes_since_2013: MA13 (3.11): u₀ = (−iℓ ± √(−ℓ²+4iτ))/2; sign of iℓ flipped

items.label: eq:direwolf
items.book_statement: Value of the phase at a saddle point, simplified with u₀² = iℓu₀ + iτ: φ(u₀) = (iℓ/2)u₀ + iτ log(u₀/√e); its real part yields the main exponential decay factor.

lean.note: The exponential factor is instead e^{−θ|τ|}·e^{(2π|δ|sin θ)²/(2cos 2θ)} from the completed square, with θ then fixed per regime; no φ(u₀), E(ρ) or υ(ρ) is ever evaluated.
∫₀^∞ r^p e^{−cr²/2+br}dr ≤ e^{b²/2c}((1+(b/c)²)√(2π/c) + √π/(c√(c/2))) for 0 ≤ p ≤ 2: the Gaussian-integral step used in place of a saddle-point evaluation.

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (new; MA13 evaluated |u_{0,+}^s e^{y/2}| with y = ℜ(−iℓu₀) instead)

items.label: eq:polan
items.book_statement: Second derivative at a saddle point: φ''(u₀) = −(u₀² + iτ)/u₀² = −(iℓu₀ + 2iτ)/u₀²; used next to find the direction of steepest descent.

lean.note: No steepest-descent direction or 1/√|φ''| width: the polynomial prefactor (0.892|τ| here, 0.588y² in norm_G_le_regimeA) comes from the Gaussian moment bound integral_rpow_exp_quad_le after a fixed rotation.

items.changes_since_2013: MA13 (3.12): φ''(u₀) = (u₀² + iτ)/u₀² = (−iℓu₀ + 2iτ)/u₀²; overall sign and sign of iℓ flipped

items.label: eq:picpio
items.book_statement: Explicit form of the right-half-plane saddle point: u_{0,+} = (iℓ + |ℓ|√(−1+4iτ/ℓ²))/2 = (ℓ/2)(i ± √(−1+(4τ/ℓ²)i)), sign = sgn ℓ (principal root); for ℓ = 0, u_{0,+} = e^{iπ/4}√τ.

lean.note: Lean keeps only the book's regime split at ρ = 4|τ|/ℓ² = 3/2, i.e. |τ| = (3/2)(πδ)²; no coordinates of u_{0,+} (no j(ρ), υ(ρ)); bounds use |δ| only, uniform in sgn δ·sgn τ.

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (new; MA13 first assumed ℓ ≥ 0, calling ℓ < 0 easier)

items.label: eq:petpan
items.book_statement: Real part of the phase at the saddle point: Re φ(u_{0,+}) = −(ℓ/2)·Im u_{0,+} − τ·arg u_{0,+}, read off from (8.16); it fixes the size e^{−Re φ} of the integrand of (8.13) there.
items.note: Step of the saddle-point proof of Thm 8.0.1, used in (8.31) (ℓ>0) and after (8.47) (ℓ<0). Checked: it is exactly the real part of (8.16) (20,000 random (ℓ,τ), relative error ≤ 4·10⁻¹³). Lean never forms Temme's integral (8.10)–(8.13). Explicit/MellinRotate rotates the ray of the Mellin transform of t²e^{−t²/2}e(δt) instead, and the peak exponent −θ|τ| + b²/(2c) plays the role of the saddle-point value.

lean.note: Modulus on the rotated ray t = re^{iθ}: r^{σ+1}·exp(−θτ − r²cos2θ/2 − 2πδr·sinθ). This is the exponent of the original Mellin integral (8.8), not of Temme's integral (8.13).
Completing the square at r₀ = b/c (line 457), b = 2π|δ|sinθ, c = cos2θ, gives the peak factor e^{b²/(2c)}; with e^{−θ|τ|} it plays the role of e^{−Re φ(u_{0,+})}.
|G_δ(s)| ≤ e^{−θ|τ|}·e^{b²/(2c)}·(explicit prefactor) for every θ ∈ [0, π/4) and −1 ≤ σ ≤ 1; k = 2 only (G_δ(s) = F_δ(s+2)); uses none of the five hypotheses.

items.changes_since_2013: Changed: 1305.2897v4 (3.13) wrote |u_{0,+}^s e^{y/2}| = |u_{0,+}|^σ e^{−τ·arg u_{0,+}} e^{y/2} for the direct saddle point of (8.8), ℓ ≥ 0 only; the book recasts it as Re φ(u_{0,+}) for Temme's phase (8.12), either sign of ℓ.

items.label: eq:masha
items.book_statement: Closed form of a principal square root: √(−1 + iρ) = √((j−1)/2) + i√((j+1)/2), where ρ = 4τ/ℓ² and j(ρ) = √(1+ρ²); found by solving a quadratic for the real and imaginary parts.
items.note: Correct: with a = √((j−1)/2) ≥ 0 and b = √((j+1)/2), a² − b² = −1 and 2ab = √(j²−1) = ρ, so a + ib is the principal root (numerical error ≤ 2·10⁻¹⁰). Needs τ ≥ 0, which the book assumes. Only used to get (8.21). The notation ρ, j is not in Lean; Lean's regime split 3/2·(πδ)² ≤ |τ| is ρ ≥ 3/2, since ρ = τ/(πδ)².

lean.note: The only critical point Lean uses is the real r₀ = b/c = 2π|δ|sinθ/cos2θ of the radial exponent (line 422). No saddle point and no complex square root are computed.

items.label: eq:damherr
items.book_statement: Rectangular coordinates of the saddle point: Re u_{0,+} = ±(ℓ/2)√((j−1)/2) and Im u_{0,+} = (ℓ/2)(1 ± √((j+1)/2)), with sign + for ℓ>0 and − for ℓ<0.
items.note: Re-verified for both signs of ℓ (relative error ≤ 2·10⁻¹⁰ over 40,000 random (ℓ, ρ)). x₀ and y₀ fix the contours of §8.4. They enter (8.31), (8.39), the I₂/I₃ estimates and the ℓ<0 lower bounds (8.45)–(8.46) on x₀. Lean's contour is a ray from 0 at angle θ (Gr_eq), so no saddle-point coordinates enter.

lean.note: Rotating the ray (|θ| < π/4, σ > −2) leaves G_δ(s) unchanged. This replaces shifting the contour of (8.13) onto lines through x₀ = Re u_{0,+}, y₀ = Im u_{0,+}.
The radial peak r₀ = b/c (line 422) is the only point Lean locates; no saddle-point coordinates are needed.

erratum.description: The parenthetical after (8.21) says Re u_{0,+} and Im u_{0,+} are always positive except when τ = ℓ = 0. The real exceptional set is τ = 0: there Re u_{0,+} = 0 for every ℓ, and u_{0,+} = 0 for ℓ ≤ 0. This is harmless. The text assumes τ > 0 and ℓ ≠ 0, where positivity holds, and §8.4.1 itself writes x₀ = Re u_{0,+} ≥ 0.

items.changes_since_2013: No labelled counterpart. 1305.2897v4 (ℓ ≥ 0, saddle point of (8.8)) never shows Re and Im of u_{0,+} as separate formulas. They appear only implicitly, as (ℓ/2)(√((j−1)/2) + i(√((j+1)/2) − 1)), inside (3.16) and the first line of (3.20). It also has y = Re(−iℓu₀) = (ℓ²/2)(υ−1) after (3.15). That is the book's ℓ<0 case with ℓ → −ℓ. The ℓ>0 formulas and the positivity remark are new.

items.label: eq:dada
items.book_statement: Modulus of the saddle point: expanding the square of (8.21) gives |u_{0,+}| = (|ℓ|/2)√(1 + j ± 2υ) = (|ℓ|/√2)√(υ² ± υ), with υ(ρ) = √((1+j)/2).
items.note: Each line checked (relative error ≤ 3·10⁻⁸). Used only in (8.36), |u_{0,+}| ≥ max(√τ, ℓ), which bounds |u_{0,+}|^{−σ} on the vertical ray and x₁ for I₃. Lean has no such factor. Its prefactors, linear in |τ| or y², match the |τ|^{k/2} growth of Cor 8.0.2 for k = 2.

lean.note: The power r^{σ+1} is bounded by 1 + r² (line 452; needs 0 ≤ σ+1 ≤ 2) instead of a |u_{0,+}|^{−σ} factor via (8.36). This yields the σ-uniform prefactors 0.892|τ| and 0.588y² of the two regimes.

items.changes_since_2013: Changed: 1305.2897v4 (3.20) gave (ℓ/√2)√(υ²−υ) for its saddle point (ℓ ≥ 0); the book has (|ℓ|/√2)√(υ²±υ). The 2013 formula is the book's ℓ<0 case, since the 2013 saddle point is the book's with ℓ → −ℓ.

items.label: eq:niels
items.book_statement: Derivation of the saddle point's argument: arg u_{0,+} is written as an arcsin of Im/|·| and, via cos(π−2θ) = 2sin²θ − 1, simplified to π/2 − ½·arccos(±√(2/(1+j))).
items.note: All steps verified. Taking arcsin(Im/|·|) is legitimate because Re ≥ 0; the half-angle identity is used with θ ∈ [0, π/2]. Intermediate to (8.24). In Lean the decay rate θ is the rotation angle, fixed explicitly, not computed from a saddle point.

lean.note: Decay e^{−θ|τ|} with the fixed angle θ = 0.28 (line 537) for |τ| ≥ max(50, (3/2)(πδ)²), i.e. ρ ≥ 3/2. No arg u_{0,+} is involved.
θ = 0.1866|τ|/(πδ)² (line 601) for 10π|δ| ≤ |τ| < (3/2)(πδ)²; the angle is chosen by hand, not from a saddle point.

items.changes_since_2013: No labelled counterpart. It extends the derivation in 1305.2897v4 (3.16), which covers ℓ ≥ 0 only and ends in ½arccos√(2/(1+j)), to both signs via ±.

items.label: eq:phal
items.book_statement: Argument of the saddle point by cases: ½·arccos(−1/υ) if ℓ>0 (lies in (π/4, π/2]) and ½·arccos(1/υ) if ℓ<0 (lies in [0, π/4)); hence arg u_{0,+} ∈ [0, π/2].
items.note: Verified, including the ranges. Used in (8.31) and for β ≤ arg(u_{0,+})/2: arg u_{0,+} ≥ 1.28842 for ρ ≤ 3/2 (recomputed 1.288434 at ρ = 3/2, υ = 1.183802). Also used after (8.47) to get −Re φ(u_{0,+}) ≤ πτ/4. Lean has no counterpart of arg u_{0,+}.

lean.note: Fixed rotation angle θ = 0.28 (line 537) gives the decay e^{−0.28|τ|}, which becomes e^{−0.1598|τ|} after the b²/(2c) loss, when ρ ≥ 3/2.
Angle θ = 0.1866|τ|/(πδ)² ≤ 0.28 (line 601) when ρ < 3/2. It replaces the role of arg u_{0,+} in the exponent.

items.changes_since_2013: Changed: 1305.2897v4 (3.16) had the single value ½arccos(1/υ) (ℓ ≥ 0, direct saddle point), which is now the ℓ<0 case; the ℓ>0 case ½arccos(−1/υ) is new.

items.label: eq:jomo
items.book_statement: Algebraic simplification used for the steepest-descent direction: rationalizing the denominator turns (ρ ± √((j−1)/2))/(1 ± √((j+1)/2)) into 2υ(−υ ± j)/ρ.
items.note: Each step of the chain agrees to 10⁻⁵⁵ (80-digit arithmetic, both signs, ρ from 10⁻⁶ to 10⁶). It only feeds the steepest-descent direction (8.26)–(8.27), which the book calls advisory for choosing contours; no bound depends on it. Lean's contour is a ray from 0 at angle θ < π/4 (TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.Gr_eq) and needs no steepest-descent analysis.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(8.25)', υ/upsilon, steepest/Temme/saddle over all .lean; Explicit/MellinRotate.lean

items.changes_since_2013: Changed: 1305.2897v4 (3.23) is the same algebra for (ρ − √((j−1)/2))/(−1 + √((j+1)/2)) = 2υ(υ+j)/ρ; the book generalizes the signs to ±.

items.label: eq:heraus
items.book_statement: Direction w of steepest descent at u_{0,+} (w²φ''(u_{0,+}) > 0, defined mod π): arg w = arg u_{0,+} + ½·arctan(2υ(−υ ± j)/ρ), plus π/2 when ℓ<0.
items.note: Verified mod π against −arg φ''(u_{0,+})/2 computed directly (error ≤ 4·10⁻¹⁰). Also checked: the preceding claims Re(ℓu_{0,+} + 2τ) > 0 and sgn ϖ = sgn ℓ. The case 'ℓ ≥ 0' formally includes ℓ = 0, where ρ is undefined. There φ''(u₀) = −2 gives arg w = π/2, the limit as ρ → ∞. Advisory only; neither the book's bounds nor Lean need it.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(8.26)', arctan with υ, steepest/saddle, 'arg' direction over all .lean; Explicit/MellinRotate.lean

items.changes_since_2013: Changed: 1305.2897v4 (3.24) had arg v = arg u_{0,+} − ½arctan(2υ(υ+j)/ρ) (ℓ ≥ 0, printed with v for υ). The book adds the ± cases and the π/2 shift for ℓ<0, and calls the direction w.

items.label: eq:rugros
items.book_statement: Closed form of the steepest-descent direction, from (8.24) and arccos(1/υ) = arctan√((j−1)/2): arg w = π/2 + ½(arctan√((j−1)/2) − arctan(2υ(j+υ)/ρ)) for ℓ<0, and π/2 + ½(arctan(2υ(j−υ)/ρ) − arctan√((j−1)/2)) for ℓ≥0.
items.note: Verified mod π (error ≤ 4·10⁻¹⁰); w²φ''(u_{0,+}) > 0 checked for w = e^{i·arg w}. This is the function plotted in Figures 8.1–8.2. Advisory only: the §8.4 contours are justified by (8.33)–(8.34) and direct estimates, not by this formula. Lean uses no steepest-descent direction.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(8.27)', arctan, steepest/saddle over all .lean; Explicit/MellinRotate.lean

items.changes_since_2013: No counterpart. 1305.2897v4 instead wrote arg v = arg u_{0,+} − arctan Υ ((3.24)–(3.26)) and proved arg v < 0 ((3.29)).

items.label: fig:argwminus
items.book_statement: Plot of arg w − π/2 against ρ ∈ (0, 10] for ℓ<0: it rises from −π/4 as ρ → 0⁺ toward 0 (about −0.135 at ρ = 10), so steepest descent is far from vertical for small ρ.
items.note: Reproduced from (8.27): −0.7854 at ρ = 10⁻⁴, −0.4823 at ρ = 1 and −0.1348 at ρ = 10, matching the plotted curve (argwminus.png). Not formalized and not needed. Lean's bound discards the sign of δτ (TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.norm_Gr_le uses |δ||sinθ|), so the ℓ<0 case gets no separate treatment.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: 'Figure 8.1', argwminus, steepest direction, ℓ<0 case over all .lean; Explicit/MellinRotate.lean

items.label: fig:argwplus
items.book_statement: Plot of arg w − π/2 against ρ ∈ (0, 10] for ℓ≥0: it starts at 0, peaks near 0.112 around ρ ≈ 2.5 and is about 0.085 at ρ = 10, so steepest descent is nearly vertical.
items.note: Reproduced from (8.27): 0 as ρ → 0⁺, a maximum of 0.11165 at ρ ≈ 2.54 and 0.0849 at ρ = 10, matching argwplus.png. So for ℓ ≥ 0 steepest descent stays within 6.4° of vertical, which §8.4.1 cites to motivate the vertical contour. Not formalized and not needed.

erratum.description: §8.4.1 cites this figure as '(see (8.2))', which reads as a reference to equation (8.2), the definitions of E(ρ), c_{1,σ,τ} and c_{2,σ,τ}. It should read 'see Figure 8.2'. Harmless.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: 'Figure 8.2', argwplus, steepest direction over all .lean; Explicit/MellinRotate.lean

items.label: eq:morb
items.book_statement: Imaginary part of the phase φ of the Temme integrand at u = x+iy: Im φ(u) = −xy + ℓx + τ log|u|. A constant-phase contour through u_{0,+} would be a level curve of it; the book drops that idea as unwieldy.
items.note: Pure motivation: the only reference to (8.28) is the next sentence (l.730). §8.4 then uses simple piecewise contours instead: two vertical rays joined by a slanted segment in §8.4.1, and a vertical ray, a quarter-circle and a vertical ray in §8.4.2. Lean has neither the phase φ nor Temme's representation (8.10)–(8.11). Explicit/MellinRotate.lean bounds the original Mellin integral on a rotated ray t = re^{iθ}; re_exponent computes only the real part of the rotated exponent, so no level-curve analysis arises. Checked against Im φ from (8.12): relative error ≤ 1.8e-15 at 2·10⁴ random points.

erratum.description: After (8.28) the book fixes the level c = Im φ(u_{0,+}) for the constant-phase curve through the saddle, then calls it 'the curve Im(φ(u)) = 0 given by (8.28)'. The level should be Im φ(u_{0,+}), which is generally nonzero. Harmless, since the curve is dropped right away.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(8.28)', 'Im φ', level curve, Temme phase over all .lean; Explicit/MellinRotate.lean (re_exponent only)

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (1305.2897v4 §3 has only a commented-out constant-phase remark, for its direct-integral phase)

items.label: eq:destined
items.book_statement: For ℓ > 0 the contour is L = L₁ ∪ L₂ ∪ L₃: a vertical ray above u_{0,+}, a slanted segment from u_{0,+} down to (x₁,0), and a vertical ray below x₁. I_j integrates |e^{−φ(u)}u^{−σ}| over L_j, so |I| ≤ I₁+I₂+I₃.
items.note: A device of the book's Temme-integral route for sgn ℓ = sgn τ. §8.4.2 defines the I_j the same way for ℓ < 0. Lean's one-ray bound is uniform in sgn δ (it uses −2πδ r sinθ ≤ 2π|δ||sinθ|r), so Thm 8.0.1's case split disappears. Thm 8.0.1 itself is never stated in Lean.

lean.note: A single contour: the ray t = re^{iθ} in the original Mellin integral of t²e^{−t²/2}e(δt). Gr s δ 0 = F_δ(s+2) (Gr_zero_eq, mellin_fδ). No splitting into pieces and no Temme integral.
Formal contour shift: Gr s δ θ = Gr s δ 0 for |θ| < π/4 and Re s > −2, via ∂_θJr = i∂_r(r·Jr) and integral_Dr_eq_zero. The book's 'shifting the contour' is informal.
‖∫‖ ≤ ∫‖·‖ on the rotated ray (line 371), the analogue of |I| ≤ ΣI_j. The rotation direction is chosen so that θ·Im s ≥ 0.

erratum.description: Just before (8.29), the vertical contour is motivated by 'the direction of steepest descent is never far from vertical (see (8.2))'. The source is \ref{fig:argwplus}, i.e. Figure 8.2 (arg w − π/2 for ℓ ≥ 0), wrapped in equation parentheses. Eq. (8.2) defines E(ρ), c_{1,σ,τ} and c_{2,σ,τ} and says nothing about directions. The remark itself is right: computed arg w − π/2 ∈ [0, 0.112] for ℓ > 0.

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (new. 1305.2897v4 §3.6 bounded the direct integral (8.8) on a limaçon-of-Pascal contour C₁∪C₂∪C₃)

items.label: eq:bankal
items.book_statement: Real part of the phase at u = x+iy: Re φ(x+iy) = (y²−x²)/2 − ℓy − τ arg(x+iy). It gives the modulus e^{−Re φ} of the integrand along each contour piece.
items.note: Exact: checked against Re φ from (8.12) at 2000 random points, with no discrepancy. Reused for (8.31), (8.34), the L₃ estimate and §8.4.2. The Lean counterpart computes the integrand's modulus on the rotated ray instead of on vertical lines.

lean.note: Exact modulus of the rotated integrand: ‖Jr‖ = r^{Re s+1}·exp(−θ·Im s − r²cos2θ/2 − 2πδ r sinθ). On a ray the arg contribution is the constant −θ·Im s.
Re(−r²e^{2iθ}/2 + 2πiδ r e^{iθ}) = −r²cos2θ/2 − 2πδ r sinθ. This is Lean's counterpart of computing the real part of the exponent.

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (the 2013 analogue, 1305.2897v4 (3.37): Re φ = (x²−y²)/2 − ℓy + θτ, is for the direct-integral phase u²/2 + iℓu − iτ log u)

items.label: eq:borgnin
items.book_statement: Real phase at the saddle (ℓ > 0): Re φ(u_{0,+}) = −(ℓ/2)y₀ − τ arg u_{0,+} = −(ℓ²/4)(1+υ(ρ)) − (τ/2)arccos(−1/υ(ρ)) = −[(1+υ)/ρ + ½arccos(−1/υ)]τ. With e^{−2π²δ²} from (8.11) it yields e^{πτ/2}e^{−E(ρ)τ} in (8.1).
items.note: All three forms match Re φ(u_{0,+}) computed from (8.15) (relative error ≤ 7e-16, 2·10⁴ random (ℓ,τ), ℓ > 0). With (8.40), −Re φ(u_{0,+}) = (π/2 − E(ρ) + 2/ρ)τ; the book's unnumbered display after (8.40) (l.962–964) drops this factor τ. The factor e^{−2π²δ²} = e^{−(2/ρ)τ} from (8.11) then leaves e^{(π/2−E(ρ))τ} in (8.41). Lean has no Temme saddle. Its general rotated-ray bound norm_Gr_le_closed reaches the same sharp exponent at θ* = ½arccos(1/υ(ρ)), the argument of the 2013 direct-integral saddle (1305.2897v4 (3.16)). Checked at 2·10⁴ random (δ,τ): relative difference ≤ 1e-8. The theorems actually used fix θ = 0.28 (regime B) or θ = 0.1866ρ (regime A). They get Cor 8.0.2's exponents 0.1598|τ| (E(3/2) = 0.15983) and 0.1065y² (y² = ρ|τ|; E(ρ)|τ| ~ y²/8 as ρ → 0), not E(ρ) itself (E(10) = 0.4306, E → π/4).

lean.note: No saddle point. The main factor is exp(−θ|τ| + (2π|δ|sinθ)²/(2cos2θ)), from completing the square, for any 0 ≤ θ < π/4 and −1 ≤ Re s ≤ 1. With ρ = |τ|/(πδ)² the exponent is −|τ|(θ − (2/ρ)sin²θ/cos2θ). Its minimum over θ is at θ* = ½arccos(1/υ(ρ)) (cos2θ* = 1/υ), where it equals −E(ρ)|τ| exactly, the sharp exponent of (8.1)/(8.41). No Lean theorem instantiates θ*.
θ = 0.28 with π²δ² ≤ (2/3)|τ| gives the exponent −0.28|τ| + 0.120192|τ| ≤ −0.1598|τ| (lines 537–549). That is Cor 8.0.2's exponent, not the sharp E(ρ).

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (the Temme-integral phase is new in the book; the 2013 direct-integral analogue, 1305.2897v4 (3.17), evaluates the saddle exponent −arg(u_{0,+})τ + y/2 = −E(ρ)τ, the same final exponent)

items.label: eq:kaylor
items.book_statement: Taylor's formula with a double-integral remainder for f ∈ C²: f(t) = f(t₀) + f′(t₀)(t−t₀) + ∫_{t₀}^t∫_{t₀}^r f″(s) ds dr. It is used to compare arctan with its tangent line.
items.note: A standard identity; its only use is the derivation of (8.33) that follows it directly (eq:kaylor is never \ref'd). The Lean route never expands arg u or arctan: on the rotated ray arg t ≡ θ exactly (norm_Jr), so no Taylor-remainder argument for the arg term is needed. The only Taylor-type estimates in MellinRotate are Mathlib's Real.sin_bound for sin 0.28 (sin_028_le) and for sin θ (norm_G_le_regimeA). They play no role analogous to (8.32).

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(8.32)', Taylor/taylor, iteratedDeriv, double-integral remainder over all .lean (only taylor6 numerics, Real.sin_bound uses)

items.label: eq:ardan
items.book_statement: Tangent-line bound for arctan: for t₀ ≥ 0 and t ≥ −t₀, arctan t ≤ arctan t₀ + arctan′(t₀)(t−t₀), because arctan″ is odd and negative on (0,∞). This lets the quadratic part of the arg term be dropped.
items.note: Correct as stated. By (8.32), the remainder is ≤ 0 for t ≥ 0 (concavity on [0,∞)). For −t₀ ≤ t < 0 it equals ∫_t^{t₀}∫_r^{t₀}arctan″, which is ≤ 0 by oddness. No violation in 2·10⁵ random (t₀,t). Used for (8.34), (8.37) and in §8.4.2.

lean.note: The role of (8.33), controlling −τ·arg u along the contour, disappears. On the ray t = re^{iθ}, |t^{s+1}| = r^{Re s+1}e^{−θ·Im s} exactly, so no concavity bound is needed.

items.label: eq:apprec
items.book_statement: On the vertical line Re u = x₀: Re φ(x₀+iy) ≥ Re φ(u_{0,+}) + (y−y₀)²/2 for y ≥ −y₀. The linear term vanishes at the saddle, and (8.33) bounds the arg term.
items.note: Checked numerically for y ≥ −y₀: no violation in 10⁵ random (ℓ,τ,y). Reused in §8.4.2, where the book says it holds for all ℓ. The Lean majorant is an exact completed square plus one sign estimate, so no range condition like y ≥ −y₀ arises.

lean.note: Gaussian majorant by completing the square: −(c/2)r² + br = b²/(2c) − (c/2)(r − b/c)² (line 457), with c = cos2θ and b = 2π|δ|sinθ. The centre b/c plays the saddle's role.
Pointwise exponent bound on the ray (lines 376–383): −θ·Im s = −|θ||Im s| and −2πδ r sinθ ≤ 2π|δ||sinθ|r. This makes the bound independent of sgn δ.

items.label: eq:chnehr
items.book_statement: So the integral of e^{−Re φ} up the ray L₁ is at most √(π/2)·e^{−Re φ(u_{0,+})}, giving I₁ ≤ |u_{0,+}|^{−σ}√(π/2)e^{−Re φ(u_{0,+})}.

lean.note: Bounds the whole ray integral, for 0 ≤ p ≤ 2: ∫₀^∞ r^p e^{−cr²/2+br}dr ≤ e^{b²/2c}((1+(b/c)²)√(2π/c) + √π/(c√(c/2))). It uses full-line Gaussian moments (lines 439–444).
Second Gaussian moment ∫u²e^{−cu²/2}du = √π/(c√(c/2)), used together with Mathlib's integral_gaussian.

items.label: eq:blondie
items.book_statement: Lower bound for the saddle's modulus when ℓ > 0: |u_{0,+}| = (ℓ/√2)√(υ²+υ) ≥ max(√τ, ℓ). It bounds |u|^{−σ} on L₁ and gives x₁ ≥ tanβ·max(√τ, ℓ) for L₃.
items.note: The equality is (8.22) with the + sign. The bound uses υ ≥ 1 (so υ²+υ ≥ 2) and υ² ≥ (1+ρ)/2 > ρ/2, then ℓ√ρ/2 = √τ. Both checked numerically: 2000 random (ℓ,τ), no violation. The τ^{−σ/2} and ℓ^{−σ} factors of (8.1) come from here.

lean.note: Lean needs no lower bound on |u|. The power r^{Re s+1} has exponent in [0,2] and is bounded above by 1 + r² (line 452).
The resulting polynomial prefactor is ≤ 0.892|τ| (line 566); regime A gives 0.588y². These replace the book's |Γ(s)|e^{πτ/2}·c/τ^{σ/2} factor.

items.changes_since_2013: no counterpart (1305.2897v4 (3.32) gives |u_{0,+}| = (ℓ/√2)√(υ²−υ) for the 2013 direct-integral saddle)

items.label: eq:journ
items.book_statement: On the slanted segment L₂, provided β ≤ arg(u_{0,+})/2: Re φ(u) ≥ Re φ(u_{0,+}) − Re((u−u_{0,+})²/2), derived from (8.12) and (8.33). It bounds I₂ and, at u = x₁, feeds the bound on I₃.
items.note: The angle condition keeps L₂ inside the range t ≥ −t₀ of (8.33). Here t is the tangent of the angle at 0 measured from u_∘: t = tan(arg u_{0,+} − β) at u_{0,+} and t = −tanβ at (x₁,0). Then Re φ on L₂ is bounded below by a quadratic that equals Re φ(u_{0,+}) and has zero slope at u_{0,+}.

lean.note: The rotated ray has no L₂ or L₃. Its Gaussian majorant is the completed square −(c/2)r²+br = b²/(2c) − (c/2)(r−b/c)² (line 457), valid on all of (0,∞) with no angle condition.
Assembles the single-piece bound that replaces I₁+I₂+I₃: exp(−θ|τ|)·exp(b²/2c)·(polynomial), with b = 2π|δ|sinθ and c = cos2θ.

erratum.description: In the paragraph giving the validity condition for (8.37), 'the angle formed by the origin, (x₁,0) and u_0' should read u_∘ (u_0 denotes the saddle points of (8.15)). Also, 't₀ = tan α₀' uses α₀ (the angle at 0 between u_{0,+} and u_∘), which is defined only in commented-out LaTeX. The condition β ≤ arg(u_{0,+})/2 and (8.37) itself are correct.

items.label: eq:cuchara
items.book_statement: First contour (ℓ > 0, τ > 0): on the slanted segment L₂ leaving u₀,₊ at angle β, |u|^{−σ} ≤ |u∘|^{−σ} and the quadratic bound (8.37) give I₂ < |u∘|^{−σ}e^{−ℜφ(u₀,₊)}√(π/(2cos 2β)).
items.note: Needs 2β ≤ arg u₀,₊ so that (8.37) holds on L₂. Used with β = π/8 for any ρ (√(π/(2cos(π/4))) = √π/2^{1/4} = 1.49045) and with β ∈ {π/6, π/5} for ρ ≤ 3/2. The any-ρ I₂ bound also needs the |u∘| bound after (8.39). Its printed derivation has a gap, but the conclusion is true.

lean.note: Replaces the whole contour estimate. On the rotated ray t = re^{iθ}, |F_δ(s+2)| ≤ e^{−|θ||τ|}∫₀^∞ r^{σ+1}e^{−r²cos2θ/2 + 2π|δ||sinθ|r}dr. No dual integral (8.11), saddle point or pieces L₁–L₃.
Lean's substitute for the contour shift: the rotated integral is independent of θ for |θ| < π/4, because the θ-derivative of the integrand is an exact r-derivative.

erratum.description: In the I₂ bound drawn from (8.38) for β ∈ {π/6, π/5}, the condition is printed 'when υ(ρ) ≤ 3/2'. It should be 'ρ ≤ 3/2': that condition makes 2β ≤ arg u₀,₊, and it is the one the conclusion and (8.41) use.

items.changes_since_2013: No counterpart. The contour for the dual integral (8.11) (Temme's suggestion) is new; 1305.2897v4 applied the saddle-point method to (8.8) on a limaçon-of-Pascal contour.

items.label: eq:empo
items.book_statement: The point u∘ of L₂ nearest the origin has |u∘| = ℜ(u₀,₊e^{−iβ}) = (ℓ/2)(√((j−1)/2)cos β + (1+√((j+1)/2))sin β), with j = √(1+ρ²).
items.note: (8.39) itself is correct. For ℓ = 3, τ = 2, β = π/8 the foot of the perpendicular has |u∘| = 1.764324, as (8.39) gives. Not needed in Lean: the rotated-ray integrand carries r^{σ+1}, which integral_rpow_exp_quad_le handles by r^p ≤ 1 + r², so no distance-to-origin bound occurs.

erratum.description: The display after (8.39) claims the squared bracket is ≥ j/2 + (7/2)sin²β − ½cos²β + (j/2)sin²β. This fails as j → 1 (small ρ). The correct bookkeeping (drop the sin2β terms, use √(2(j+1)) ≥ 2) gives no (j/2)sin²β term. The next line's |u∘| ≥ (ℓ/2)√((j/2)(1+sin²β)) still holds for β ∈ [π/8, π/4]. Separately, 'arg u₀ = arg u₀,₊ − β' before (8.39) should read arg u∘ = β.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: the display after (8.39) fails for small rho (beta = pi/8: S = 0.585786 < 0.659010 at j = 1, failing for rho < 0.103623) while |u_o| >= (l/2)sqrt((j/2)(1+sin^2 beta)) holds for beta in [pi/8, pi/4], and arg u_o = beta, not arg u_{0,+} - beta.
check.note: The display after (8.39) claims the square is at least j/2 + (7/2)sin^2 b - (1/2)cos^2 b + (j/2)sin^2 b. This is false near j = 1: at beta = pi/8 the square is 0.585786 against 0.659010 at j = 1, and the display fails for rho < 0.10362. The next line, |u_o| >= (l/2)sqrt((j/2)(1+sin^2 beta)), still holds for beta in [pi/8, pi/4] (minimum margin (7/2)sin^2(pi/8) - 1/2 = 0.01256, at j = 1), so nothing downstream changes. The sharp condition is tan beta >= 1/sqrt 6, not the printed 1/sqrt 7. Separately, 'arg u_0 = arg u_{0,+} - beta' (l.866) should read arg u_o = beta.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: the display after (8.39) fails for small rho (beta = pi/8: S = 0.585786 < 0.659010 at j = 1, failing for rho < 0.103623) while |u_o| >= (l/2)sqrt((j/2)(1+sin^2 beta)) holds for beta in [pi/8, pi/4], and arg u_o = beta, not arg u_{0,+} - beta.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '(8.39)', u∘, cos β/sin β, distance-to-origin bound, 'π / 8' over all .lean; Explicit/MellinRotate.lean

items.label: eq:jame
items.book_statement: Restates the exponent E(ρ) = ½arccos(1/υ(ρ)) − (υ(ρ)−1)/ρ of (8.2), so that for ℓ > 0 one has −ℜφ(u₀,₊) = (π/2 − E(ρ) + 2/ρ)τ.
items.note: Agrees with (8.2): both give 0.1036642 at ρ = 0.8889. With cos2θ* = 1/υ one gets θ* = ½arccos(1/υ) and 2sin²θ*/(ρcos2θ*) = (υ−1)/ρ. So E(ρ) = max_θ[θ − 2sin²θ/(ρcos2θ)] exactly (numerically to 10⁻¹⁵ on ρ ∈ [0.01, 10⁴]). The rotated ray is therefore as sharp as the saddle point in the exponent.

lean.note: Its exponent is −θ|τ| + (2π|δ|sinθ)²/(2cos2θ) = −|τ|(θ − 2sin²θ/(ρcos2θ)). The optimum, at cos2θ = 1/υ(ρ), is exactly −E(ρ)|τ|. Lean never defines E or optimizes θ.
θ = 0.28 (the optimum at ρ = 3/2 is 0.28236) gives exponent ≤ −0.1598|τ| for ρ ≥ 3/2, the constant of (8.48) (E(1.5) = 0.15983).
θ = 0.1866ρ gives exponent −0.1065ρ|τ| = −0.1065y² (y = |τ|/(π|δ|)) for ρ < 3/2, the bound E(ρ) ≥ 0.1065ρ of (8.48).

erratum.description: The display right after (8.40), −ℜφ(u₀,₊) = (1+υ)/ρ + ½arccos(−1/υ) = π/2 − E(ρ) + 2/ρ, omits the factor τ. By (8.31) it should read −ℜφ(u₀,₊) = (π/2 − E(ρ) + 2/ρ)τ. The next step (with 2π²δ² = (2/ρ)τ) uses the corrected form. Harmless.

items.changes_since_2013: Same function as E(ρ) in 1305.2897v4's theorem (eq:cormo), written there ½(arccos(1/υ) − 2(υ−1)/ρ) with ρ = |τ|/(πδ)². There it entered a three-term bound.

items.label: eq:huj
items.book_statement: Conclusion when sgn ℓ = sgn τ (sgn δ ≠ sgn τ): |F_δ(s)| ≤ |Γ(s)|e^{πτ/2}e^{−E(ρ)τ} times c₁/τ^{σ/2} (any ρ) or c₂/ℓ^σ (ρ ≤ 3/2). Verbatim the theorem's (8.1).
items.note: Follows from the |I| bounds, (8.11) and the corrected display after (8.40). Spot checks used rotated-ray quadrature over δ ∈ [−3, −0.02], τ ∈ [0.25, 40], σ ∈ [0.05, 3]. They give |F_δ(s)|/RHS ≤ 0.85 for c₁ and ≤ 0.80 for c₂, with the largest ratios at small σ and large τ (0.90 for c₁ at σ = 0.01, τ = 80, ρ = 0.02). On the c₂ branch with σ ∈ [2,3] the ratio stays ≤ 0.34, and at small τ (0.02–0.2) ≤ 0.58. So the bound holds and is fairly tight. The c₂ case rests on the derivation flagged at (8.42); the claim survives. In Lean, norm_G_le_regimeB/A play the role of (8.41) combined with Cor 8.0.2 (k = 2); norm_G_tail consumes them in Explicit/ZeroSumBound.lean.

lean.note: For F_δ(s+2) with −1 ≤ ℜs ≤ 1, any δ and τ, θ ∈ [0, π/4): ≤ e^{−θ|τ|}e^{b²/2c}((1+(b/c)²)√(2π/c) + √π/(c√(c/2))), with b = 2π|δ|sinθ, c = cos2θ. Same optimal exponent; no Γ(s) factor; only k = 2.
Gr s δ 0 = ∫₀^∞ t^{s−1}·t²e^{−t²/2}e(δt)dt, i.e. the book's F_δ(s+2).

items.changes_since_2013: Rewritten. 1305.2897v4 (eq:wilen) gave C₀e^{−E(ρ)|τ|} + C₁e^{−0.4798|τ|} + C₂e^{−min((τ/πδ)²/8, 25|τ|/32)}. The single-term form with |Γ(s)|e^{πτ/2}, c₁, c₂ (and the explicit δ ≠ 0) is new.

items.label: eq:marmota
items.book_statement: Defines c_{1,σ,τ}, c_{2,σ,τ} (as in (8.2)): half the summed normalized I₁, I₂, I₃ contributions, for β = π/8 (any ρ) and for β ∈ {π/6, π/5} (ρ ≤ 3/2).

lean.note: Lean's prefactor (1+(b/c)²)√(2π/c) + √π/(c√(c/2)) plays the role of c₁, c₂. It comes from completing the square and r^p ≤ 1+r² (0 ≤ p ≤ 2). norm_G_le_regimeB/A bound it by 0.892|τ| and 0.588y².

erratum.description: For ρ ≤ 3/2 the book bounds I₂ by the smaller of its β = π/6 and β = π/5 values. But it always adds the β = π/6 term e^{−τ/6}/(1/√3)^σ for I₃, and one contour (one β) must serve all three pieces. For σ > 1.4875 the minimum picks β = π/5. By the book's own estimate, that contour's I₃ term is e^{−0.11803τ}/0.72654^σ, which is larger when τ > 4.73σ. A sharper I₃ estimate makes the printed c₂ valid.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: for sigma > 1.48748 and tau > 4.7262 sigma the printed c_2 in (8.42) uses the beta=pi/6 I_3 term with the beta=pi/5 I_2 term (one contour gives c_2 = 3.19278, 5.05219 at tau=20, sigma=2, 3, against printed 3.15691, 5.02186), and y_0 >= l restores the printed c_2.
check.note: For rho <= 3/2, c_2 in (8.42) takes the smaller of the beta = pi/6 and beta = pi/5 I_2 terms but always adds the beta = pi/6 I_3 term, although one contour has a single beta. For sigma > 1.48748 the min picks pi/5, whose I_3 term by the book's estimate is e^{-0.11803 tau}/0.72654^sigma, larger exactly when tau > 4.7262 sigma. At tau = 20 one contour gives c_2 = 3.19278 (sigma = 2) and 5.05219 (sigma = 3) against the printed 3.15691 and 5.02186; the best single admissible beta still gives 3.17814 at sigma = 2. Repair: y_0 >= l and l^2 >= 8 tau/3 raise the I_3 exponent to 0.62951 tau (the exact value is >= 1.101 tau), which makes the printed c_2 valid, so the claim survives as a proof gap.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: for sigma > 1.48748 and tau > 4.7262 sigma the printed c_2 in (8.42) uses the beta=pi/6 I_3 term with the beta=pi/5 I_2 term (one contour gives c_2 = 3.19278, 5.05219 at tau=20, sigma=2, 3, against printed 3.15691, 5.02186), and y_0 >= l restores the printed c_2.

items.book_statement: For ρ ≤ 3/2, the saddle point's real part satisfies x₀ ≥ (√(√13−2)/6)|ℓ|ρ = (2√(√13−2)/3)τ/|ℓ| ≥ 0.84473|τ|/|ℓ|: the ρ ≤ 3/2 case of (8.4).

items.label: eq:blondie2
items.book_statement: For ρ ≥ 3/2, since (j(ρ)−1)/ρ increases, x₀ = (|ℓ|/2)√((j−1)/2) ≥ √((√13−2)/6)·√τ ≥ 0.51729√τ. This is the first case of (8.4), which (8.4) misstates as holding for arbitrary ρ.
items.note: √(√13−2)/√6 = 0.5172928 ≥ 0.51729. Directly, x₀/(0.51729√τ) ≥ 1.0000055 on ρ ∈ [1.5, 10⁴], and ((j−1)/ρ)′ = (j−1)/(ρ²j) ≥ 0 as printed. (8.4) of Thm 8.0.1 states x₀ ≥ 0.51729√τ 'for ρ arbitrary'. But x₀/√τ = √((j−1)/(2ρ)) increases from 0 (as ρ → 0) to 0.5172928 at ρ = 3/2: it is 0.45509 at ρ = 1, and x₀ = 0.15895 at δ = 1, τ = 1 (ρ = 0.1013). So the first case of (8.4) holds only for ρ ≥ 3/2, or for ℓ = 0, where x₀ = √(τ/2). §8.5 uses it only for ρ ≥ 3/2, so this is a harmless misprint in Eq 8.4 (outside this batch). Used in (8.3)/(8.4) and §8.5. Not needed in Lean (no saddle point x₀).

items.label: eq:chanmayo
items.book_statement: Summing the second contour's pieces (ℓ < 0 ≤ τ): |F_δ(s)| ≤ |x₀|^{−σ}((1+π/2^{3/2})e^{−ℜφ(u₀,₊)} + ½e^{−τπ/2})e^{−ℓ²/2}|Γ(s)|. With −ℜφ(u₀,₊) ≤ πτ/4 this yields (8.3).
items.note: I₁ ≤ x₀^{−σ}√(2π)e^{−ℜφ(u₀,₊)} and I₂ ≤ (π^{3/2}/4)x₀^{−σ}e^{−ℜφ(u₀,₊)} are right. They give 1 + π/2^{5/2} = 1.5554; the printed 1 + π/2^{3/2} = 2.1107 is safe. The I₃ bound is wrong: L₃ in fact carries the true size |Γ(s)||ℓ|^{−σ}e^{−πτ/2}. (8.3) inherits the error, and Cor 8.0.2's proof uses its e^{−ℓ²/2} in (8.49).

In fact ∫_{−∞}^{−x₀}e^{−(y−ℓ)²/2}dy = ∫_{x₀−|ℓ|}^∞e^{−t²/2}dt ≥ √(π/2) once x₀ ≤ |ℓ|. So the e^{−τπ/2} term loses its e^{−ℓ²/2} factor: it is only ≤ x₀^{−σ}e^{−τπ/2}|Γ(s)|.

items.label: eq:dorof
items.book_statement: Lower bound for the exponent E(ρ) of (8.2): E(ρ) ≥ 0.1598 for ρ ≥ 1.5 (E increasing, E(1.5) = 0.15982…), E(ρ) ≥ 0.1065ρ for ρ < 1.5 (Taylor bounds for ρ ≤ 1/2, interval bisection on [1/2, 3/2]).
items.note: The book asserts that E is increasing without proof (the 2013 Lemma kimil was dropped). It is true: E(ρ) = max_θ[θ − (2/ρ)sin²θ/cos2θ], attained at cos2θ = 1/υ(ρ), and the bracket increases in ρ for each θ. That bracket is exactly Lean's rotation exponent per |τ|. Lean's θ = 0.28 gives 0.159812 at ρ = 3/2 (vs E(1.5) = 0.159828), and θ = 0.1866ρ gives ≥ 0.10654ρ. So Lean needs neither E(ρ) nor bisection.

lean.note: Branch ρ ≥ 3/2 (|τ| ≥ (3/2)(πδ)²): the fixed rotation angle θ = 0.28 and π²δ² ≤ (2/3)|τ| give exponent −0.28|τ| + 0.120192|τ| ≤ −0.1598|τ| (lines 549–555, 573–576). No E(ρ) and no monotonicity argument. Needs |τ| ≥ 50.

Branch ρ < 3/2: θ = 0.1866|τ|/(πδ)² = 0.1866ρ (line 601) gives −0.1866y² + 0.0801y² = −0.1065y², where y² = ρ|τ| (lines 654–661). Uses polynomial sin/cos bounds and nlinarith, not Taylor bounds plus bisection. Needs y ≥ 10.

The 2013 proof used Lemma kimil, E ≥ ρ/8 − 5ρ³/384 (which also gave monotonicity), for ρ ≤ 1.19, plus bisection on [1.19, 1.5]. The book states E ≥ … directly, with a Taylor argument for ρ ≤ 1/2 and bisection on [1/2, 3/2]. Constants unchanged.

The function increases on (0,1], so the supremum of 3.15683^{k+1}e^{−80/(3t)}/t^{k+1} there is 3.15683^{k+1}e^{−80/3}: 8.3·10⁻¹², 2.6·10⁻¹¹ and 8.3·10⁻¹¹ for k = 0, 1, 2. The printed 0.04355, 0.00759 and 0.00224 exceed these by factors of 5.3·10⁹, 2.9·10⁸ and 2.7·10⁷. This is harmless, since (8.50) is negligible anyway, and is not an erratum.

lean.note: Bounds the δ-term −2πδr sin θ of the rotated integrand by 2π|δ||sin θ|r (line 378), so one bound serves both signs of δ. There is no same-sign case, no lower bound for x₀ and no e^{−ℓ²/2} factor.
Closed form after completing the square, with θ' = ±θ chosen by the sign of ℑs (line 487). Both regime bounds start from it.
The Lean bound for ρ < 3/2 (|τ| < (3/2)(πδ)²): |F_δ(s+2)| ≤ 0.588y²e^{−0.1065y²}, y = |τ|/(π|δ|) ≥ 10, −1 ≤ ℜs ≤ 1, for either sign of δ. It covers the same-sign term that (8.49) estimates.

In this same-sign case, reduced to τ > 0, ℓ = −2πδ < 0, so ℓ^σ is not a positive real: it is undefined for non-integer σ and negative for odd σ. Thm 8.0.1's (8.4) has the correct 0.84473|τ|/|ℓ|. The slip first appears at the end of (8.45). With |ℓ| every step holds.

items.label: eq:auste
items.book_statement: Same-sign case (sgn δ = sgn τ or δ = 0; take τ > 0), τ ≥ 20, σ ≤ 3: |F_δ(s)| ≤ |Γ(s)|e^{πτ/2}e^{−0.1598τ} times 4·10⁻⁷|ℓ|^{−σ} (ρ ≤ 3/2) or 6·10⁻⁵τ^{−σ/2} (ρ ≥ 3/2): negligible beside (8.1).
items.note: Used in the last step of Cor 8.0.2 ('remembering to add (8.50)'). For δ ≠ 0, one of |F_δ(s+k)| and |F_δ(1−s+k)| is in the main case (8.1) and the other in the same-sign case; for δ = 0 both are same-sign. 4·10⁻⁷ is added to the c₂ bounds in κ_{k,0}, and 6·10⁻⁵ to the c₁ bounds in κ_{k,1}. For ρ < 3/2 this needs e^{−0.1598τ} ≤ e^{−0.1065ρτ}, i.e. 0.1065·1.5 = 0.15975 ≤ 0.1598. Lean treats only k = 2 (F_δ(s+2), −1 ≤ ℜs ≤ 1). Both regime bounds feed TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.norm_G_tail (ZeroSumBound.lean:115, 134).

lean.note: For |τ| ≥ (3/2)(πδ)² (ρ ≥ 3/2), |τ| ≥ 50 and −1 ≤ ℜs ≤ 1: |F_δ(s+2)| ≤ 0.892|τ|e^{−0.1598|τ|} for either sign of δ, since only |δ| enters (norm_Gr_le, line 378). The same-sign term therefore needs no separate negligible bound. Each |F_δ(s+2)| is bounded on its own, not the pair sum to which (8.50) is added.
The same for ρ < 3/2: 0.588y²e^{−0.1065y²} with y = |τ|/(π|δ|) ≥ 10 (that is, |τ| ≥ 5|ℓ|), for either sign of δ.

erratum.description: As in (8.49), 1/ℓ^σ should be 1/|ℓ|^σ: in this case ℓ = −2πδ < 0 once τ > 0. The display just before (8.50) has the same slip. The numerical constants are correct.

The corollary proof folded it together with the main case's C₁ term into 1.025|τ|^{(k+1)/2}e^{−0.4798|τ|} ≤ 1.3·10⁻¹¹e^{−0.1598|τ|} for |τ| ≥ 100 ((doutes)–(cocoko), majarcs.tex l.2603–2625). items.label: eq:sitirlo
items.book_statement: Stirling's formula with remainder (|R₂(s)| < √2/(180|s|³) for Re s ≥ 0) and arctan r ≤ r give |Γ(s)|e^{πτ/2} ≤ √(2π)|s|^{σ−1/2}exp(1/(12|s|) + √2/(180|s|³)) for σ ≥ 0, τ > 0.
items.note: Checked numerically. The quoted remainder bound holds on Re z ≥ 0, |z| ∈ [0.05, 20]: the largest ratio |R₂|/bound is 0.9993, on the real axis. (8.51) itself holds on a grid σ ∈ [0,3], τ ∈ [0.1, 1000] (largest ratio 0.99992). The derivation assumes τ > 0 (arg s = π/2 − arctan(σ/τ)); for τ < 0 the printed form is trivially true. (9.86) restates it with |ℑs|, by conjugation.

lean.note: Use in Ch. 8: the rotated-ray bound for F_δ(s+2) is closed-form and never factors out Γ(s)e^{πτ/2}, so no Stirling estimate is needed.

Reuse in Ch. 9 (as (9.86), the Γ factor of M(η₊²) in Prop 9.5.1): Lean uses |Γ(x+iy)| ≤ e^{−φ|y|}Γ(x)/cos^x φ, 0 ≤ φ < π/2, instead of Stirling. The decay rate is below π/2, with no polynomial factor.
Applies norm_Gamma_le_rot with φ = 1.2 to M(t²e^{−t²}) = Γ(s/2+1)/2, giving ≤ 8e^{−0.6|ℑs|} on −1 ≤ ℜs ≤ 2. This plays the role of (9.86)–(9.87).

items.note: Checked: √(2π)·1.004177 times 1.000625, 1.007491 and 1.028204 gives 2.5186716, 2.5359540 and 2.5880907. The maxima of |1+iσ/τ|^{σ−1/2} at |τ| = 20 are 1.00062441, 1.00749066 and 1.02820366. e^{1/240+√2/(180·20³)} = 1.0041763. items.label: lem:agamon
items.book_statement: For C¹ η with η, η′ ∈ L² and ηt^{σ−1}, η′t^{σ−1} ∈ L¹ near [1/2,3/2], χ primitive mod q: Σ Λ(n)χ(n)e(δn/x)η(n/x) = I_{q=1}η̂(−δ)x − Σ_ρ G_δ(ρ)x^ρ − R + O*((log q+6.01)(|η′|₂+2π|δ||η|₂))x^{−1/2}.

The book's R misses η(0)log x for even χ when η(0) ≠ 0, a case Lean excludes.
items.evidence: Lean: limit identity with exact ℜs=−1/2 integral for GoodSmoothing φ (holomorphic at 0, exponential decay); book: L¹/L² hypotheses, R term, O*((log q+6.01)(|η′|₂+2π|δ||η|₂))x^{−1/2}.

lean.note: χ primitive ≠ 1, any GoodSmoothing φ: rectangle zero sums along T_k ∈ [k+1,k+2] tend to −S − (1/2π)∫_{ℜs=−1/2}(L′/L)Mx^s. No R; s=0 is in the sum for even χ.
q = 1: zero sums tend to M(1)x − S − (1/2π)∫(ζ′/ζ)Mx^s on ℜs = −1/2.
Line-integral error: ≤ x^{−1/2}VgL(D_N,K_v,θ_v) given |M(−1/2+iy)| ≤ K_v e^{−θ_v|y|}; Landau-based, not (log q+6.01).

Combines explicit formula, zero-sum bound and line bound into |S| for general smoothings (used for η₊).
Specialization to φ = fδ δ (η = t²e^{−t²/2}).
Admissible smoothings: continuity, Mellin convergence at 3/2, holomorphy on ℜs > −1 (so η(0)=0), exponential decay on −1/2 ≤ ℜs ≤ 3/2.

items.label: eq:bleucol
items.book_statement: Bound for the residue term R of Lemma 9.1.1, for every primitive χ: |R| ≤ |η(0)|(3 log q + 15.289) + |c₀|, from Lemma 9.1.2, M(q) ≤ q^{4/5} and |log(2π/q) + γ| ≤ log q + log(e^γ·2π/9).
items.note: Only Prop 9.2.2 (the Gaussian, η(0) = 1) uses (9.23) (expform.tex l.1002). The main-line propositions have η(0) = 0 and take R = O*(c₀) directly (l.1320, 1662, 1790). Recomputed: c = 5 log(2√3 ζ(9/8)/ζ(9/4)) = 15.070164; log(e^γ·2π/9) + 15.07017 = 15.28804 ≤ 15.289; |log(2π/q) + γ| ≤ log q + 0.21787 for all q ≥ 3, with equality at q = 3; 15.289 > log 2π covers q = 1. Through Lemma 9.1.2 the bound needs GRH up to height 5/8. Caveat (an erratum of Lemma 9.1.1, not of (9.23)): Lemma 9.1.1 defines R as Res_{s=0}(L′/L)G_δ, without the factor x^s of the integrand. For even χ, q > 1 and η(0) ≠ 0, both L′/L and G_δ have simple poles at 0, so the residue of (L′/L)G_δx^s is R + η(0) log x. (9.23) bounds only the stated R. This affects only the Gaussian Prop 9.2.2, whose x^{−1} term lacks (log x)/x. For x ≥ 10⁸ that term is ≤ 0.0019/√x, inside the ≈0.99 of slack in Thm 7.1.1's constant 112. Lean is unaffected, since its G_δ has no pole at 0.

lean.note: Only the c₀ part has a Lean counterpart. Lean's smoothings vanish at 0, so R is the residue G_δ(0) at the trivial zero s = 0 (even χ). Lean keeps s = 0 among the rectangle zeros and bounds it by E0b (step hA, lines 468–484), via |G_δ(0)| ≤ 112 (norm_G_uniform).

E0b = 112·log(B′₀/0.355)/log(10/3): the bound 112 for |G_δ(0)| times a Jensen count of the zeros near 0. MajorArcs.E0b_le (Cor713.lean:510) gives E0b ≤ 15300 for q ≤ 3·10⁵ (recomputed: 15228 at q = 3·10⁵). For t²e^{−t²/2} the book has |c₀| ≤ 2.138 + 10.99|δ| (expform.tex l.1321).
The same treatment for the other smoothings (η₊, η₊², η₊²·log): a zero at 0 contributes at most G₀·Z3g B 0. For ζ, through (s−1)ζ(s), there is no zero at 0 and the term is vacuous.

items.label: lem:garmola
items.book_statement: Partial summation over zeros: for piecewise C¹ f with f(t)t log t → 0 and y ≥ 1, Σ_{γ>y} f(γ) = (1/2π)∫_y^∞ f log(qT/2π) + ½O*(|f(y)|g_χ(y) + ∫_y^∞|f′|g_χ). For real decreasing f, the error is claimed to be O*(¼∫f/T).
items.note: No Lean declaration cites this lemma. In [H] it is used by Lemma 9.1.4, through (9.32) and with a discontinuous f. It is also used by the tail bounds (9.35), (9.49), (9.66) and (9.90), which go through the false decreasing clause. Lean replaces both kinds of use by Jensen windows and never uses an asymptotic N(T,χ). The N⁺ = N/2 issue is reported in README.md:192 and NOTES.md:12–14. The decreasing-clause error and the jump failure are new findings.

lean.note: Jensen's formula: L(s,χ) (χ ≠ 1 primitive) has at most log(B′_T/0.355)/log(10/r) zeros in |s − (2+iT)| ≤ r, where B′_T = 1400q⁹(q+1)(|T|+22)(1.25(|T|+11))¹⁰. This local upper count replaces N(T,χ). The generic and ζ form is zero_count_polyG (ZeroSumGen.lean:39).

For |γ| ≤ T₀ < Jh: if every window of height h carries multiplicity ≤ Z, then Σ m_u|f(ℑu)| ≤ Z((1/h)∫_{−Jh}^{Jh}|f| + ∫_{−Jh}^{Jh}|f′|), for f with a continuous derivative. Both signs of γ are handled at once, with a Sobolev bound per window in place of a Stieltjes integral.

For |γ| > T₀: Σ m_u Eρ^{k(u)} ≤ E(Z₀/(1−ρ) + c/(1−ρ)²) when window k (height 4.4 above T₀) holds ≤ Z₀ + c(k+1) zeros (count_tail_window). This replaces Lemma 9.1.3 in the tail bounds, in the roles of Lemmas 9.3.1 and 9.4.1 and of (9.90). The Gaussian Lemma 9.2.1 has no Lean counterpart.

erratum.description: The closing clause is false. For real decreasing f, f(y)g_χ(y) − ∫_y^∞ f′g_χ = 2f(y)g_χ(y) + 0.5∫_y^∞ f/T, not 0.5∫_y^∞ f/T, so the error is only O*(f(y)g_χ(y) + ¼∫_y^∞ f(T)/T dT). (9.24) itself also fails if 'piecewise C¹' allows jumps, because jumps are not counted in ∫|f′|g_χ. The book needs that reading in Lemma 9.1.4, where f is cut off at T₀. Separately (repo-docs), the proof's N⁺ = N/2 holds only for real χ, so (9.24) is unproven for complex χ. The two-sided form, summing f(|γ|) for continuous f, is fine. 'T ≥ T₀' in the proof should read 'T ≥ y'.

items.label: eq:melos
items.book_statement: Explicit zero count for T ≥ 1: the number N(T,χ) of non-trivial zeros with |γ| ≤ T is (T/π)log(qT/2πe) + O*(g_χ(T)). It is quoted from Rosser (q = 1), McCurley and Trudgian.
items.note: Constants checked. [Tru, Thm 1] (arXiv:1206.1844v2) gives, for primitive nonprincipal χ and T ≥ 1, |N(T,χ) − (T/π)log(qT/2πe)| ≤ 0.315 log qT + 6.455, with N counting zeros with 0 < β < 1 and |γ| ≤ T. This implies g_χ = 0.5 log qT + 17.7. McCurley's constants, as tabulated there, are C₁ = 0.506 and C₂ = 16.989 at η = 0.05, consistent with 0.5 log qT + 17.7 for η slightly below 0.05. For q = 1, doubling Rosser's bound for N(T) (T ≥ 2) and adding 7/4 gives at most 0.274 log T + 0.886 log log T + 4.93, below g. For 1 ≤ T < 14.13, N = 0 and |(T/π)log(T/2πe)| ≤ 2. This is a two-sided count, so it supports sums of f(|γ|) but not one-sided sums for complex χ (see the Lemma 9.1.3 erratum). Lean drops the asymptotic entirely.

lean.note: Jensen's formula with the polynomial growth bound B′_T for L(s,χ) (LGrowthPoly) gives only an upper count per disc around 2 + iT, of order log(qT). It gives no main term.
The same for any PolyDatum, used for ζ through zetaF = (s−1)ζ(s) (polyDatum_zeta2).
The window form: the zeros of the explicit-formula rectangle in |u − (2+ic)| ≤ r have total multiplicity ≤ log(B′_c/0.355)/log(10/r).

items.note: This step depends on the preceding unnumbered step Σ f(γ) = −½∫f′(N(T,χ) − N(y,χ)) dT, i.e. N⁺ = N/2, which is false for complex χ (see the Lemma 9.1.3 erratum). It also needs f to be continuous.

lean.note: Lean has no partial summation against a counting function. Per-window Sobolev bounds times Jensen counts take its place for |γ| ≤ T₀.
The same role for |γ| > T₀.

items.label: eq:linstrau
items.book_statement: Integration by parts for the main term: −½∫_y^∞ f′(T)[M(T) − M(y)] dT = (1/2π)∫_y^∞ f(T) log(qT/2π) dT, where M(T) = (T/π)log(qT/2πe) and M′(T) = (1/π)log(qT/2π).
items.note: Correct, given f(T)T log T → 0 (so the boundary term vanishes) and f continuous. Lean does not need it: the window method has no main term (T/π)log(qT/2πe) to integrate, and the zero density enters only through the per-window Jensen counts.

items.label: lem:hausierer
items.book_statement: Zeros up to height T₀, for general real η: if GRH holds up to T₀ ≥ 1, Σ_{|γ|≤T₀}|G_δ(ρ)| ≤ (|η|₂+|η·log|₂)√T₀ log qT₀ + (17.21|η·log|₂ − log(2π√e)|η|₂)√T₀ + |η/√t|₁(1.32 log q + 34.5).
items.note: Lean keeps the strategy: Cauchy–Schwarz plus Mellin–Plancherel, giving √T₀·log. It replaces partial summation with N(T,χ) by Sobolev bounds on windows of height 3.48, each carrying ≤ ZL zeros (Jensen). There are no separate terms for low-lying zeros or for |f(1)|g_χ(1). The GRH hypothesis is the explicit argument hG, supplied by Platt's check (PlattGRH). All linked declarations use none of the five hypotheses. The only Lean mention of the lemma is the module comment at Prop932.lean:14.

lean.note: For η = t²e^{−t²/2}, with |γ| ≤ T₀ < Jh and each window of height h carrying multiplicity ≤ Z: Σ m|G_δ(½+iγ)| ≤ Z((1/h)√(2π·0.6647·2Jh) + √(2π·0.1707·2Jh)). It has no log q term and no |η/√t|₁ term.
Jensen gives Z = ZL zeros per window of height 3.48 (a disc of radius 2.3 about 2 + ic). This replaces the N(T,χ) formula and the separate count N(1,χ) ≤ 0.819 log q + 16.8.

Step hB (lines 485–505). Under GRH up to T₀ (the explicit argument hG), the non-zero rectangle zeros with |γ| ≤ T₀ lie on ℜs = ½. Since |x^ρ| = √x there, combining this with sum_window_fline_le and count_line_window gives √x·E1b, Lean's version of √x·(9.29).
Step hB for any smoothing with Plancherel data Q₁ ≥ ∫|F|² and Q₂ ≥ ∫|F′|² (E1g). It is used for η₊, η₊², η₊²·log and for ζ (q = 1).
Mellin–Plancherel over the whole line: ∫_ℝ|G_δ(½+it)|²dt = 2π|η|₂², with |η|₂² = 3√π/8. integral_norm_sq_flineD (l.253) gives ∫_ℝ|G′_δ|² = 2π∫(log v)²η² ≤ 2π(3/2 − 3√π/4).

erratum.description: The Cauchy–Schwarz step for ∫₁^∞|f′|g_χ is wrong. As displayed it gives |η·log|₂√((1/π)∫g_χ²), and the summing step uses |η·log|₂√(∫g_χ²). These need ∫₁^{T₀}|f′|² ≤ |η·log|₂²/π and ≤ |η·log|₂² respectively, but even the claimed symmetry gives only π|η·log|₂². So the (½log qT₀ + 17.21)|η·log|₂√T₀ term lacks a factor √π. Also, √((log qT₀/2πe)² + 1) ≤ log(qT₀/2πe) + ½ needs qT₀ ≥ 36.2, and one display lacks a square. (9.29) is not established in general.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: for eta = t^2 e^{-t^2/2}, q = 1, T0 = 10, int_1^T0 |f'| g_chi = 16.92 exceeds the displayed Cauchy-Schwarz bound 12.65, and int_1^T0 |f'|^2 = 0.194 > |eta log|_2^2 = 0.1636.
check.note: In the proof of Lemma 9.1.4 the Cauchy–Schwarz bound for ∫₁^∞|f′|g_χ is |η·log|₂√((1/π)∫g_χ²), and the summing step uses |η·log|₂√(∫g_χ²); for η = t²e^{−t²/2}, δ = 0, q = 1, T₀ = 10, ∫₁^{T₀}|f′|g_χ = 16.92 > 12.65 and ∫₁^{T₀}|f′|² = 0.194 > |η·log|₂² = 0.1636, while Plancherel gives (1/2π)∫|G′|² = |η·log|₂² (the book omits the square). The step √(x²+1) ≤ x + ½ needs qT₀ ≥ 36.16. The gap claim survives; the claim's repaired-chain comparison with (9.29) was not re-run.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: for eta = t^2 e^{-t^2/2}, q = 1, T0 = 10, int_1^T0 |f'| g_chi = 16.92 exceeds the displayed Cauchy-Schwarz bound 12.65, and int_1^T0 |f'|^2 = 0.194 > |eta log|_2^2 = 0.1636.

items.label: eq:arnbax
items.book_statement: Lemma 9.1.4's bound on Σ_{|γ|≤T₀}|G_δ(ρ)|: (|η|₂+|η·log|₂)√T₀ log qT₀ + (17.21|η·log|₂ − log(2π√e)|η|₂)√T₀ + |η/√t|₁(1.32 log q + 34.5).
items.note: Lean bounds the low-zero sum with Jensen-window counts instead of Lemma 9.1.4; its constant is about 12 times (9.29) at qT₀ = 10⁸. For t²e^{−t²/2}, (9.29) evaluates to (9.57)'s 1.22, 5.056, 1.423, 37.19.

lean.note: Lean's analogue: ZL·((1/3.48)√(2π·0.6647·2J·3.48) + √(2π·0.1707·2J·3.48)), order √T₀(log q + log T₀); enters as E1b·√x.
The window-sum inequality behind E1b, for η = t²e^{−t²/2} and any per-window zero count Z.
E1b q (10⁸/q) ≤ 3.42·10⁶/√q for 2 ≤ q ≤ 3·10⁵; now with no Fact hypotheses.

items.label: eq:sandunga
items.book_statement: Trivial bound on the critical line: |G_δ(½ + iτ)| ≤ ∫₀^∞|η(t)|t^{−1/2} dt = |η(t)/√t|₁. It is used for zeros with |γ| ≤ 1 and for the term |f(1)|g_χ(1).
items.note: The bound is correct, since |e(δt)t^{iτ}| = 1. For t²e^{−t²/2}, |η/√t|₁ = 2^{1/4}Γ(5/4) = 1.07790 (recomputed). Lean never states it: the Sobolev-window argument bounds |G_δ(½+iγ)| through ∫|G| and ∫|G′| over the window.

lean.note: Lean's pointwise control on each window is |f(γ)| ≤ (1/(b−a))∫_a^b|f| + ∫_a^b|f′|, fed by Plancherel. Low-lying zeros get no separate treatment, and there is no |f(1)|g_χ(1) term.

|G_δ(s)| ≤ 112e^{−θ_δ|ℑs|} on −1 ≤ ℜs ≤ 1, used only at s = 0 (zero_sum_bound step hA) and on ℜs = −1/2 (ExplicitBound, ZetaBound). Lean has other pointwise bounds too: norm_G_tail above T₀, norm_G_le_strip on −½ ≤ ℜs ≤ 3/2, and norm_G_uniform_ext. None is applied to zeros with |γ| ≤ T₀, and the trivial bound (9.30) itself (1.0779 for t²e^{−t²/2}) is never stated.

erratum.description: A stray clause 'where F_δ is as in (9.47)' follows (9.30). F_δ, the Mellin transform of the twisted Gaussian defined later in §9.3, occurs neither in (9.30) nor in Lemma 9.1.4.

items.label: eq:candonga
items.book_statement: Trivial bound for the derivative: |G′_δ(σ+iτ)| ≤ ∫₀^∞|(log t)η(t)|t^{σ−1} dt = |(log t)η(t)t^{σ−1}|₁.
items.note: Never used: no proof refers to (9.31), and the proof of Lemma 9.1.4 bounds ∫|G′_δ(½+iT)|² by Plancherel instead.

lean.note: d/dt G_δ(½+it), written as a Fourier transform of −2πix·e^{−x/2}fδ(e^{−x}). It includes e(δt).
Lean, like the proof of Lemma 9.1.4, uses the L² identity ∫_ℝ|G′_δ(½+it)|²dt = 2π∫(log v)²η(v)²dv rather than an L¹ bound.
L² identity for G′_δ on ℜs = 1/2 (Plancherel), not the L¹ pointwise bound of (9.31).

erratum.description: The middle expression omits e(δt). G′_δ(s) = ∫₀^∞(log t)η(t)e(δt)t^{s−1}dt; what is printed, ∫(log t)η(t)t^s dt/t, is the derivative of the Mellin transform of η alone. The final bound is unaffected, since |e(δt)| = 1.

items.label: eq:datora
items.book_statement: Lemma 9.1.3 at y = 1 with f(t) = |G_δ(½+it)| cut off at T₀: Σ_{1<|γ|≤T₀} f(γ) = (1/π)∫₁^{T₀} f(T)log(qT/2π) dT + O*(|f(1)|g_χ(1) + ∫₁^∞|f′|g_χ). The step relies on a claimed symmetry of f in τ.
items.note: Read as a statement about F(|γ|) with F continuous, (9.32) is the two-sided partial summation and holds for every χ. The gap lies in applying it to |G_δ(ρ)|. With F = max(|G_δ(½+it)|, |G_δ(½−it)|) one has ∫₁^{T₀}F² ≤ 2π|η|₂² and ∫|F′|² ≤ 2π|η·log|₂². In the book's applications T₀ ≫ |δ| (e.g. T₀ ≥ 4π²|δ|), so the jump term is exponentially small.

lean.note: Bounds Σ m|G_δ(½+iγ)| over |γ| ≤ T₀ < Jh with integrals over [−Jh, Jh]. It handles both signs of γ with G_δ itself, so no symmetry and no cutoff jump are needed.
The generic window lemma, for f with a continuous derivative. Since there is no Stieltjes integration, there is no boundary term.
The per-window zero count ZL replaces g_χ(1) and the N(T,χ) asymptotic.

erratum.description: The justification 'f(σ+iτ) = f(σ−iτ) because η is real-valued' is false for δ ≠ 0. In fact conj G_δ(s) = G_{−δ}(s̄), so |G_δ(½−iτ)| = |G_{−δ}(½+iτ)|. Hence Σ_{1<|γ|≤T₀}|G_δ(ρ)| is not Σ f(|γ|), and the next step, (1/π)∫₁^{T₀}|f|² ≤ |η|₂², fails. Also, f drops from f(T₀) to 0 at T₀. In the two-sided normalisation of (9.32), this adds the omitted boundary term |f(T₀)|g_χ(T₀). Taking F = max(|G_δ(½+it)|, |G_δ(½−it)|) repairs the step, with worse constants.

check.note: The sentence after (9.32), f(σ+iτ) = f(σ−iτ) 'because η is real-valued', is false for δ ≠ 0: for η = t²e^{−t²/2}, δ = 1, |G_δ(½+5i)| = 7.51·10⁻⁸ but |G_δ(½−5i)| = 0.4986 = |G_{−δ}(½+5i)|. At δ = −2 the next step fails: (1/π)∫₁^{40}|G_δ(½+iT)|²dT = 1.327 > |η|₂² = 0.665, and the cutoff at T₀ = 10 drops f from 0.333 to 0. The claim survives.

items.label: lem:garmonas
items.book_statement: For the one-sided Gaussian η♥ = e^{−t²/2}, χ primitive mod q and GRH up to T₀ ≥ 50, the zeros with |ℑρ| > T₀ give Σ|F_δ(ρ)| ≤ log(qT₀/2π)(3.53e^{−0.1598T₀} + 22.5(δ²/T₀)e^{−0.1065(T₀/π|δ|)²}), F_δ = M(η♥(t)e(δt)).
items.note: Side branch: feeds only Prop 9.2.2 and thence Thm 7.1.1, which Part III never cites. Its argument is the template for the main-line Lemmas 9.3.1 and 9.4.1, which repeat the pairing and the false clause at (9.49) and (9.66). Statement typos: F_δ is defined from η, meaning η♥; 'ℜ(s) = 1/2' should read 'ℜ(ρ) = 1/2'. x plays no role, and neither does the GRH hypothesis, since Cor 8.0.2 covers the whole strip. Lean has no explicit k = 0 analogue of Cor 8.0.2. Its explicit bounds are for G_δ(s) = F_δ(s+2) on −1 ≤ ℜs ≤ 1: TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.norm_G_le_regimeA and TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.norm_G_le_regimeB (0.588 and 0.892 per zero).

erratum.description: The proof fails for every χ. Its step (9.35) is Lemma 9.1.3's clause for real decreasing f. That clause drops a boundary term: f(y)g_χ(y) − ∫_y^∞f′g_χ equals 2f(y)g_χ(y) + ∫f g_χ′, not ½∫f/T. So (9.35) is false even for q = 1. For complex χ two more steps fail: the pairing ρ ↔ 1−ρ before (9.33), and N⁺ = N/2. A valid route bounds each zero by f (Cor 8.0.2 depends only on |τ|), counts all zeros with (9.26) and keeps the boundary term. That gives twice the printed bound plus 2f(T₀)(0.5 log qT₀ + 17.7). This is about 20 times the printed exponential term at q = 1, T₀ = 50, and about 5 times at qT₀ = 10⁸. The printed constants are not shown false, because Cor 8.0.2's majorant is far from tight.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: step (9.35) of the proof fails for zeta (0.0018539 > 0.0015796 at T0 = 52.9), and for chi mod 5 with chi(2) = i, 1 - rho is not a zero (|L(1-rho)| = 2.817).
check.note: The proof's step (9.35) fails even for ζ (δ = 0.01, T₀ = 52.9: 1.8539·10⁻³ > 1.5796·10⁻³), and for χ mod 5 with χ(2) = i the pairing ρ ↔ 1−ρ fails (ρ = ½+6.18358i is a zero, |L(1−ρ,χ)| = 2.817). With the boundary term restored the exponential coefficient at q = 1, T₀ = 50 is 143.8 against the printed 7.32 (in units of e^{−0.1598T₀}). The gap claim survives; the lemma's printed constants are not shown false.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: step (9.35) of the proof fails for zeta (0.0018539 > 0.0015796 at T0 = 52.9), and for chi mod 5 with chi(2) = i, 1 - rho is not a zero (|L(1-rho)| = 2.817).

items.label: eq:gargara
items.book_statement: First step of Lemma 9.2.1: pairing each zero ρ with 1−ρ and bounding |F_δ(ρ)| + |F_δ(1−ρ)| by Cor 8.0.2 (k = 0) gives Σ_{|ℑρ|>T₀}|F_δ(ρ)| ≤ Σ_{ℑρ>T₀} f(ℑρ).
items.note: Cor 8.0.2 needs σ ∈ [0,1] and |τ| ≥ 20, met since T₀ ≥ 50. The same 'pairs ρ, 1−ρ' step opens the proofs of Lemmas 9.3.1 and 9.4.1 ('As usual'), which are on [H]'s main line; the repo flags only Lemma 9.1.3's N⁺ = N/2.

erratum.description: The identity before (9.33) assumes the zeros of L(s,χ) come in pairs ρ, 1−ρ. The functional equation sends a zero ρ of L(s,χ) to the zero 1−ρ of L(s,χ̄); zeros of L(s,χ) are only symmetric under ρ ↦ 1−ρ̄. So for complex χ the identity fails and (9.33) is unproved. It holds for real χ; in general the right side also needs the zeros of L(s,χ̄) above T₀.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: for chi mod 5 with chi(2) = i the zeros are not symmetric under rho -> 1-rho: 1/2+50.66421i is a zero but |L(1-rho,chi)| = 1.424 (1-rho is a zero of L(s,chi-bar)).
check.note: The identity before (9.33) uses 'zeros come in pairs ρ, 1−ρ', which holds only for real χ: for χ mod 5 with χ(2) = i the zeros with 50 < t < 55 are at t = 50.664, 51.977, 53.442, 54.485 and at t = −51.090, −53.757, and |L(1−ρ,χ)| = 1.424 at ρ = ½+50.6642i (1−ρ is a zero of L(s,χ̄)); in 50 < |t| < 90 there are 26 zeros above and 25 below. The claim survives.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: for chi mod 5 with chi(2) = i the zeros are not symmetric under rho -> 1-rho: 1/2+50.66421i is a zero but |L(1-rho,chi)| = 1.424 (1-rho is a zero of L(s,chi-bar)).

items.label: eq:darmo
items.book_statement: Defines the majorant f(τ) = 3.001e^{−0.1065(τ/πδ)²} + 3.286e^{−0.1598|τ|}, the sum of Cor 8.0.2's two regime bounds for k = 0 (κ₀,₀ ≤ 3.001, κ₀,₁ ≤ 3.286); it bounds the pair sum for all |τ| ≥ 20 and decreases in τ.
items.note: Adding both terms avoids the case split |τ| ≶ (3/2)(πδ)²; Cor 8.0.2's (2|τ|/|ℓ|)² is (τ/πδ)² with ℓ = −2πδ. At δ = 0 the first term is 0. Lean has no k = 0 bound; for t²e^{−t²/2} it proves per-zero bounds TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.norm_G_le_regimeA (0.588y²e^{−0.1065y²}, MellinRotate.lean:580) and TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.norm_G_le_regimeB (0.892|τ|e^{−0.1598|τ|}, MellinRotate.lean:530).

lean.note: k = 2 analogue of the κ₀,₁ term: |G_δ(s)| ≤ 0.892|τ|e^{−0.1598|τ|}; no k = 0 bound.
k = 2 analogue of the κ₀,₀ term: 0.588y²e^{−0.1065y²}; no k = 0 bound.

items.label: eq:happin
items.book_statement: Applies Lemma 9.1.3 (f decreasing, y = T₀): Σ_{ℑρ>T₀} f(ℑρ) ≤ ∫_{T₀}^∞ f(T)((1/2π)log(qT/2π) + 1/(4T)) dT.
items.note: The boundary-term defect is the error in Lemma 9.1.3's closing clause, also recorded under that lemma. The same step recurs at (9.49) (Lemma 9.3.1) and (9.66) (Lemma 9.4.1), which are on [H]'s main line through Cor 7.1.3 and Thm 7.1.4. It recurs again at (9.90) (Prop 9.5.1, q = 1), where q = 1 avoids only the N⁺ = N/2 issue. (9.90) also applies this one-sided integral to the two-sided sum Σ_{|ℑρ|>T₀}, with the single-zero majorant (9.89), so a factor 2 appears to be missing there. At the book's heights (T₀ ≥ 333) the effect is negligible: for Lemma 9.2.1 at qT₀ = 10⁸ the corrected term is about 4.9 times the printed one. The hypothesis that f decreases on [T₀, ∞) holds.

erratum.description: False as printed, for real and complex χ alike, q = 1 included. (9.35) is Lemma 9.1.3's clause for real decreasing f at y = T₀, and that clause drops a boundary term. Integration by parts gives f(y)g_χ(y) − ∫_y^∞f′g_χ = 2f(y)g_χ(y) + ∫f g_χ′. So the error is O*(f(T₀)g_χ(T₀) + ¼∫f/T), not O*(¼∫f/T). For complex χ, the proof's N⁺ = N/2 (flagged in the repo) is a second, independent failure. Correct forms: for real χ, add f(T₀)(0.5 log qT₀ + 17.7) to the right side. For any χ, Σ_{|ℑρ|>T₀} f(|ℑρ|) ≤ ∫f((1/π)log(qT/2π) + 1/(2T))dT + 2f(T₀)(0.5 log qT₀ + 17.7).

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: for zeta, delta = 0.01, T0 = 52.9 the left side of (9.35) is 0.0018539 > 0.0015796, the right side; (9.35) fails at 90 of 201 grid points and holds once f(T0)g(T0) is added.
check.note: (9.35) as printed is false for ζ: with δ = 0.01, T₀ = 52.9 the left side is 1.8539·10⁻³ and the right side 1.5796·10⁻³, and on T₀ ∈ [50,100] (step 0.25) it fails at 90 of 201 points (worst ratio 1.288 at T₀ = 75.5). Adding f(T₀)(0.5 log qT₀ + 17.7) to the right side restores it on the whole grid. The claim survives.

items.label: eq:vysyvat
items.book_statement: Bounds the exponential part: ∫_{T₀}^∞e^{−ct}((1/2π)log(qt/2π) + 1/(4t))dt ≤ (2πc)^{−1}(log T₀ + log(q/2π) + (1/c + π/2)/T₀)e^{−cT₀}, c = 0.1598, from ∫_y^∞(log t + c₁/t)e^{−ct}dt ≤ (log y + (1/c + c₁)/y)e^{−cy}/c.
items.note: Its general inequality (with c = π/4, c₁ = 0) is quoted again ('We recall (9.36)') in the proof of Prop 9.5.1, on [H]'s main line via Prop 7.1.5. Lean's Prop 9.5.1 (TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.prop_9_5_1) does not use it: its high-zero tails come from TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.phi1_tail, TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.phi2_tail and TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.sum_geom_windows.

erratum.description: Misprints in the middle line: the coefficient of ∫e^{−ct}dt should be log(q/2π)/(2π), not log(q/2π)/(2πc), and the relation signs are swapped (the first step is an identity; the last uses E₁(x) ≤ e^{−x}/x, so it is '≤'). Read literally, the middle line lies below the left side when q < 2π. The final bound is correct.

items.label: eq:haroldo

erratum.description: Two gaps. (i) The step uses Lemma 9.1.3's clause for real decreasing f, which is false. (ii) Lemma 9.1.3 counts only zeros with Im ρ > T₀. The sum here is over |Im ρ| > T₀ with f bounding a single term, and unlike (9.33) and (9.66), §9.5 does not pair zeros, so the bound must be doubled. Repaired, the tail at the book's H = 200, T₀ = 450 is about 17 times (9.73)'s first line. So Prop 9.5.1, and through (9.93) the E₁ form of Prop 7.1.5, are not established; the E₂ form survives. items.note: Lean splits off the non-coprime n first and expands in characters mod q, the route the book calls 'more obvious'. The O* term should carry |η(p^α/x)|.
items.evidence: Lean: ‖S_{η₊}(α) − S′_q(α)‖ ≤ 10⁻¹⁵x and ‖S_{η_*} − S′_q‖ ≤ 10⁻¹²x/κ for q ≤ 3·10⁵, x ≥ 4.9·10²⁶, then characters mod q on coprime sums; book: primitive-character identity with O* term.

lean.note: Analogue of the O* term: |S_{η₊}(α) − S′_q(α)| ≤ 10⁻¹⁵x, S′_q over (n,q)=1, for q ≤ 3·10⁵, x ≥ 4.9·10²⁶.
The same for η_*: |S_{η_*} − S′_q| ≤ 10⁻¹²·x/κ.
Dual form for coprime-supported sums: Σ_b ψ(b)S(b/q+β) = τ(ψ)S_{ψ⁻¹}(β). Through totient_mul_sum_units it gives the ℓ² bound over b used on the major arcs (arc_chars, arc_chars_star).
The main identity of (10.8) for coprime-supported coefficients, with characters mod q: φ(q)S(b/q+β) = Σ_ψ ψ(b⁻¹)τ(ψ)S_{ψ⁻¹}(β). The theorem itself states only the norm inequality.
Passes to the primitive character: S_ψ = S_{ψ*} on the coprime part. S_{ψ*} over all n then differs by at most D (norm_Schar_le, Schar_sub).
Pointwise consequence |S(b/q+β)| ≤ D + |M|/φ(q) + √q(E + D), i.e. the √q-lossy 'more obvious way'. Used only for the minor-arc base gap, not by major_total.

erratum.description: The O* term is printed with η(p^α/x), but the proof gives |η(p^α/x)|: it bounds |1 − μ((q,n^∞))/φ((q,n^∞))|·Λ(n)|η(n/x)| by 2Λ(n)|η(n/x)|. Since (10.1) allows complex η, and the η₊ used later takes negative values, the printed term is not literally the bound that is proved. Harmless: read |η|. The same slip recurs in (10.11) and in LS_η of (10.38).

items.label: eq:shangh

items.evidence: Lean: Schar χ a β = Σ' a(n)χ(n)e(nβ), with a(n) = Λ(n)η(n/x); book: same with β = δ/x.

lean.note: Schar χ a β = Σ' a(n)χ(n)e(nβ); with a(n) = Λ(n)η(n/x), β = δ/x it is S_{η,χ}(δ/x,x).
Σ Λ(n)χ(n)φ(n/x) for a complex weight φ. Taking φ(t) = e(δt)η(t) gives S_{η,χ}(δ/x,x); used in the explicit-formula files.
The case η(t) = t²e^{−t²/2}.
Bridges the Schar and Ssum encodings.

items.label: eq:orgor
items.book_statement: Product of three copies of (10.8): S_{η₁}S_{η₂}S_{η₃}(α)e(−Nα) as a triple sum over χ₁,χ₂,χ₃ mod q of τ(χ̄_j)χ_j(a)S_{η_j,χ_j*}(δ/x,x), times e(−Na/q)e(−δN/x)/φ(q)³.
items.note: Lean forms no triple character sum: only the principal term of each factor is kept and the rest is bounded in ℓ² over b.
items.evidence: Lean: S₊²S_* − M₊²M_* = S₊²R_* + M_*R₊(S₊+M₊) with M = μ(q)/φ(q)·η̂(−βx)x (sum_cubic_error); book: full triple character expansion.

lean.note: No triple character sum: each factor keeps its principal term M; exact identity S₊²S_* − M₊²M_* = S₊²(S_*−M_*) + M_*(S₊−M₊)(S₊+M₊).

The principal-character coefficient: (μ(q)/φ(q))³Σ_{b∈Bset q} e(−Nb/q) = coefN N q. That is ∏_{p|q} a_p(N), with a_p(N) = (1 − [p|N]p)/(p−1)³, for squarefree q, and 0 otherwise.

items.label: eq:joko

For each b, |S_{η_*}(b/q+β) − M_*|² ≤ 1.34·10⁻¹¹(x/κ)². The bound is one term of the ℓ² sum over b.
Exact algebraic expansion of the product, so no cross terms are lost.

The proof bounds that part by C_{φ,0,K}x = 1.04488x∫_0^{1/K}φ (Cor C.1.3), and the second case keeps it inside h_φ. Since φ may be any continuous L¹ function, it can put its mass at tiny w, and the printed bound then fails by large factors. Adding C_{φ,0,K}/|φ|₁ to g_{x,φ} restores it; see Eq 11.18. (2) Proof gap: the δ ↦ wδ erratum, which the repo's NOTES.md says Helfgott reported himself. At scale wx the approximation is 2α = a/q + (wδ)/(wx). For w < 1, Thm 3.1.1 then gives only g_{wx}(r_w) with r_w = max(1,w|δ|/8)q. When |δ| > 8 this r_w is smaller than r, so the bound is weaker than the g_{wx}(r) the proof uses. K = 1 turns the correction term of R_{x,K,φ,t} into 0/0 (its limit is 0). R_{x/K,2r} needs 9(x/K)^{1/3}/(4.008r) > 1, i.e. r < 2.2455(x/K)^{1/3}. erratum.description: Step (12.29) covers small R by Lemma 12.2.3 with σ = c₊ = 1.36. But the lemma bounds the quotient by (log Q₀ + σ)/(log Q + 1.312), which is weaker than (12.23)'s (log Q₀ + 1.36)/(log Q + c_E). Applying the lemma as stated needs σ <= 1.36 − ω(ρ)(c_E − 1.312) ≈ 1.34709. Then c(c₊) falls by 0.35% and ϖ₀ by about 0.48%, and the printed comparison ϖ₀ > λ at q = 3.3·10⁹ (210 ∤ q) fails. A careful repair avoids this: re-deriving the lemma against log Q + c_E costs less (c ≈ 0.90918), both printed comparisons still hold, and the printed λ bound is loose anyway. The claim itself is not refuted, and its thresholds survive a careful repair.

items.label: lem:jardinbota
items.book_statement: Summation-by-parts majorant: for f, g ≥ 0 on {a,…,b} whose partial sums of f are bounded by a continuous, piecewise differentiable, non-decreasing F, Σ f(n)g(n) ≤ (max_{n≥a} g)·F(a) + ∫_a^b (max_{n≥u} g(n)) F′(u) du.
items.note: Its only use is Prop 13.1.2, where g is non-increasing, so the restriction costs nothing. [H]'s general-g form follows by applying abel_le to the running maximum h(n) = max_{m≥n} g(m) when f ≥ 0. Proved by induction, no sorry, none of the five hypotheses used. [H]'s proof goes through the misprinted (13.3).

lean.note: Assumes g non-increasing on [a,b] with g(b) ≥ 0 instead of using the running maximum; no sign condition on f, no regularity or monotonicity of F, partial-sum bound only at integers. Conclusion g(a)F(a) + Σ_{a<n≤b} g(n)(F(n)−F(n−1)) equals [H]'s integral for non-increasing g.

lean.note: Hypothesis hS: Σ_{m∈[a,n]} f(m) ≤ F(n) for integers a ≤ n ≤ b only. Equivalent to (13.1) when F is non-decreasing; Lean does not assume F monotone, so its hypothesis is weaker.
Discharges hS with F = H − I₀: this is (13.8) and the display after it.

items.note: The printed ≤ holds with equality (Abel's identity), so it is correct as stated. [H] then applies it with the running maximum h in place of g; in Lean g is already non-increasing.

erratum.description: The sentence before (14.47) recalls 'c⁻ = 0.6294 > 0', a stale 2013 value; the book's c⁻ is 0.6394 (Thm 13.2.1, (14.37)). Only c⁻ > 0 is used. items.note: Lean's constant is 1.0376 in place of 1.00948 (from Mexpr ≤ 1.037, t = 5·10⁻⁴); the final margin is 1.049 − 1.0376. The book's argument does not give 1.00948 (Thm 3.1.1's 0.5 should be 0.8102, and the Thm 13.2.1 scale gap); Lean closes this via repair 3.
items.evidence: Lean: same integral ≤ 1.0376x²/κ for N ≥ 10²⁷ (x ≥ 4.9·10²⁶); book: ≤ 1.00948x²/κ.

lean.note: N ≥ 10²⁷, x = xOf N: ∫_{(0,1]∖𝔐_{8,r0}(x)}|S_{η*}||S_{η+}|² ≤ 1.0376x²/κ; Facts PlattGRH, RamareMoebius.

erratum.description: The book's argument does not establish 1.00948, for two reasons. First, it is Thm 13.2.1 evaluated with g built on Thm 3.1.1's constant 0.5, which the proof of Thm 3.1.1 does not give ((6.77) yields 0.81020). Second, Thm 13.2.1's ℓ∞ input is proved only off the arcs at scale y = x/κ, while Z_{r₀}, its ℓ² input and J use the scale-x arcs, which are κ times narrower (the Thm 13.2.1 scale mix-up). The main theorem still holds, but not through the book's argument. The 0.8102 correction alone gives about 1.0356 in [H]'s scheme. The scale gap is closed by repair 3 (fresh Dirichlet approximations, levels to ≈ x^{0.3}, base gap via Cor 7.1.3), which Lean proves with 1.0376 < 1.049 ≤ 1.058259.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: (6.77)'s constant is 0.81020, not 0.49911 (so not 0.5), and with it the section 14.3 chain gives Z = 1.0384 x^2/kappa > 1.00948 (still < 1.058259); the scale issue is not numerical and is not checked.
check.note: In (6.77) the constant is log 2/(2√ρ) + (√ρ/2)·0.67506 = 0.81020, not the printed (1/2)(log 2/√ρ + (√ρ/2)·0.67506) = 0.49911. So Thm 3.1.1's +0.5 is not proved. With 0.8102, starting from the printed M = 0.80508, the §14.3 chain gives Z ≈ 1.0384x²/κ > 1.00948, though still < 1.058259. The claim's 1.0356 comes from a full re-run whose M starts at 0.80287. The scale mix-up (part 2 of the claim) is not numerical and was not checked.
