items.label: eq:clager
items.book_statement: Defines the auxiliary weight h(t) = t²(2−t)³e^{t−1/2} on [0,2], zero elsewhere. Its band-limited version h_H is what η₊ is built from. A verbatim restatement of (7.5).
items.note: 'As before' points to (7.5). But (11.2) uses the letter h for t³(2−t)³e^{t−1/2}, a different function, and that clash is the source of the (A.2) misprint. Lean has only this h (hBase), so the clash does not arise there. Check: ∫₀² h(t)/t dt = 2.02055185 = 92e^{−1/2} − 12e^{3/2}, the C₀ of (A.9), which confirms the t² version.

lean.note: Same formula on Icc 0 2, zero elsewhere.
Smooth formula u²(2−u)³e^{u−1/2} on all of ℝ. Helfgott.hBase_eq_hP (HHBound.lean:215-216) identifies it with hBase on [0,2]; it is used for derivatives.
g(u) = h(e^u), the form in log coordinates. Its Fourier transform ĝ(ξ) = Mh(−2πiξ) takes the place of Mh(iτ) everywhere in Lean.

items.label: eq:cleoapp
items.book_statement: Defines the target weight η_◦(t) = t³(2−t)³e^{−(t−1)²/2} on [0,2], zero elsewhere, which η₊ approximates. It also writes η_◦ as h·η_♡, with η_♡(t) = e^{−t²/2}.
items.note: Restates (7.3) and (11.3). Lean's η_◦ is defined on ℝ and is zero off [0,2] (MajorArcs.etaO_of_nonpos). NOTES.md writes the correct relation η◦(t) = h(t)te^{−t²/2} but does not flag the misprint.

lean.note: The indicator of [0,2] times P0, i.e. the explicit right-hand side. Its docstring cites [H, (11.3)], which is correct.
For t > 0, η_◦(t) = hBase(t)·t·e^{−t²/2}. This is the corrected first equality (h·η_♦, not h·η_♡).

erratum.description: With the h of (A.1), the middle expression h(t)η_♡(t) is false: it equals t²(2−t)³e^{−(t−1)²/2} = η_◦(t)/t. It should read h(t)·t·η_♡(t) = h(t)η_♦(t), with η_♦(t) = te^{−t²/2}; the book itself uses this in (A.19) and (A.34). The error is harmless, because the explicit right-hand side is the definition used everywhere. It is left over from (11.3), where h is the t³(2−t)³e^{t−1/2} of (11.2).

items.label: eq:patra
items.book_statement: Defines the smoothing η₊(t) = h_H(t)·t·e^{−t²/2}: the band-limited h_H takes the place of h in η∘(t) = h(t)·t·e^{−t²/2}, so η₊ approximates η∘ (η₊ itself is not band-limited). H > 0 is fixed later (H = 200). Restates (7.4).
items.note: The proof of Prop 9.4.2 (expform.tex:1661) cites (A.3) for η₊(0) = 0. Lean's bounds on η₊ hold for H = 200 only and have cruder constants: Helfgott.abs_etaPlus_le_A gives |η₊| ≤ 1.94, against 1.079955 from (A.38)/(14.3). Lemmas about h_H, such as Helfgott.abs_hH_le_eps, are generic in H. η₊ itself is not band-limited. By (2.9) and (A.6), Mη₊(iτ) = (1/2π)∫_{−H}^{H} Mh(ir)Mη♦(i(τ−r))dr with η♦(t) = te^{−t²/2}, which does not vanish for |τ| > H; §9.4 says its decay is that of M(te^{−t²/2}) delayed by H. Numerically, for H = 5: |Mη₊(iτ)| = 0.0705 at τ = 6 and 2.1·10⁻³ at τ = 10.

lean.note: hH 200 t · t · e^{−t²/2}: H is fixed at the book's value 200 (Thm 7.1.2, Ch. 14), while hH itself is generic in H.
Lean defines η₊ on ℝ and it vanishes for t ≤ 0 (the book's η₊ maps [0,∞) → ℝ). This gives η₊(0) = 0, which the proof of Prop 9.4.2 takes from (A.3).

items.label: eq:dirich
items.book_statement: Defines the kernel F_H(y) = sin(H log y)/(π log y) and h_H = h ∗_M F_H, that is, h_H(t) = ∫₀^∞ h(t/y)F_H(y)dy/y, for a positive constant H. A restatement of (7.6).
items.note: Lean defines hH directly by the integral, not through Helfgott.mellinConv (which is used for η_*). MajorArcs.hH_of_neg gives h_H(t) = 0 for t < 0. The Lean docstrings silently correct the t/y slips.

lean.note: Same formula. At y = 1, Lean's convention x/0 = 0 gives the value 0 instead of the limit H/π; this is a null set.
∫_{y>0} h(t/y)F_H(y)/y, the book's integral. For t > 0 the integrand is absolutely integrable (zero for y < t/2, O(y⁻³) as y → ∞), so the Bochner integral gives the book's value.
For t > 0, h_H(t) = ∫ h(u)F_H(t/u)du/u, i.e. (h ∗_M F_H)(t) in the sense of (2.7). The integrand is that of Helfgott.mellinConv, although hH is not defined through it.
In log coordinates: h_H(t) = ∫ g(log t − v)·sH(v)dv, where Helfgott.sH (HHBound.lean:19-20) is the continuous version of F_H(e^v) = sin(Hv)/(πv).

erratum.description: Both lines have a wrong variable. In 'F_H(t) = sin(H log y)/(π log y)' the left side should be F_H(y), and 'h_H(t) = (h ∗_M F_H)(y)' should end in (t). Harmless: the final integral is right. The same misprint is in (7.6) and in 1305.2897v4 (B.4).

items.book_statement: For real τ, the Mellin transform of F_H on the imaginary axis is 1 for |τ| < H, 1/2 at |τ| = H and 0 for |τ| > H, because F_H is a Dirichlet kernel in the variable log y.
items.note: Checked numerically: Re MF_H(iτ) = (1/π)[Si((H+τ)R) + Si((H−τ)R)] tends to 1.000, 0.500 and 0.000 for τ/H = 0.5, 1 and 1.5 (R = 10⁶). The integral converges only conditionally (sinc ∉ L¹). At |τ| = H its imaginary part ∫sin²(Hv)/(πv)dv diverges on each half-line, so the value 1/2 is a symmetric principal value. This concerns a null set, and the Lean route needs none of it.

lean.note: The dual identity sin(Hv)/(πv) = ∫_{|ξ|≤H/2π} e(ξv)dξ (H > 0, v ≠ 0): the kernel is the inverse Fourier transform of an indicator. It is elementary and avoids the conditionally convergent MF_H(iτ).
Fubini together with sH_eq_integral gives the band-limitation (A.6) directly; MF_H(iτ) is never computed.
(H/π)·sinc(Hv), the continuous version of F_H(e^v).

items.label: eq:karmor
items.book_statement: Hence Mh_H(iτ) equals Mh(iτ) for |τ| < H, half of it at |τ| = H, and 0 for |τ| > H. On the imaginary axis, h_H is h with its Mellin transform cut off outside [−H, H].
items.note: Checked with H = 5: h_H(t) computed from (A.4) equals (1/2π)∫_{−H}^{H}Mh(iτ)t^{−iτ}dτ to 6 digits at t = 0.3, 1, 1.7, 2.5 (1.563929 at t = 1). Mh_H(iτ) is not an absolutely convergent integral: h_H(e^u) ≈ Im(e^{iHu}Mh(−iH))/(πu) as |u| → ∞ (H = 5, u = 40: −2.193e−3 vs −2.165e−3; |Mh(200i)| = 5.37e−7 ≠ 0). So (A.6) holds in the L² / principal-value sense. Used in (A.20), (A.29), (A.31) and Lemma 9.4.1.

lean.note: For H, t > 0: h_H(t) = ∫_{|ξ|≤H/2π} e(ξ log t)ĝ(ξ)dξ, where ĝ(ξ) = Mh(−2πiξ). This is (A.6) in Fourier-inversion form (τ = −2πξ), proved by Fubini rather than via (2.8).
h_H(t) = 𝓕(Kc H)(−log t), with Kc H = ĝ·1_{[−H/2π,H/2π]} (MajorArcs.Kc, l. 296-297). The cutoff interval is closed, so there is no factor ½ at |τ| = H; this is a null set.
The H = 200 instance (Explicit.hHc, aH = 200/2π) used for Ch. 9.
The Plancherel consequence ‖g − g_H‖₂² = ∫_{|ξ|>H/2π}|ĝ|², the analogue of (A.20).
M(h_H·g)(s) = ∫_{|ξ|≤aH} ĝ(ξ)Mg(s+2πiξ)dξ: the step combining (2.9) and (A.6) in §§9.4–9.5 and §§A.3–A.4.

items.label: eq:dotorwho
items.book_statement: Up to four integrations by parts for the Mellin transform of a compactly supported φ, C² and piecewise C⁴, with φ^{(k)}(t)t^{k−1} = O(1) at 0⁺: Mφ(s) = (−1)^k∫φ^{(k)}(x)x^{s+k−1}dx/(s(s+1)⋯(s+k−1)), k ≤ 4, Re s > −1, s ≠ 0.
items.note: Lean never states (A.7) and never forms the Mellin transform of h. It works with g(u) = h(e^u) and Mathlib's Fourier transform, for which Mh(ir) = ĝ(−r/2π) (checked numerically). In the book, (A.7) gives the pointwise decay (A.8) with constants C₀…C₄. That bound feeds (A.17)/(A.18) (L¹ norms of Mh(it), used in Ch. 9 at expform.tex:1533 and 1910, and in §A.3–A.4) and (A.21)–(A.24) (∫_H^∞|Mh|² ≤ C₄²/(7H⁷), hence |η₊−η◦|₂ ≤ 274.86/H^{7/2}). Lean fills these roles with different arguments. For the tails it uses the L² Plancherel bounds above, with ‖g′‖₂² ≤ 19.5 and ‖g″‖₂² ≤ 368 in place of C₄. For the L¹ role it uses the trivial bound |ĝ| ≤ C_g = ∫|g| = C₀ over |ξ| ≤ 100/π (TernaryGoldbach.Explicit.norm_mellin_fP_le), about 128.6 instead of 16.19. The only overlap with (A.7) is its k = 1 case for φ = h on Re s = 0, and Lean takes that from Mathlib (Real.fourier_deriv, Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/FourierTransformDeriv.lean:792) rather than proving it. Applying the rule a second time gives M[(x d/dx)²h] = s²Mh, not the book's k = 2 step s(s+1)Mh: at s = 3i the two are −5.996+2.346i and −5.214+4.345i. The k = 3, 4 steps, the distributional h⁽⁴⁾, Re s ≠ 0 and general φ have no counterpart. TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.tail_fourier_le_deriv2 is a general-W L² tail of the same Plancherel type, but it is used for other weights. Hence 'replaced', not 'inlined'.

lean.note: Plancherel tail ∫_{|ξ|>H/2π}|ĝ|² ≤ ‖g′‖₂²/H² ≤ 19.5/H² for g(u) = h(e^u). Its only integration by parts is Mathlib's Real.fourier_deriv (line 446, applied at 462): 𝓕(g′)(ξ) = 2πiξ·ĝ(ξ). That is ∫h′(x)x^s dx = −s·Mh(s) at s = −2πiξ, the k = 1 case of (A.7) for φ = h and Re s = 0 only. It feeds the crude (A.23)-type bound integral_sq_etaPlus_sub_etaO_le.

Sharper tail ≤ ‖g″‖₂²/H⁴ ≤ 368/H⁴, from Real.fourier_deriv applied twice (lines 230–233, 248–249): 𝓕(g″) = (2πiξ)²ĝ. In Mellin terms this is M[(x d/dx)²h](s) = s²Mh(s), not the book's k = 2 step ∫h″x^{s+1}dx = s(s+1)Mh(s). The main line uses this lemma, through integral_sq_etaPlus_sub_etaO_le' and EtaPlusSqLog, where the book uses (A.8)→(A.21) with C₄. The k = 3, 4 steps and the distributional h⁽⁴⁾ have no counterpart.

items.label: eq:kust
items.note: Lean keeps only the trivial term; the pointwise decay terms are never formalized. Their use in (A.21)–(A.23) is replaced by Plancherel tails in log coordinates. Their use in (A.17) is replaced by a sup×length bound (2a·C_g). (A.18) is not needed at all.

lean.note: ‖ĝ(ξ)‖ ≤ C_g, i.e. |Mh(ir)| ≤ C_0 for all r (C_g = C_0, see (A.9)). Only the first term of the minimum.

Replaces the decay terms where (A.21) uses them: ∫_{|ξ|>H/2π}|ĝ|² ≤ ‖g′‖₂²/H² ≤ 19.5/H². At H = 200 it gives the crude ‖η₊−η◦‖₂² ≤ 19.5/(2·200²) (integral_sq_etaPlus_sub_etaO_le). Lean uses that only for the tail of η̂₊ (EtaPlusL2.tail_etaPlus_le) in the truncated integral ∫_{|ξ|<T}|η̂₊|² (integral_fourier_etaPlus_Ioo_bounds, used in L2Major). Lean's ‖η₊‖₂² comes from (9.94) instead.

Sharper tail ≤ ‖g″‖₂²/H⁴ ≤ 368/H⁴. It gives ‖η₊−η◦‖₂² ≤ 368/(2·200⁴) (integral_sq_etaPlus_sub_etaO_le', used in MajorTotal) and the O(H⁻⁴) tails in Lean's proof of (9.94) (MajorArcs/EtaPlusSqLog.lean). This is Lean's analogue of (A.23)/(14.5).

erratum.description: The left side is printed Mh(it), a complex number; it should be |Mh(it)|. With the absolute value the bound is correct.

items.label: eq:nessu0
items.note: Recomputed: 2.0205518495054971. In the book C_0 only feeds (A.17)/(A.18). In Lean it is load-bearing: |ĝ| ≤ C_g, and C_g·2a ≤ 129.24 (cA_le) bounds the Mellin transforms of η₊e(δ·) and η₊² in Lean's versions of Thm 7.1.4 and Prop 7.1.5.

lean.note: C_g := ∫|g(u)|du with g(u) = h(e^u). It equals the book's C_0 = ∫_0^∞|h(x)|dx/x under x = e^u.
C_g = ∫_0^2 t(2−t)³e^{t−1/2}dt (the change of variables, via integral_comp_exp).
C_g = 92e^{−1/2} − 12e^{3/2}, from the antiderivative (−t⁴+10t³−42t²+92t−92)e^{t−1/2}.
The decimal is weakened to C_g ≤ 2.03 (book: 2.02055184…).

items.label: eq:nessu1
items.book_statement: Because h′ > 0 on (0,1) and h′ < 0 on (1,2) (H_1 vanishes at −4, 0, 1, 2), C_1 = ∫|h′| is the total variation of h: 2h(1) = 2√e.
items.note: Lean has (A.10) in pre-limit form. There the value enters a sup bound for h_H, which plays the role of the book's §A.5, rather than the decay of Mh.

lean.note: ∫_ε^2|h′| = 2e^{1/2} − h(ε) for 0 < ε ≤ 1, proved exactly as in the book (sign on [ε,1] and [1,2], then telescoping). Letting ε → 0 gives C_1 = 2√e; Lean never takes that limit.
h′(u) = e^{u−1/2}u(2−u)²(1−u)(4+u), checked by hasDerivAt_hP. This factorization is behind the zeros −4, 0, 1, 2.
Uses 2√e as the total variation of h to get |h_H(t)| ≤ 5Hε²/π + (6/π)e^{1/2}, hence |h₂₀₀| ≤ 3.15.

items.label: eq:depard
items.book_statement: Numerical zeros of h″ in (0,2), certified by sign changes: α_{2,1} ≈ 0.48756597185712, α_{2,2} ≈ 1.48777169309489. H_2 also vanishes at 2 and at two points outside [0,2].
items.note: The roots serve C_2 (A.12) and |h′|_∞ = |h′(α_{2,2})| in (A.37). Lean needs neither: its sup bound on h_H uses the total variation 2√e. Lean has h″ only as an explicit formula (TernaryGoldbach.MajorArcs.hP'', HHFourier2.lean:23). It is used for ‖g″‖₂² ≤ 368 and for the weights' second derivatives in EtaPlusSqLog (k0'', k1''), and its zeros are never located. Recomputed: 0.4875659718571249678…, 1.4877716930948954385…; the other real zeros are ≈ −1.780 and −6.195.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '0.48756','1.4877','hP'' .* = 0' (only hP''_two in HHFourier2.lean:43), zeros of h'' in MajorArcs/HHFourier*.lean, index docs '(A.11)'.

items.label: eq:nessu2
items.book_statement: Splitting at α_{2,1} and α_{2,2} (h″ has signs +, −, +) and integrating by parts once gives C_2 = ∫|h″(x)|x dx = 2Σ_{j=1,2}(−1)^{j+1}(α_{2,j}h′(α_{2,j}) − h(α_{2,j})) ≈ 10.79195821037.
items.note: In the book C_2 enters only via (A.17)/(A.18). Lean replaces (A.17) by a bound that uses C_0 alone and does not need (A.18). Recomputed 10.7919582103733, both by the book's formula and by direct quadrature. The telescoping is correct, since x h′ − h vanishes at 0 and 2.

verification.absence_searched_at_P: '10.79','C_2/C₂' (only Explicit C₃ = Σ Λ(n)n^{-3/2}, unrelated), '|hP''| * x', index docs '(A.12)'.

items.book_statement: Same method for C_3 = ∫|h‴(x)|x²dx: with the zeros α_{3,1}, α_{3,2} of h‴ in (0,2) (signs −, +, −), two integrations by parts give 2Σ_{j=1,2}(−1)^j(α²h″(α) − 2αh′(α) + 2h(α)) at α = α_{3,j}.
items.note: Not needed in Lean, since C_3 feeds only (A.17)/(A.18). The algebra is right: F = x²h″ − 2xh′ + 2h vanishes at 0 and 2, so the alternating sum telescopes to 2(F(α_{3,2}) − F(α_{3,1})). The sign pattern of H_3 is confirmed.

erratum.description: In the display giving the roots, α_{3,2} is printed 1.80999654602916…; the zero of H_3 is 1.80999654602918…. The second line of (A.13) also puts 'dx' outside the bracket. Both are harmless: C_3 is insensitive to small errors in α (the integrand vanishes at the roots), and (A.14) is right.

items.label: eq:marpales
items.book_statement: Integrating the piecewise minimum in (A.8) over t (using |t+ki| ≥ |t| and breakpoints C_{k+1}/C_k) gives ∫_ℝ|Mh(it)|dt ≤ 16.1939176.
items.note: The book uses (A.17) in Lemma 9.4.1, in (9.85) for η₊², and for (A.28). Lean never bounds an L¹ norm of Mh. Since Mh_H is supported on |r| ≤ H, it uses sup|ĝ| times length: (1/2π)∫_{−H}^{H}|Mh| ≤ 2a·C_0 = 128.6. That is about 50 times the book's 2.5773, and it suffices.

lean.note: Lean's analogue of Lemma 9.4.1: bounds |M(η₊e(δ·))(s)| above T₀ with the factor C_g·2a where the book uses |Mh(ir)|₁/2π from (A.17).
|∫_{|ξ|≤a} ĝF| ≤ C_g·sup|F|·2a: the generic sup×length estimate that replaces the L¹ norm of Mh_H.
C_g·2a ≤ 129.24, against the book's (1/2π)|Mh|₁ ≤ 2.5773 (true value ≈ 1.9097).
(C_g·2a)² ≤ 16703, used for M(η₊²) on the Prop 7.1.5 route, where (9.85) uses |Mh_H|₁²/2π ≤ 41.73727.
∫(log v)²η₊² ≤ 1.129 via |h_H| ≤ 3.15. It replaces the book's (A.28), |η₊ log|₂ ≤ 0.8299818, which is derived from (A.17).

erratum.description: The derivation writes |Mh(it)|₁ = 2∫_0^∞ Mh(it)dt, without the absolute value in the integrand. The bound (A.17) itself is correct.

items.label: eq:estor
items.book_statement: Since η₊ = h_H·te^{−t²/2} and η◦ = h·te^{−t²/2}, |η₊ − η◦|₂² = ∫|h_H − h|²t²e^{−t²}dt ≤ (max_{t≥0} t³e^{−t²})·∫₀^∞|h_H − h|² dt/t. The maximum is (3/2)^{3/2}e^{−3/2}.
items.note: In u = log t the Lean identity is exact (t³e^{−t²} = Ew(u)); only the constant 1/2 > 0.40992 is weaker. The same step recurs as hQ0 in integral_etaPlus_sq_log (EtaPlusSqLog.lean:933–939, via Ew_le).

lean.note: H = 200. Substitutes t = eᵘ and rewrites eᵘ(η₊ − η◦)²(eᵘ) = |g(u) − g_H(u)|²·e^{3u}e^{−e^{2u}} (hpt, via hH_eq_fourier_K). Then bounds the weight by 1/2, where the book's exact maximum is 0.409916.
Only the maximum step: s³e^{−s²} ≤ 1/2 for s ≥ 0, instead of (3/2)^{3/2}e^{−3/2} = 0.40992.
The same step in the crude 19.5/(2·200²) version.

items.label: eq:sev
items.book_statement: Mellin isometry (2.6) at σ = 0, with Mh_H(it) equal to Mh(it) truncated to |t| ≤ H: ∫₀^∞|h_H − h|² dt/t = (1/2π)∫|Mh_H(it) − Mh(it)|² dt = (1/π)∫_H^∞|Mh(it)|² dt.
items.note: The Lean proof does not need g_H ∈ L¹, which is false: ĝ_H jumps at ±H/2π (|Mh(200i)| = 5.37·10⁻⁷ ≠ 0), so g_H decays only like 1/|u|. It uses Plancherel for g and for ĝ·1_{[−a,a]} plus the cross term (integral_cross). The book's isometry likewise holds here only in the L² sense, not under the ℓ¹∩ℓ² sufficient condition stated after (2.6).

lean.note: For any real H: ∫|g(u) − 𝓕(K_H)(−u)|² du = ∫_{|ξ|>H/2π}|ĝ(ξ)|² dξ, where g(u) = h(eᵘ). Since Mh(iτ) = ĝ(−τ/2π), this is (A.20) in u = log t, keeping both tails instead of using |Mh(−iτ)| = |Mh(iτ)|.
Identifies 𝓕(K_H)(−log t) with h_H(t) for H, t > 0. This is the truncation property (A.6) that the second equality rests on.

items.label: eq:shei
items.book_statement: From the decay bound (A.8), |Mh(it)| ≤ C₄/t⁴, so the tail satisfies ∫_H^∞|Mh(it)|² dt ≤ ∫_H^∞ C₄²t⁻⁸ dt = C₄²/(7H⁷).
items.note: Not comparable with the book's bound: Lean's is better for H < 7.94 and the book's beyond. At H = 200 they give 7.23·10⁻⁷ and 4.52·10⁻¹¹. The printed C₄ = 2013.18185012 from (A.15) overestimates the true 1896.0209, so (A.21) holds as printed.

lean.note: Any H > 0: ∫_{|ξ|>H/2π}|ĝ|² ≤ ‖g″‖₂²/H⁴ ≤ 368/H⁴, i.e. ∫_H^∞|Mh(it)|² ≤ 368π/H⁴. Plancherel for g″ (two derivatives in L²) replaces four pointwise integrations by parts. This is the main-line version.
‖g″‖₂² = ∫₀² t(th″ + h′)² dt ≤ 368 (true value 142.61). It plays the role of C₄².
Cruder bound 19.5/H², via ‖g′‖₂² ≤ 19.5 (true value 6.9233). Used only through integral_sq_etaPlus_sub_etaO_le and tail_etaPlus_le.

items.label: eq:sevshei
items.book_statement: Combining (A.20) and (A.21): ∫₀^∞|h_H(t) − h(t)|² dt/t ≤ C₄²/(7πH⁷).
items.note: The book's bound holds for every H > 0 and feeds both (A.23) and (A.24). Lean has only H = 200, with 368/H⁴ in place of C₄²/(7πH⁷).

lean.note: H = 200 only: ∫(h₂₀₀(eᵘ) − h(eᵘ))² du ≤ 368/200⁴ = 2.3·10⁻⁷, against the book's 1.44·10⁻¹¹ at H = 200. Proof: integral_norm_sq_gC_sub plus tail_fourier_gC_le'.
The same combination inline. The crude version uses 19.5/200² instead (HHFourier.lean:549–552).

items.label: eq:impath
items.note: Lean proves only H = 200 with a weaker constant (decay H⁻² rather than H^{-7/2}); it suffices because the (9.94) cross terms are bounded by Parseval.

lean.note: Crude H = 200 bound ‖η+ − η◦‖₂² ≤ 19.5/(2·200²); feeds EtaPlusL2.
Plancherel form ∫|η̂+ − η̂◦|² ≤ 1.15·10⁻⁷; plays the role of (14.5).

items.label: eq:lozhka
items.book_statement: ∫₀^∞(η₊ − η◦)²|log t| dt ≤ (max_{t≥0} e^{−t²}t³|log t|)·∫|h_H − h|² dt/t. The maximum, found by bisection, is 0.14882234545…, so by (A.22) the integral is ≤ 27427.502/H⁷ = (165.61251/H^{7/2})².
items.note: The book uses (A.24) only in its derivation of (9.94), for the square term. Lean's (9.94) handles the square term the same way, with weaker constants, and the cross terms by Parseval.

lean.note: Step hQ1 (H = 200): |∫(η₊ − η◦)² log t dt| = |∫D²·Ew·u du| ≤ 0.37·368/200⁴ = 8.5·10⁻⁸; the book gives 2.14·10⁻¹² at H = 200. The pointwise step hF is at lines 912–916.
|u|e^{3u}e^{−e^{2u}} ≤ 0.37, i.e. t³e^{−t²}|log t| ≤ 0.37 for t > 0. The book's maximum is 0.1488223455.

erratum.description: The middle term of (A.24), '0.148822346·C₄²/(7π)', drops the factor H⁻⁷ that (A.22) supplies; it should read 0.148822346·C₄²/(7πH⁷). As printed, the next inequality would need the constant 27427.5014 to be ≤ 27427.502/H⁷. That holds only for H ≤ 1 + 3·10⁻⁹ and fails for every larger H, in particular for every H ≥ 25 used in the book. The final bound 27427.502/H⁷ is right.

items.label: eq:mastodon
items.note: Lean fixes H = 200 and bounds ‖η₊‖₂² directly in [0.640204, 0.640208], inside the book's interval; the dependency is reversed (η∘ integrals → (9.94) → ‖η₊‖₂).
items.evidence: Lean at P: 0.640204 ≤ ∫η₊² ≤ 0.640208 (no hypotheses) for H = 200; book: 0.800128 ∓ 274.8569/H^{7/2} for general H.

lean.note: ∫_{t>0} η₊² ≤ 0.6403, i.e. ‖η₊‖₂ ≤ 0.80019; the norm fed to Prop 9.4.2's Lean counterpart.

items.changes_since_2013: 1305.2897v4 (B.25) has only the upper bound. The lower bound 0.800128 − 274.8569/H^{7/2} is new.

items.label: eq:lamia
items.book_statement: |η∘|₂ = √0.640205997… = 0.8001287…, by symbolic integration of t⁶(2−t)⁶e^{−(t−1)²} over [0,2].
items.note: Lean states the book's value to nine digits.

lean.note: 0.640205997 ≤ ∫₀² P0² ≤ 0.640205998, P0 = η∘ on [0,2]; Taylor polynomial for the Gaussian and exact polynomial integration.
Cruder 0.63965 ≤ ∫η∘² ≤ 0.6408, re-derived from ‖η₊‖₂; used for the main-term constant.

items.label: eq:sonamo
items.book_statement: Closed form, with η♦(t) = te^{−t²/2}: |η♦·log|₂² = ∫₀^∞ t²e^{−t²}log²t dt = (√π/32)(8log²2 + 2γ² + π² + 8(γ−2)log 2 − 8γ). Hence |η♦·log|₂ ≤ 0.3220301.
items.note: Checked: the closed form equals Γ″(3/2)/8 = 0.1037033634 and quadrature agrees; its square root 0.32203007 ≤ 0.3220301. It is only an input to (A.28).

lean.note: Never isolates |η♦·log|₂. It bounds log²v·η₊(v)² ≤ (v + 1/v − 2)·3.15²v²e^{−v²} and integrates, implicitly using ∫(v + 1/v − 2)v²e^{−v²} dv = 1 − √π/2 = 0.11377 in place of the book's 0.103703.
log²v ≤ v + v⁻¹ − 2: the elementary inequality that replaces the closed form.

items.label: eq:pamiatka
items.book_statement: By isometry, (Mη₊)′(1/2+it) = (1/2π)·(Mh_H ∗ (Mη♦)′)(t). Young's inequality and |Mh|₁ ≤ 16.1939176 (A.17) then give |η₊·log|₂ ≤ 2.5773421·|η♦·log|₂ ≤ 0.8299818, for every H.
items.note: Checked: 16.1939176/(2π) = 2.5773420 ≤ 2.5773421, and 2.5773421·0.3220301 = 0.8299817 ≤ 0.8299818. The input (A.17) is a valid bound (true |Mh(it)|₁ = 11.9987). For η₊² (Prop 9.5.1) the Lean analogue is integral_log_sq_phi1_sq_le (EtaPlusSqBound.lean).

lean.note: H = 200: ∫₀^∞ log²v·η₊(v)² dv ≤ 1.129, i.e. ‖η₊·log‖₂ ≤ 1.0625; the book has 0.8299818 (squared 0.68887). Proof: |η₊(t)| ≤ 3.15te^{−t²/2} (abs_hH200_le) and log²v ≤ v + 1/v − 2, not Young.
Feeds the bound to Lean's Prop 9.4.2 as ∫|(Mφ)′(1/2+it)|² ≤ 2π·1.129. This is the |η·log|₂ input that the book's Lemma 9.1.4 takes from (A.28).

items.label: eq:lesalpes
items.book_statement: For σ > −2, Cauchy–Schwarz and Plancherel give |η₊(t)t^σ|₁ ≤ |t^{σ+3/2}e^{−t²/2}|₂·|h_H(t)/√t|₂ ≤ |t^{σ+3/2}e^{−t²/2}|₂·|h(t)/√t|₂, since Mh_H(ir) is Mh(ir) cut off at |r| ≤ H.
items.note: A step towards (A.30). Lean needs no ℓ¹ norms of η₊(t)t^σ. Integrability and Mellin convergence come from the pointwise majorant |η₊(t)| ≤ 3.15te^{−t²/2} (MajorArcs.abs_etaPlus_le_gauss, from Helfgott.abs_hH200_le). The explicit formula uses Mellin bounds instead (see (A.30)).

verification.absence_searched_at_P: 'σ + 3/2', Cauchy–Schwarz/Plancherel on η₊ t^σ, 'integral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq', MellinPlancherel*.lean, EtaPlus*.lean, HHFourier*.lean, index docs '(A.29)'.

items.label: eq:paytoplay
items.note: Checked: ∫₀² h²/t = 2.257042946, agreeing with the closed form; its square root 1.50234581 ≤ 1.5023459, and 1.5023459/√2 = 1.06231897 ≤ 1.062319. The book uses (A.30) in Props 9.4.2 and 9.5.1 and, at σ = 0, for |η₊|₁ ≤ 1.062319 in (14.3). Lean's proof of (14.7) uses no |η₊|₁.

lean.note: |η₊(t)| ≤ 3.15·|te^{−t²/2}| (from |h₂₀₀| ≤ 3.15). This gives all the integrability of η₊(t)t^σ (σ > −2) that Lean needs, without the constant 1.062319.
Lean's Prop 9.4.2 explicit formula needs no ℓ¹ norms: neither Lemma 9.1.1's c₀ nor Lemma 9.1.4's |η/√t|₁. It uses |M₊(0)| (norm_mellin_fP_zero) and a bound on ℜs = −1/2 (norm_mellin_fP_vert).

items.label: eq:grabai
items.book_statement: For s = −1/2 + it, Mη₊(s) = (1/2π)∫_{−H}^{H} Mh(ir)Mη♦(s − ir) dr and |s| ≤ 3|s − ir||1 + ir|. Hence |s||Mη₊(s)| ≤ (3/2π)(f∗g)(t), with f(r) = |ir − 1||Mh(ir)| and g(r) = |−1/2 + ir||Mη♦(−1/2 + ir)|.
items.note: On ℜs = −1/2, the explicit formula uses norm_mellin_fP_vert (EtaPlusBound.lean:143). Lean never needs |s||Mη₊(s)| in L².

lean.note: The convolution identity of (A.31)'s first line, for η₊(t)e(δt) and all ℜs > −1: M₊(s) = ∫_{|ξ|≤H/2π} ĝ(ξ)G_δ(s − 1 + 2πiξ) dξ, with r = −2πξ.
Replaces the weighted convolution inequality by a sup bound on −1/2 ≤ ℜs ≤ 2: |M₊(s)| ≤ 2aC_g·300e·e^{−θ′|ℑs|}, using |ĝ| ≤ C_g = 92e^{−1/2} − 12e^{3/2} (the book's C₀).

erratum.description: Misprints in (A.31). The second line has Mη♥(s − ir) where Mη♦(s − ir) is meant: g and the first line use η♦, and Mη♦(s) = Mη♥(s + 1). The first line lacks |·| around the integral, although its left side is real. The final '=' should be '≤', since f is not truncated to [−H, H]. The key inequality |s − ir||ir − 1| ≥ |s|/3 and the conclusion are correct.

items.label: eq:miran
items.book_statement: Plancherel on ℜs = −1/2, (A.31), Young's inequality (|f∗g|₂ ≤ |f|₁|g|₂), |f|₁ ≤ 27.8622803 from (A.18) and |g|₂² = 2π|η♦′|₂² = 3π^{3/2}/4 give |η₊′|₂ ≤ 10.845789.
items.note: The book uses (A.32) only in Props 9.4.2 and 9.5.1, which assume H ≥ 25, so nothing downstream breaks. As printed, with the full-line |f|₁, the proof establishes the constant for no H. Read with f·1_{[−H,H]}, it does so for H ≤ 7.88, and the direct estimate covers H ≥ 1.41. These are float computations, not interval arithmetic.

lean.note: The book needs |η′|₂ for the x^{−1/2} term of Lemma 9.1.1. Lean's explicit formula takes |M₊(−1/2 + iy)| ≤ 2aC_g·300e·e^{−θ′|y|} instead, and Lean never differentiates η₊.
Lean's Prop 9.4.2 bound for χ ≠ 1, built from Mellin bounds; the ζ case is norm_SsumG_fP_zeta_le. For η₊² (Prop 9.5.1) the analogues are norm_SsumG_phi1_le and norm_SsumG_phi2_le.

erratum.description: (A.32) rests on (A.18), |f|₁ = |(r+i)Mh(ir)|₁ ≤ 27.8622803, which is false: (A.18)'s own text bounds the norm by 'two times' a bracket, and 27.8622803 is the bracket itself. With the factor, the argument gives only |η₊′|₂ ≤ 21.69 (≈14.28 with the true |f|₁ ≈ 36.68). The printed bound is nevertheless true, numerically for every H > 0. For H ≤ 7.88 the book's argument works with f truncated to [−H, H], which the integral in (A.31) allows. For H ≥ 1.41 a direct estimate gives it. Where the book uses the bound (H ≥ 25, Props 9.4.2 and 9.5.1), |η₊′|₂ ≤ 1.979.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: the (A.32) route needs |f|_1 <= 27.8622803 but gives 21.6916 with the factor 2 and 14.2771 with the true norm (truncated norm 35.3839 > 27.8622803 at H = 25); the bound itself holds for H >= 25 since |eta_+'|_2 <= 1.9788 there.
check.note: The derivation of (A.32) uses the false (A.18); with the factor 2 it gives 21.6916, with the true norm 14.2771, and the norm of f truncated to [-H,H] already exceeds 27.8622803 for H >= 7.889. The bound |eta_+'|_2 <= 10.845789 is still true where used (H >= 25): a Plancherel estimate gives |eta_+'|_2 <= 1.654548 + 7.82066/H + 7.11149/H^2 <= 1.9788.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: the (A.32) route needs |f|_1 <= 27.8622803 but gives 21.6916 with the factor 2 and 14.2771 with the true norm (truncated norm 35.3839 > 27.8622803 at H = 25); the bound itself holds for H >= 25 since |eta_+'|_2 <= 1.9788 there.

items.label: eq:uzsu

items.label: eq:jorat
items.book_statement: First step toward |η₊|_∞: with η₊ = h_H·η♦ (η♦ = te^{−t²/2}) and η◦ = h·η♦, the triangle inequality and factoring out t give |η₊|_∞ ≤ |η◦|_∞ + |(h−h_H)/t|_∞·|η♦(t)t|_∞; here |η◦|_∞ = 1, |η♦t|_∞ = 2/e.
items.note: Both inequalities are valid, but the second is vacuous: |(h−h_H)/t|_∞ = ∞ because h_H(t) decays only like 1/log(1/t) as t → 0+ (see (A.36)). The step needs η◦ = h·η♦ = t³(2−t)³e^{−(t−1)²/2} (the explicit formula of (A.2), also Lean's MajorArcs.etaO), not the printed 'h(t)η♥(t)'. Lean compares η₊ with η◦ only in ℓ² (MajorArcs/HHFourier.lean), never in ℓ∞.

lean.note: No comparison with η◦: Lean bounds |η₊(t)| = |h₂₀₀(t)|·te^{−t²/2} ≤ 3.15·(1/1.625) ≤ 1.94 directly (abs_hH200_le, mul_exp_neg_sq_half_le).

items.label: eq:narco
items.book_statement: Rewrites h_H(t) as ∫_{t/2}^∞ h(t/y)·sin(H log y)/(π log y) dy/y and, with w = H log y, as ∫_{−H log(2/t)}^∞ h(te^{−w/H})·sin w/(πw) dw, preparing integration by parts against the sine integral Si.
items.note: Verified: with y = e^{w/H}, dy/y = dw/H and F_H(e^{w/H}) = H sin w/(πw), and y = t/2 ↔ w = −H log(2/t). Since h(2) = h(0) = 0, the integration by parts that follows has no boundary terms. hH_eq_conv is the literal statement up to the dummy rescaling v = w/H. hH_eq_u is the equivalent form that Lean actually integrates by parts.

lean.note: For H, t > 0: h_H(t) = ∫_ℝ gL(log t − v)·sH H v dv, where gL(u) = h(e^u) and sH H v = sin(Hv)/(πv), continuous at 0. This is the second form of (A.35) with dummy variable v = w/H. The lower limit −H log(2/t) is implicit, since gL(log t − v) = 0 once te^{−v} > 2. It uses none of the five hypotheses, is in the cone, and feeds hH_eq_fourier.

Substitution y = t/u: h_H(t) = ∫₀^∞ h(u)F_H(t/u)du/u, equivalent to (A.35) via w = H log(t/u). abs_hH_le_eps, Lean's substitute for the (A.36)–(A.38) sup-norm argument, cuts it to u ∈ (0,2] (step h02, lines 324–332). It then integrates by parts against −G_H(log t − log u) = −Si(H log(t/u))/π (hibp, lines 374–387).
Definition h_H(t) = ∫_{(0,∞)} h(t/y)F_H(y)dy/y, the book's first form. The cut y > t/2 is implicit in supp hBase ⊆ [0,2].

items.label: eq:havana
items.book_statement: Claims |h_H(t)−h(t)|/t < |h'|_∞(1 − e^{−1/H} + (4/π)(log H)/H) < |h'|_∞(1 + (4/π)log H)/H, via integration by parts against Si, |Si(x) ∓ π/2| < 2/|x|, and E₁(1/H) < log H for H ≥ e.
items.note: The w > 0 half, the E₁ step (E₁(1/200) = 4.726 < log 200 = 5.298) and the second inequality (1 − e^{−1/H} < 1/H) are fine. A valid substitute is |h−h_H|_∞ ≤ (1/π)∫_H^∞|Mh(iτ)|dτ ≤ 64e^{3/2}/(πH³): each series term has |iτ+k| ≥ τ, so |Mh(iτ)| ≤ 192e^{3/2}/τ⁴. This is nearly sharp: sup|h−h_H| ≈ 1.136e−5 at t = 2 for H = 200, against a bound of 1.1413e−5. The book's own (A.8) with C₄ from (A.15) gives the cruder C₄/(3πH³). Either rescues (A.38) and (A.40)–(A.42) for H ≥ 25. The repo docs do not mention this.

lean.note: |h_H(t)| ≤ 5Hε²/π + (6/π)e^{1/2} for all t > 0, H > 0, 0 < ε ≤ 1. It bounds h_H itself (integration by parts against −G_H, using the total variation 2e^{1/2} of h), not (h_H−h)/t, and is uniform in t, so the flaw never arises.
|G_H(z)| = |Si(Hz)|/π ≤ 3/π, proved from scratch; takes the place of the Abramowitz–Stegun facts and the bounds |Si(x) ∓ π/2| < 2/|x|.

erratum.description: False for small t, so |(h−h_H)/t|_∞ = ∞. The derivative bound t|h'|_∞e^{−w/H}/H is right, but for w < 0 its weight e^{−w/H} = e^{|w|/H} ranges over [1, 2/t], while the next display integrates the w < 0 half as if it were e^{−|w|/H} (the factor 2). In fact h_H(t) − h(t) ≈ |Mh(iH)|·sin(H log(2/t)+θ)/(π log(1/t)) as t → 0+, not O(t). Going down from t = 2, the inequality first fails at t ≈ 9.2·10⁻⁸ (H = 200) and t ≈ 1.08·10⁻⁴ (H = 25); the ratio is unbounded as t → 0+.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: |h - h_H|/t first exceeds the right side of (A.36) near t = 9.21e-08 (H = 200) and t = 0.000108 (H = 25) and grows without bound as t -> 0+ (3657 at t = 1e-12, H = 200), so (A.36) is false for small t.
check.note: (A.36) fails for small t: |h - h_H|/t first exceeds the right side near t = 9.21e-8 (H = 200) and t = 1.08e-4 (H = 25) and grows without bound (3657 at t = 1e-12, H = 200), so |(h - h_H)/t|_oo is infinite. The error is in the w < 0 half of the integration by parts, where the weight e^{-w/H} reaches 2/t.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: |h - h_H|/t first exceeds the right side of (A.36) near t = 9.21e-08 (H = 200) and t = 0.000108 (H = 25) and grows without bound as t -> 0+ (3657 at t = 1e-12, H = 200), so (A.36) is false for small t.

items.label: eq:malgache
items.note: Book uses: the proof of Prop 9.5.1 ((9.75), (9.76), c₀, (9.79), (9.80), H ≥ 25) and, at H = 200, (14.3), which feeds (14.25), (14.28), K_{r,2} of (10.27) and (14.51). The statement survives for every H ≥ 25, which covers all uses (Prop 9.5.1 with H ≥ 25; (14.3) at H = 200): |h−h_H|_∞ ≤ 64e^{3/2}/(πH³) gives |η₊|_∞ ≤ 1 + 64e/(πH³).

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: |(h - h_H)/t|_oo is not bounded by (A.36) (it grows without bound as t -> 0+), so the printed proof of (A.38) fails, but |h - h_H|_oo <= 64e^{3/2}/(pi H^3) gives |eta_+|_oo <= 1.003544 < 1.421007 at H = 25 and the statement holds for all H >= 25.
check.note: The printed proof needs |(h - h_H)/t|_oo, which (A.36) does not bound (it is infinite), so the argument fails. The statement holds for all H >= 25: |h - h_H|_oo <= 64e^{3/2}/(pi H^3) gives |eta_+|_oo <= 1.003544 at H = 25 and 1.0000069 at H = 200.

items.label: eq:rasal
items.book_statement: Repeats (A.34) for three weighted norms: |η₊·w|_∞ ≤ |η◦·w|_∞ + |(h−h_H)/t|_∞·|η♦·t·w|_∞ with weights w(t) = log t, 1/t and t.
items.note: Valid, but every right side is +∞ because |(h−h_H)/t|_∞ = ∞ (see (A.36)); the notation |(h−h_H(t))/t|_∞ mixes a function with its value (harmless). The book needs the log t and 1/t versions only in Prop 9.5.1, which Lean proves by Mellin/Plancherel bounds (prop_9_5_1, MajorArcs/Prop715.lean:300).

lean.note: For w = t Lean factors t|η₊| = |h₂₀₀|·t²e^{−t²/2} ≤ 3.15·0.7358 (phi_le_two_div_e), with no η◦ comparison. Lean has nothing for w = log t or 1/t (not needed).

items.label: eq:dalida
items.book_statement: From the bisection values |η◦(t)log t|_∞ ≤ 0.279491 and |η♦(t)·t log t|_∞ ≤ 0.3811561 with (A.36)–(A.37): |η₊ log t|_∞ ≤ 0.279491 + 1.069456·(1+(4/π)log H)/H.
items.note: Used only in the proof of Prop 9.5.1: (9.75), (9.76), c₀, (9.78) (its 0.4976 is this bound at H = 25), (9.79), (9.80). Lean's prop_9_5_1 has error constant 10⁻⁸, x ≥ 4.9·10²⁶ and RH to height 500, instead of the book's err_{ℓ₂,η₊}.

lean.note: η₊(t)² ≤ 9.9225·t²e^{−t²} (from |h₂₀₀| ≤ 3.15) is the only pointwise input to Lean's Prop 9.5.1; log-weighted norms of η₊² come from moments with log²v ≤ v + 1/v, not from ℓ∞ bounds.
Plancherel data for φ₂ = η₊²·log: |Φ(u)| ≤ 9.93e^{−|u|}, consumed by prop_9_5_1 (MajorArcs/Prop715.lean:300).

erratum.description: Obtained from (A.39) with |(h−h_H)/t|_∞ bounded by (A.36), which fails near t = 0 (that norm is infinite), so the printed proof fails. The bound holds for H ≥ 25, its only use (Prop 9.5.1): |η₊ log t|_∞ ≤ |η◦ log t|_∞ + |h−h_H|_∞·|η♦ log t|_∞ with |h−h_H|_∞ ≤ 64e^{3/2}/(πH³).

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: |(h - h_H)/t|_oo is not bounded by (A.36) (it grows without bound as t -> 0+), so the printed proof of (A.40) fails, but the corrected route gives |eta_+ log t|_oo <= 0.281515 < 0.497592 at H = 25 and the bound holds for all H >= 25.
check.note: The printed proof goes through the false l_oo form of (A.36), so it fails. The bound holds for H >= 25: |eta_+ log t|_oo <= 0.27949072 + |h - h_H|_oo * 0.34649 <= 0.281515 at H = 25 (book 0.497592).
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: |(h - h_H)/t|_oo is not bounded by (A.36) (it grows without bound as t -> 0+), so the printed proof of (A.40) fails, but the corrected route gives |eta_+ log t|_oo <= 0.281515 < 0.497592 at H = 25 and the bound holds for all H >= 25.

items.label: eq:gobmark
items.note: The book needs it only inside Prop 9.5.1, with H ≥ 25: for |η_{+,2}'|₂ in (9.76), for η_{+,2}'t^{σ−1} ∈ ℓ¹, and for the residue term c₀. Lean states |η₊(t)| ≤ 3.15te^{−t²/2} (abs_etaPlus_le_gauss, norm_fP_le), so |η₊/t|_∞ ≤ 3.15 at H = 200. Through etaPlus_sq_le this bound is the η₊/t input of Lean's different Prop 9.5.1 route (Mellin convergence, Plancherel decay, L² moments). The book's quantitative uses have no Lean counterpart.

lean.note: Lean's explicit formula for φ₂ = η₊²·log takes Mellin decay |M(s)| ≤ Ke^{−c|Im s|} (GoodSmoothing, via mellin_hHc_mul) instead of derivative norms. So the book's quantitative uses of |η₊/t|_∞ ((9.76) and the residue c₀) have no counterpart.
Same Mellin-decay admissibility for φ₁ = η₊². Its conv and diff fields need φ₁ = O(t²) at 0 (phi1_isBigO_bot, from etaPlus_sq_le).

η₊(t)² ≤ 9.9225·t²e^{−t²} for t ≥ 0 (the square of norm_fP_le), i.e. |η₊(t)/t| ≤ 3.15e^{−t²/2} at H = 200. This is how Lean's Prop 9.5.1 route controls η₊/t: phi1_isBigO_bot (Mellin convergence in prop_9_5_1 and GoodSmoothing), PhiG_phi1_le and PhiG_phi2_le (Plancherel decay 9.93e^{−|u|}), and norm_phi1_sq_le (the L² moments).

|η₊(t)| ≤ 3.15·|te^{−t²/2}| for all t (from abs_hH200_le: |h₂₀₀| ≤ 3.15), hence |η₊/t|_∞ ≤ 3.15. The book gives 1.153456 at H = 200. The same bound is Explicit.norm_fP_le (EtaPlusMellin.lean:66), from which etaPlus_sq_le is derived. This copy is used for the integrability of η₊, the non-coprime terms (ArcChars) and EtaPlusL2.

erratum.description: Proved through (A.39) and the ℓ∞ form of (A.36), which is false: |(h−h_H)/t|_∞ = ∞. The derivation of (A.36) bounds the w < 0 half using e^{−|w|/H} in place of e^{−w/H}, which reaches 2/t. The bound itself holds for H ≥ 25 (indeed for H ≥ 4.4), the range of its only use (Prop 9.5.1): |η₊/t|_∞ ≤ |η◦/t|_∞ + |h−h_H|_∞, with |h−h_H|_∞ ≤ 64e^{3/2}/(πH³) because |Mh(ir)| ≤ 192e^{3/2}/r⁴.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: |(h - h_H)/t|_oo is not bounded by (A.36) (it grows without bound as t -> 0+), so the printed proof of (A.41) fails, but the corrected route gives |eta_+/t|_oo <= 1.093387 < 1.434606 at H = 25 and the bound holds for all H >= 25.
check.note: The printed proof goes through the false l_oo form of (A.36), so it fails. The bound holds for H >= 25: |eta_+/t|_oo <= 1.08754395 + |h - h_H|_oo <= 1.093387 at H = 25 (book 1.434606).
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: |(h - h_H)/t|_oo is not bounded by (A.36) (it grows without bound as t -> 0+), so the printed proof of (A.41) fails, but the corrected route gives |eta_+/t|_oo <= 1.093387 < 1.434606 at H = 25 and the bound holds for all H >= 25.

items.label: lem:wollust
items.book_statement: For all real t, |g(t)| ≤ 7.87052, where g(t) = 4e(−t/4) − 4e(−t/2) + e(−t) is the Fourier transform of the Dirac part of η₂''/4. The proof is a rigorous grid search controlled by (B.4)–(B.5).
items.note: The book uses B.1.1 for |t| ≥ 655 in Lemma B.1.2 and in Lemma B.2.2. The Lean main line uses neither. (B.6) is proved with c₀ = 32 by kernel grids. (B.11) comes from 48 log 2 + c₀ log(ρ/4) (norm_eta2log4_le, eta2log_fourier_bound), which bypasses B.2.2. norm_trig_le is left over from the former axiom eta2DD_small route.

lean.note: ‖4z³−16z+16‖ ≤ 31.4821 for ‖z‖ = 1. With z = e(−t/4), 4z³−16z+16 = 4z̄·g(t), so this says |g(t)| ≤ 7.870525 (book 7.87052, true max 7.8705103). Proved exactly, with no grid: |·|² = 512c³−256c²−896c+656, c = Re z, by nlinarith. Off-cone.
Step `htrig` (lines 290–293): ‖16e(−t/2)−16e(−t/4)−4e(−t)‖ = 4|g(t)| ≤ 31.4821. This is B.1.1 in t, used for the |t| ≥ 655 half of (B.6). Off-cone.
The main line never uses B.1.1. For t ≥ 2, −4g(t) = 16z²−16z−4z⁴ is the w⁰ part of Fz. The kernel grids gridB_pos/gridB_neg bound it together with the w-terms, giving ≤ 32.

erratum.description: The proof says 'g(t) depends only on t mod 4π' and subdivides [0,4π]. With e(x) = e^{2πix}, g has period 4, and 4π is not a period. Harmless: [0,4π] ⊇ [0,4] still covers a full period, so the computation and the bound 7.87052 stand.

items.book_statement: The inequality of Lemma B.1.1: |4e(−t/4) − 4e(−t/2) + e(−t)| ≤ 7.87052 for every real t. The true maximum is 7.8705103.
items.note: The erratum in the proof (the period '4π') is recorded under Lemma B.1.1.

lean.note: Via z = e(−t/4), equivalent to |g(t)| ≤ 31.4821/4 = 7.870525, against the book's 7.87052. Off-cone. See Lemma B.1.1.
`htrig`: 4|g(t)| ≤ 31.4821, stated directly in t. Off-cone.

items.label: eq:ellib
items.book_statement: Defines g(t) = 4e(−t/4) − 4e(−t/2) + e(−t), the Fourier transform of 4δ_{1/4} − 4δ_{1/2} + δ₁. So 4g is the point-mass part of η̂₂''.
items.note: The companion's draft Companion/Book/Lemma_B_1_2.lean (not in the declaration index, so not linked) defines the printed g as lemma_B_1_2_g. Its docstring and module doc cite (B.2) correctly, and lemma_B_1_2_g_eq_dirac writes g as the Fourier transform of 4δ_{1/4} − 4δ_{1/2} + δ₁.

lean.note: TernaryGoldbach has no standalone g. The first three terms of eta2DD, 16e(−t/2) − 16e(−t/4) − 4e(−t), equal −4g(t), because Lean's eta2DD = −η̂₂''.
On the main line, the w⁰ part 16z² − 16z − 4z⁴ equals −4g(t) at z = e(−t/4). The grid treats z as a free point of the unit circle.
Polynomial form: 4z³ − 16z + 16 = 4z̄·g(t).

items.label: eq:maran
items.book_statement: Interpolation bound on [a,b]: g(t) is the chord value plus (b−a)²/8 · O*(max|g''|), for complex-valued C² g. A parenthetical derives it by reducing to real g and integrating twice.
items.note: The book cites no source ('in all likelihood well-known'). The reduction 'assume g has a local extremum at t' is loose but sound: apply the argument at the maximizer of Re(e^{−iθ}(g−L)).

lean.note: Lean's grids use first-order bounds. For t ≤ 2, each cell is checked at its centre, with the 24-Lipschitz bound norm_eta2DD_sub_le and Taylor error 120X⁵⁰/50!. The repo has no second-order interpolation lemma.
For t ≥ 2: the centre value of Fz plus the Lipschitz terms LzQ(w₁)(m₁−m₀) and LwQ(w₁)(w₁−w₀)/2 plus the remainder 6120w₁³, required ≤ 32 on each (m, w) cell.

erratum.description: The derivation has three misprints; (B.3) itself is true. (i) 'Dividing by g by g(t)' repeats 'by'. (ii) The chain 'g(t) = Re g(t) ≤ (1/8)max|(Re g)''| ≤ max|g''|' drops the 1/8 in its last term; as printed it gives only |g(t)| ≤ max|g''|. (iii) '∫₀ᵗ (v−t)M dv' has a nonpositive integrand; it should be (t−v).

items.label: eq:elek1
items.book_statement: From (B.3): on [a,b], max|g| ≤ max(|g(a)|,|g(b)|) + (b−a)²/8 · max|g''|. This is the book's tool for rigorous maximization on a grid, used in Lemmas B.1.1, B.1.2, B.2.2 and B.2.3.
items.note: In the proof of Lemma B.1.2, the book applies (B.4) with step ≤ √(2ε/M), i.e. error ½δ²M = 24π²δ₁². That is four times more cautious than the 6π²δ₁² that (B.4) allows, and valid. (B.4) holds for complex g because the chord value is a convex combination of g(a) and g(b).

lean.note: For t ≤ 2 (x = 2πt ∈ [0,12.6]), each cell must satisfy |P(centre)| + 12·(cell width) + 120X⁵⁰/50! ≤ 32. This is a first-order (Lipschitz) cell bound from norm_eta2DD_sub_le.
For t ≥ 2: a Lipschitz cell bound giving ‖Fz‖ + 6120w³ ≤ 32 on (m, w) rectangles.
Lean's B.1.1 needs no sampling: the cubic in Re z is maximized exactly.

items.label: eq:elek2
items.book_statement: The second-derivative bound |g''(v)| ≤ 4(π/2)² + 4π² + (2π)² = 9π² for all v. It feeds (B.4) in the proofs of Lemmas B.1.1 and B.1.2 (|(4g+f̂)''| ≤ 48π²).
items.note: Checked: 9π² = 88.826, and the sampled max|g''| is 81.747. Lean's t ≥ 2 grid likewise uses the z- and w-Lipschitz constants LzR and LwR (norm_Fz_sub_z, norm_Fz_sub_w) rather than any curvature bound.

lean.note: Lean never bounds g''. The t ≤ 2 grid uses a first-derivative bound instead: eta2DD(x/2π) is 24-Lipschitz in x. This replaces the book's |(4g+f̂)''| ≤ 4·9π² + 12π² = 48π².
B.1.1 is proved by exact algebra, so it needs no derivative bound.

items.label: lem:camelo
items.book_statement: For η₂(t) = 4max(log 2 − |log 2t|, 0), the Fourier transform of η₂'' satisfies |η̂₂''(t)| ≤ 31.521 for all real t. The range |t| ≥ 655 follows from Lemma B.1.1 and (B.8); the rest is a rigorous computation.
items.note: Book proof: |t| ≥ 655 from 4·7.87052 + 80/(π|t|); |t| < 655 by sampling at step 0.001 with error ½δ²·48π², evaluating f̂ by Simpson's rule in interval arithmetic. Lean history (NOTES): reaching 31.521 needed the axiom eta2DD_small for |t| ≤ 655. That axiom was removed by switching to c₀ = 32, as Helfgott suggested (README). The companion draft Companion/Book/Lemma_B_1_2.lean (not indexed) proves the printed lemma equivalent to its [0,655) range (lemma_B_1_2_iff_Ico). Its module doc (lines 86–89) already notes the 'f̂(t)' misprint. That file is companion work, not the formalization's own docs.

lean.note: (2πt)²‖𝓕η₂(t)‖ ≤ c₀ = 32 for all real t, i.e. |η̂₂''|_∞ ≤ 32 (book 31.521; true max 31.520652 at t ≈ 17.415). Negative t via norm_fourier_eta2_neg, the book's conjugation symmetry. In cone, no hypotheses.
c₀ := 32, used downstream in place of the book's c₀ = 31.521. For example, c₂ = 6π/(5√c₀) = 0.66643 (book 0.67148), and per the README Thm 3.1.1's 2.5x/√t becomes 2.511x/√t.

‖eta2DD t‖ ≤ 32 for t ≥ 0, where eta2DD = −η̂₂''. For t ≥ 2: three integrations by parts plus a kernel bisection over |z| = 1, w ≤ 2/25. For t ≤ 2: Taylor polynomials of degree < 50 plus a kernel bisection.

The book's constant 31.521, but only on the narrower range |t| ≥ 655. It uses the book's own argument: htrig (B.1.1 with 31.4821) + 80/(π|t|) ≤ 0.0389. Off-cone. The book's computation on [0,655) is not formalized.

erratum.description: The proof says 'The largest value of f̂(t) we find is 31.52065…'. That number is the maximum of |4g(t) + f̂(t)| = |η̂₂''(t)|; |f̂| itself never exceeds 12. Also, '(2π)²·O*(|x²f|₁) = 12π²' should read ≤ 12π² (or O*(12π²)). The conclusion survives.

items.changes_since_2013: Statement identical (Lemma A.2 of 1205.5252v4). The proof's footnote now points to §2.6 for interval arithmetic instead of citing Platt's implementation and Lambov.

items.label: eq:elundot
items.book_statement: |η̂₂''|_∞ ≤ 31.521 (Lemma B.1.2); this is c₀ in the Type I and minor-arc estimates.
items.note: Lean uses c₀ = 32 instead of 31.521. The citing declarations at P (lemma_4_2_2_caseA/B, lemma_4_2_3_caseB, lemma_4_2_4) only use eta2_fourier_bound'.
items.evidence: Lean: (2πt)²|η̂₂(t)| ≤ 32 for all t (31.521 only for |t| ≥ 655); book: ≤ 31.521.

lean.note: (2πt)²‖η̂₂(t)‖ ≤ c₀ = 32 for all t, in place of 31.521.
‖eta2DD t‖ ≤ 32 for t ≥ 0 (eta2DD = −η̂₂''); kernel-checked computation.
31.521 exactly, but only for |t| ≥ 655.
Wrapper in `fourier eta2` form, ≤ c₀ = 32; its docstring cites Lemma B.2.3 following the book's §6.1.

items.label: eq:petruchka
items.book_statement: Decomposes η₂'' as a distribution: 4(4δ_{1/4} − 4δ_{1/2} + δ₁) + f, where f is −4x⁻² on [1/4,1/2), 4x⁻² on [1/2,1) and 0 elsewhere. Hence η̂₂'' = 4g + f̂.
items.note: Checked: η₂' is 4/x on (1/4,1/2) and −4/x on (1/2,1), so it jumps by +16, −16, +4 at 1/4, 1/2, 1, and the smooth part is ∓4x⁻². Numerically, (2πt)²η̂₂(t) = eta2DD(t) = −(4g+f̂)(t) to 10⁻¹⁰ at t = 0.7, 3.1, 17.41. |η₂''|₁ = 36 + 12 = 48, as the book says.

lean.note: (2πt)²·𝓕η₂(t) = eta2DD t for t ≠ 0. This is the Fourier transform of (B.7) with the sign flipped (eta2DD = −4g − f̂). Two integrations by parts per piece (ibp2) produce the Dirac masses as boundary terms; η₂'' is never formed.
16e(−t/2) − 16e(−t/4) − 4e(−t) + 4Jq(1/4,1/2,t) − 4Jq(1/2,1,t). The Jq terms equal −f̂(t) for the book's f.
Two integrations by parts against e(−ut) for a C² piece.

items.label: eq:fedsan
items.book_statement: Decay of the absolutely continuous part: |f̂(t)| = |f̂'(t)/(2πit)| ≤ |f'|₁/(2π|t|) = 80/(π|t|), because the total variation of f is 2·16 + 2·64 = 160.
items.note: Checked: |f'|₁ = 64 + 32 + 4 (jumps) + 48 + 12 (smooth) = 160. At t = 654.9, |f̂| = 0.0192 ≤ 80/(654.9π) = 0.0389. The book reuses this bound as (B.13) in Lemma B.2.3.

lean.note: ‖∫_a^b e(−ut)u⁻² du‖ ≤ 1/(π|t|a²), by one integration by parts on each piece. The book instead uses one total-variation bound, |f'|₁ = 160 (jumps 100 plus smooth part 60). The totals agree. Off-cone.
Main line (t ≥ 2): three integrations by parts with remainder |w|³·6(a⁻⁴ − b⁻⁴), w = 1/(2πt), giving eta2DD = Fz + O*(6120w³).

items.book_statement: For y ≥ 4 and η_(y)(t) = log(yt)·η₂(t): |η_(y)'|₁ < (log y)·|η₂'|₁ = 8 log 2·log y. In fact |η_(y)'|₁ = 2η_(y)(1/2) = 8 log 2·log(y/2), since η_(y) increases on (1/4,1/2) and decreases on (1/2,1).
items.note: §6.2.1 checks (4.38) for η₂ with ρ₀ = 4 through (6.2), whose second line repeats this lemma. The strict inequality is never used, so Lean's ≤ is enough. Lean writes |η₂'|₁ as eta2'L1 = 8 log 2 (InnerSums.lean:64). The proof checks out (y = 4: 3.8436 < 7.6872).

lean.note: For ρ ≥ 4: eVariationOn (eta2log ρ) ≤ 8 log 2·log ρ. The inequality is non-strict, and total variation stands for |η_(ρ)'|₁ (equal for this absolutely continuous function). The proof finds the exact value 2η_(ρ)(1/2) = 8 log 2·log(ρ/2) (line 157).
η_(ρ) is monotone on [1/4,1/2], and antitoneOn_eta2log (line 77) gives the decrease on [1/2,1]. Together they replace the book's derivative-sign computations.
η_(ρ)(t) = log(ρt)·η₂(t), the book's η_(y). It is zero off (1/4,1) because eta2 is.
Passes the bound to Lemma 4.2.3 (TypeILogProof.lean) as the variation field V = |η₂'|₁·log ρ of SmoothData, i.e. the second condition of (4.38).

items.changes_since_2013: notation only: η_y became η_(y), and the remark 'sketched in [Helf, (2.4)]' is commented out (1205.5252v4 Lemma A.3).

items.book_statement: The inequality |η_(y)'|₁ < (log y)·|η₂'|₁ for y ≥ 4, the conclusion of Lemma B.2.1.
items.note: Same content as Lemma B.2.1.

lean.note: Lean form: eVariationOn (eta2log ρ) Set.univ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (eta2'L1 * log ρ) for ρ ≥ 4. Non-strict.

items.label: lem:lujur
items.book_statement: For y ≥ 4, with g(t) = 4e(−t/4) − 4e(−t/2) + e(−t) and k(t) = 2e(−t/4) − e(−t/2): |g(t)·log y − 4 log 2·k(t)| ≤ 7.87052·log y for every real t.
items.note: The proof of Lemma B.2.3 uses this lemma tacitly. Its 'as before' large-|t| step needs the transform of the point masses of η_(y)'', which is 4(g log y − 4 log 2·k), to be at most 4·7.87052·log y. Inputs: Lemma B.1.1 (|g| ≤ 7.87052) and |k| ≤ 3. The π/3 angle trick returns in (B.14). No Lean declaration mentions g·log y − 4 log 2·k.

lean.note: Lean's proof of (B.11) has no large-|t| case, so it never needs this bound on the point-mass part of η_(y)''. It splits η̂_(ρ) = η̂_(4) + (log ρ − log 4)η̂₂ and bounds the ρ = 4 part analytically (norm_eta2log4_le).

erratum.description: The proof asserts |arg(g(t)/k(t))| < 0.7 for t ∈ [−2,2], a full period of g and k. The true maximum is 0.854834, at t = ±0.49635. The conclusion survives: 0.8548 < π/3 ≈ 1.0472, which is all the π/3 argument needs, so (B.10) holds. Minor misprint in the same proof: 'k(t)·(4 log 2)/log y ≤ 6' should read |k(t)|.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: max |arg(g/k)| on [-2,2] is 0.854834 > 0.7 (at t = +-0.49635), but it is below pi/3 and max |g - s k| = 7.870238 <= 7.87052, so (B.10) still holds.
check.note: The proof asserts |arg(g/k)| < 0.7 on [-2,2]; the maximum is 0.8548337 at t = +-0.4963536 (already 0.85477 at t = 1/2). Since 0.8548 < pi/3 the argument still gives (B.10), and a direct scan gives max |g - s k| = 7.87024 <= 7.87052. The misprint 'k(t)' for |k(t)| was not checked numerically.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: max |arg(g/k)| on [-2,2] is 0.854834 > 0.7 (at t = +-0.49635), but it is below pi/3 and max |g - s k| = 7.870238 <= 7.87052, so (B.10) still holds.

items.label: eq:gotora
items.book_statement: The bound |g(t)·log y − k(t)·4 log 2| ≤ 7.87052·log y (Lemma B.2.2). Four times its left side is the transform of the point masses of η_(y)'' at 1/4, 1/2 and 1.
items.note: The inequality is true. For s = 4 log 2/log y ∈ (0,2], the max of |g − s·k| over t is 7.870510, attained as s → 0. The slip in its proof is recorded under Lemma B.2.2.

lean.note: Lean's analytic proof of (B.11) does not need it.

items.label: lem:octet
items.book_statement: For y ≥ 4 and η_(y)(t) = log(yt)η₂(t): |η̂_(y)''|_∞ < 31.521·log y.
items.note: Lean proves the bound with 32 in place of 31.521 by an analytic route (48 log 2 at ρ = 4 plus (B.6)); the book's numerics (B.12)–(B.16) are not formalized. The new citer eta2_fourier_bound is (B.6), not this lemma.
items.evidence: Lean: (2πt)²|η̂_(ρ)(t)| ≤ 32 log ρ for ρ ≥ 4; book: < 31.521 log y for y ≥ 4.

lean.note: For ρ ≥ 4, all t: (2πt)²‖η̂_(ρ)(t)‖ ≤ c₀ log ρ, c₀ = 32; non-strict. Docstring still says 31.521.
ρ = 4 case: ‖(2πt)²η̂_(4)(t)‖ ≤ 48 log 2, by integration by parts, no numerics.
(B.6) with 32, bounding the (log ρ − log 4)η̂₂ part.
Supplies K = c₀ log ρ, the (4.38) condition, to Lemma 4.2.3.

erratum.description: (i) After (B.14), |16 log 2·k − ĥ| is bounded by 48 log 2 + 25 ≈ 58.27, and max(31.521 log y, 58.27) = 31.521 log y is asserted; this fails for 4 ≤ y < 6.35. (ii) The decay bound covers |t| ≥ 2252.51, but the numerics only cover t ≤ 2252.21. The lemma is still true: |η_(4)''|₁ = 48 log 2 gives |η̂_(y)''| ≤ 48 log 2 + 31.521(log y − log 4) < 31.521 log y. Misprints: 'log k(t)' for k(t), and '[−1/4,1]' for [1/4,1].

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: 48 log 2 + 25 = 58.271 > 31.521 log 4 = 43.697 (the max step fails for 4 <= y < 6.351) and the decay range starts at 2252.505 > 2252.21, while |eta_(4)''|_1 = 48 log 2 < 31.521 log 4 repairs the lemma.
check.note: The step max(31.521 log y, 48 log 2 + 25) = 31.521 log y fails for 4 <= y < 6.3512, since 48 log 2 + 25 = 58.271 > 31.521 log 4 = 43.697, and the decay bound starts at t = 2252.505, beyond the checked range t <= 2252.21. The lemma holds anyway: |eta_(4)''|_1 = 48 log 2 = 33.271, so |hat(eta_(y)'')| <= 48 log 2 + 31.521 log(y/4) < 31.521 log y. The misprints 'log k(t)' and '[-1/4,1]' were not checked.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: 48 log 2 + 25 = 58.271 > 31.521 log 4 = 43.697 (the max step fails for 4 <= y < 6.351) and the decay range starts at 2252.505 > 2252.21, while |eta_(4)''|_1 = 48 log 2 < 31.521 log 4 repairs the lemma.

items.label: eq:yotoman
items.book_statement: |η̂_(y)''|_∞ < 31.521·log y for y ≥ 4, the conclusion of Lemma B.2.3. This is the condition |η̂_(ρ)''|_∞ ≤ c₀ log ρ of (4.38), with c₀ = 31.521.
items.note: The inequality is true; the gaps in its proof are recorded under Lemma B.2.3.

lean.note: (2πt)²‖𝓕(η_(ρ))(t)‖ ≤ c₀ log ρ with c₀ = 32: non-strict, and 32 in place of 31.521. (2πt)²|f̂(t)| stands for |(f'')^(t)|, so no distributional derivatives are needed.

items.label: eq:kokoso
items.book_statement: Write η_(y)'' = log y·η₂'' + (log·η₂)''. Its transform is (4g + f̂)·log y + (−16 log 2·k + ĥ). The g and k terms come from point masses at 1/4, 1/2 and 1; f and h are the remaining parts.
items.note: Checked numerically: 4g + f̂ = −(2πt)²η̂₂ and −16 log 2·k + ĥ = −(2πt)²(log·η₂)^ agree to about 10⁻¹² at t = 0.3, 1, 7.7, 17.4, 40. Lean's proof of (B.11) uses only the coarse split ghat_eta2log, regrouped as η̂_(4) + (log ρ − log 4)η̂₂.

lean.note: η̂_(ρ) = (log·η₂)^ + log ρ·η̂₂. This is the same split on the level of η̂, before the factor (2πit)², with neither piece evaluated.
(2πt)²η̂₂(t) = eta2DD t = −(4g(t) + f̂(t)): the first bracket.
The step hsum: c²(log·η₂)^(t) = 16 log 2·e(−t/2) − 32 log 2·e(−t/4) + ∫(log·η₂)''e(−ut), with c = −2πit. This is −16 log 2·k(t) + ĥ(t), the second bracket.

items.label: eq:pasaremos
items.book_statement: One integration by parts gives |f̂(t)| ≤ |f'|₁/(2π|t|) = 80/(π|t|) and |ĥ(t)| ≤ 160(1 + log 2)/(π|t|). The norms |f'|₁ and |h'|₁ count the jumps of f and h.
items.note: Checked, counting jumps: |f'|₁ = 2(16 − (−64)) = 160 and |h'|₁ = 2(128 + 32)(1 + log 2) = 320(1 + log 2) ≈ 541.81. Together with Lemma B.2.2 these give the decay range |t| ≥ 2252.505.

lean.note: Lean's (B.11) proof has no large-|t| case, so neither decay bound is used.
Off-cone. Lines 294–300 get the f̂ half, 4‖J(1/4,1/2)‖ + 4‖J(1/2,1)‖ ≤ 80/(π|t|), from norm_Jq_le; this is (B.8). Lean has no bound for ĥ.

items.label: eq:hotor
items.book_statement: The angle condition on I = [0.3, 2252.21] \ [3.25, 3.65]: the argument of (4g + f̂)/(−16 log 2·k + ĥ) lies in (−π/3, π/3). This is meant to bound |η̂_(y)''| by the larger of the two parts.
items.note: The display that follows, |η̂_(y)''| < max(|4g + f̂| log y, |16 log 2·k − ĥ|), applies the π/3 trick to z₁ log y and −z₂. That confirms the intended sign.

lean.note: Lean has no angle comparison: (B.11) follows from η̂_(ρ) = η̂_(4) + (log ρ − log 4)η̂₂ and two norm bounds.

erratum.description: The denominator has the wrong sign. The two parts point in nearly opposite directions, so as printed arg(z₁/z₂) is near ±π (|arg| ≥ 2.15 on I): (B.14) is false, and it would not yield |z₁ log y + z₂| ≤ max(|z₁| log y, |z₂|). The intended quantity is arg((4g + f̂)/(16 log 2·k − ĥ)) = arg(z₁/(−z₂)). Its maximum on I, 0.99134, is exactly the value the book reports.

check.output_line: CONFIRMED: as printed |arg(z1/z2)| >= 2.1503 > pi/3 at every sampled t in I, so (B.14) is false; with the denominator 16 log 2 k - hat h the maximum is 0.99134 at t = 7.500, the book's 0.99134.
check.note: As printed, |arg((4g + hat f)/(-16 log 2 k + hat h))| >= 2.1503 > pi/3 at every sampled t in I, so (B.14) is false as written. With the denominator 16 log 2 k - hat h the maximum on 0.005Z cap I, t <= 50, is 0.991339 at t = 7.5, which is the book's 0.99134. The sign is a misprint, and the intended statement supports the proof.
check.rerun: CONFIRMED: as printed |arg(z1/z2)| >= 2.1503 > pi/3 at every sampled t in I, so (B.14) is false; with the denominator 16 log 2 k - hat h the maximum is 0.99134 at t = 7.500, the book's 0.99134.

items.label: eq:aros
items.book_statement: Sampling error for 4g + f̂ on the grid 0.005ℤ: at most (1/2)·0.005²·max(4|g''| + |f̂''|) ≤ (0.0001/8)·48π² < 0.00593.
items.note: (1/2)δ²M is four times the interpolation error (1/8)δ²M of (B.4), so the bound is conservative.

lean.note: Lean does no sampling; the bound is analytic.

erratum.description: The maximum is over v ∈ I, but the f̂'' term is written at t, and a parenthesis is unbalanced. The bound itself is right.

items.label: eq:oros
items.book_statement: Sampling error for −16 log 2·k + ĥ on 0.005ℤ: at most (0.0001/8)(16 log 2·6π² + 24π²(2 − log 2)) < 0.0121, using |ĥ''| ≤ 4π²|x²h|₁ = 24π²(2 − log 2).
items.note: Feeds the arcsin margin 0.0121/2.1166 in the final angle estimate 1.0027062 < π/3.

lean.note: Lean does no sampling; the bound is analytic.

erratum.description: The phrase completing (B.16) calls this the error 'in the evaluation of 16 log 2·|k''(v)| + |(ĥ)''(t)|'; it should read −16 log 2·k(t) + ĥ(t). v and t are mixed as in (B.15). |k''| ≤ 6π² is valid but loose: 1.5π² suffices. The bound < 0.0121 holds.

items.label: eq:koasl
items.book_statement: |log·η₂|₁ = 2 − log 4.
items.note: Lean states the consequence |f̂|_∞ ≤ 2 − log 4 used in §6.2.1, not the L¹ identity; the identity is evaluated inside the proof.
items.evidence: Lean: ‖(log·η₂)^(t)‖ ≤ 2 − log 4; book: |log·η₂|₁ = 2 − log 4.

lean.note: ‖(log·η₂)^(t)‖ ≤ 2 − log 4 for all t; the L¹ norm is computed exactly inside the proof.
Combines (B.17), (B.18) into logFourierBound δ = min(2 − log 4, 96 log 2/(πδ)²) at −δ/2.

items.label: lem:marengo
items.book_statement: The second distributional derivative of log·η₂ has total mass 96 log 2. By (2.1) with k = 2, this gives |(log·η₂)^(t)| ≤ 96 log 2/(2πt)².
items.note: Only an ℓ¹-type bound is needed, since this term is lower order in the S_{I,1} bound (6.3) of §6.2.1, which applies (2.1) with k = 2 to it. Lean proves exactly the form that is used, with [H]'s constant.

lean.note: States the consequence via (2.1), not the L¹ identity: (2πt)²‖(log·η₂)^(t)‖ ≤ 96 log 2. The derivative jumps 32 log 2 (at 1/4) and 16 log 2 (at 1/2), plus ∫|lg1''| and ∫|lg2''|, are computed and summed (lines 250–283).
∫_{1/4}^{1/2}|(log·η₂)''| = 32 log 2, from the constant sign and the FTC. integral_abs_lg2'' (line 198) gives 16 log 2 on [1/2,1].
min(2 − log 4, 96 log 2/(πδ)²), the §6.2.1 input built from (B.17) and (B.18).

erratum.description: The proof has misprints. It writes |(log·η₂)''|_∞ for the L¹ norm. It also says 'log·η(t)' is increasing and negative on (1/4,1/2) and decreasing and positive on (1/2,1); that describes the derivative (log·η₂)'. log·η₂ itself is negative on (1/4,1), decreasing then increasing. The value 96 log 2 is correct.

items.label: eq:carengo
items.book_statement: |(log·η₂)''|₁ = 96 log 2, the conclusion of Lemma B.2.4.
items.note: The value is verified numerically (66.5421 = 96 log 2); the misprints in its proof are recorded under Lemma B.2.4.

lean.note: Fourier form (2πt)²‖(log·η₂)^(t)‖ ≤ 96 log 2. The 96 log 2 is assembled at lines 272–283 from the jump terms and integral_abs_lg1''/lg2''.

items.label: lem:expfor
items.book_statement: Explicit formula: for φ continuous, piecewise C¹, φ'' ∈ L¹, compactly supported in [1,∞): ΣΛ(n)φ(n) = ∫₁^∞(1 − 1/(x(x²−1)))φ − Σ_ρ Mφ(ρ).
items.note: Not needed: Lean replaces Cor C.1.3 by a trivial Chebyshev bound. The new Weil explicit formula at P (Explicit/WeilFormula.weil_formula) uses band-limited test functions with zero prime side and does not state this lemma.
items.evidence: Lean: no explicit formula for compactly supported φ; the sole use (C.1.2/C.1.3) is replaced by the unconditional 17z bound.

lean.note: Not this item's role: ζ explicit formula for GoodSmoothing φ (Mellin decay in a strip, excludes compact support); used for ψ bounds.
The only use (Lemma C.1.2 → Cor C.1.3) is bypassed by ‖S_{η₂}(α,z)‖ ≤ 17z from Chebyshev, no explicit formula.

erratum.description: Read literally, the hypotheses allow φ(1) ≠ 0, since φ is only required to be continuous on [1,∞). Then ∫₁ φ(x)/(x(x²−1)) dx diverges and Mφ(ρ) ~ −φ(1)/ρ is not absolutely summable, so (C.1) fails. A tacit φ(1) = 0 is needed: support in (1,∞), or φ continuous on (0,∞). items.label: prop:gosto
items.book_statement: Every odd n with 5 ≤ n ≤ n₀ is a sum of three primes; n₀ = 5.90698·10²⁹, 6.15697·10²⁸ or 1.23163·10²⁷ for RH verified to height 2.44·10¹², 2.419·10¹¹ or 3.061·10¹⁰.
items.note: Lean proves only the range 5 < n ≤ 10²⁷ (below the book's Platt case n₀ = 1.23163·10²⁷) and uses no RH verification or ψ/θ bounds: prime gaps come from a kernel-checked Proth-prime ladder. Lean's range starts above 5, which corrects the book's false case n = 5.
items.evidence: Lean: TernaryGoldbachUpTo (10^27) = ∀ odd n, 5 < n ≤ 10²⁷ → sum of three primes, from binary Goldbach and a kernel-checked prime ladder; book: 5 ≤ n ≤ 1.23163·10²⁷ via RH-based prime gaps.

lean.note: Odd n with 5 < n ≤ 10²⁷, from n = 3 + (n−3) or a ladder prime p ∈ [n−4·10¹⁸, n−4] plus binary Goldbach. Only [Fact BinaryGoldbachInput].
Kernel-checked Proth-prime ladder up to 10²⁷; replaces the book's prime-gap step ([RS03] Δ = 28314000, Ramaré's tables [Rpc], RH to 3.061·10¹⁰).
[OSHP]: every even m with 4 ≤ m ≤ 4·10¹⁸ is a sum of two primes (BinaryGoldbachInput).

erratum.description: The range should start at 7. n = 5 is odd and ≥ 5 but is not a sum of three primes, since any three primes sum to at least 6. The proof's first step, n = 3 + (n−3) with [OSHP], needs n − 3 ≥ 4. Theorem 1.1.1 correctly says 'greater than 5'. For 7 ≤ n ≤ n₀ the proposition holds.
